News.title: Kim Jong Un ramps up nuke programme after ignoring Trump’s offer to meet
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Kim Jong Un visited facilities producing nuclear materials and called for building more atomic weapons, days after ignoring US president Donald Trump’s offer to meet during his recent visit to Asia.

Mr Kim's statement signals again that he won't give up his evolving nuclear programme and is eager to bolster North Korea’s status as a nuclear power.

The KCNA news agency reported on Thursday that Mr Kim inspected two factories producing nuclear materials, one newly inaugurated and the other being expanded. Pictures showed Mr Kim and military officials walking between dense rows of what appeared to be centrifuges used to produce uranium and touring halls displaying what were believed to be warheads. Some of the images were blurred.

KCNA said Mr Kim visited a nuclear-powered equipment production base and a nuclear research institute as well on Wednesday.

North Korea has disclosed a uranium-enrichment site a few times since it showed one at its main Yongbyon nuclear complex to visiting American scholars in 2010.

North Korea didn't say where the nuclear materials production factories that Mr Kim visited this week were located. In June, when North Korea disclosed parts of a uranium-enrichment site while reporting on Mr Kim's visit there, outside experts assessed it was likely an additional facility at Yongbyon.

Mr Kim said that his latest inspection visit was part of efforts to strengthen the country’s defence capabilities in response to “variable nuclear threats approaching the Korean Peninsula moment by moment," KCNA said.

He accused the US of inciting its regional allies to possess nuclear-powered submarines and committing to sharing its nuclear weapons with them. “The validity and substantiality of our possession of nuclear weapons and the trend of bolstering up its nuclear capability in quality and quantity are an irreversible reality,” Mr Kim said, according to KCNA.

He also said the deployment of low-yield battlefield nuclear weapons was crucial given the country’s “inevitable reality facing the border with the most dangerous enemy state", a reference to rival South Korea.

North Korea has in recent years focused on developing and deploying such tactical nuclear weapons amid heightened tensions with its neighbour.

South Korea said it took Mr Kim's comments on battlefield nuclear weapons seriously and added that Seoul maintained a firm military readiness against Pyongyang's nuclear threats under an alliance with the US.

South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff declined to share an analysis of the North Korean nuclear facilities reported by KCNA, calling it confidential information for South Korea and the US.

Mr Kim has accelerated the expansion of his military nuclear programme since his earlier high-stakes diplomacy with Mr Trump collapsed in 2019.

He has also shifted his foreign policy focus towards strengthening ties with allies Russia and China, seeking to strengthen his regional footing while pushing to establish North Korea as a permanent nuclear power.

Trump still hopes to meet Kim

Mr Trump reiterated his eagerness to restore diplomacy with Mr Kim as he visited China last week for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.

But a Trump-Kim meeting didn't happen, with Pyongyang not publicly responding to the president’s overture. In an interview with the New York Post this week, Mr Trump dismissed the suggestion that Mr Kim had rebuffed his outreach. “No, he didn’t ignore it. You know, we had many leaders there,” he said. “There’ll be a time when we meet. It was just not really the right time. It was a very busy two-day period.”

Mr Trump also claimed he could revive diplomacy with Mr Kim at any time by restarting the exchange of letters they maintained during his first term, although he acknowledged that the two leaders had not corresponded “recently”.

Mr Kim has previously said he could return to talks if the US drops its “hostile policy” against his country and respects what he calls the North’s status as a nuclear state.

Experts say Mr Kim aims to win international recognition as a nuclear state so that he could demand the lifting of international sanctions.

Last week, International Atomic Energy Agency director general Rafael Grossi assessed North Korea had been expanding its original uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon, calling the move “a cause for serious concern”.

Nuclear weapons can be built using either highly enriched uranium or weapons-grade plutonium, and North Korea has facilities to produce both at Yongbyon. Last year, South Korea’s unification minister Chung Dong Young said North Korea was operating four uranium enrichment facilities and that they were running every day.

News.title: Tube strikes: What you need to know about today’s walkout and future dates
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Passengers are being warned of tube strikes affecting the whole network this Thursday, with more dates to follow in the lead-up to Christmas.

The Rail, Maritime and Transport union (RMT) announced eight sets of 24-hour strikes starting in November, ending in February 2027 over plans for a voluntary four-day week for drivers.

The first walkout will take place on Thursday, 26 November, and is expected to cause disruption across all Tube lines.

The RMT suspended planned strikes in March and May this year after progress in talks, but strike action is scheduled to go ahead after last-ditch negotiations failed this week between the union and Transport for London (TfL).

The Tube drivers’ strikes land on some of the busiest days of the year, including the last weekend before Christmas Day.

Here’s everything we know so far about the strike dates.

When are the tube strikes?

Some Tube drivers plan to strike on certain dates from November 2026 to February 2027, affecting the whole network.

The 24-hour strikes will run from midday on the first day to midday the following day.

November 2026

12pm Thursday 26 to 11.59am Friday 27 November 2026

December 2026

12pm Thursday 17 to 11.59am Friday 18 December 2026

12pm Saturday 19 to 11.59am Sunday 20 December 2026

January 2027

12pm Monday 4 to 11.59am Tuesday 5 January 2027

12pm Wednesday 6 to 11.59am Thursday 7 January 2027

February 2027

12pm Wednesday 17 to 11.59am Thursday 18 February 2027

12pm Tuesday 23 to 11.59am Wednesday 24 February 2027

12pm Thursday 25 to 11.59am Friday 26 February 2027

Will some trains still be running?

TfL says that during the strike, trains will run on most Tube lines, but disruption is expected across the network.

On the first strike day, services are likely to run as normal until 10am, but will then start to be reduced.

From 12pm, it is expected there will be disruption on all lines, with no service on the Waterloo & City line from midday.

No service is expected on the Circle and Piccadilly lines all day.

After 9pm, TfL says no Tube services are expected to run.

As the strike runs into its second day, services are expected to resume from around 7am, but there will still be disruption across all lines, as well as no service expected on the Circle, Piccadilly and Waterloo & City lines.

From midday, as the 24-hour strike comes to an end, disruption will continue across the Tube network as services recover.

TfL expects normal services to resume from 6pm on the second day.

Which lines are affected during the driver’s strike?

There will likely be some disruption across all Tube lines.

The Elizabeth line, DLR, London Overground, buses and trams will be running as normal during the strikes but will be busier than usual.

What advice is being given to travellers?

Passengers are being told to plan ahead and check the live train timetables during the strikes.

TfL added that passengers should allow more time than usual to complete their journey.

Why are strikes taking place?

RMT has announced strike dates in retaliation over plans to impose new working arrangements, including a voluntary four-day week, which the union says would mean drivers face spending more time driving trains, longer duties, earlier starts and later finishes.

The union has also raised concerns that the proposals would pave the way for hundreds of job cuts, with initial rosters published for the Bakerloo line indicating significant reductions in staffing.

“London Underground is attempting to dress up a wholesale attack on drivers’ working conditions as a voluntary four-day week,” RMT general secretary Eddie Dempsey said.

“But there is nothing voluntary about a scheme that forces drivers to give up existing protections whether they work four days or five, and threatens those who refuse with displacement from their depots.

He added: “RMT is not opposed to a genuine four-day working week that benefits our members, but we will not accept it being used as a vehicle for job cuts, intensified working and the erosion of terms and conditions.”

Aslef, Britain's trade union for train drivers, said the switch to a four-day week would give train drivers an extra 35 days off a year.

“We are surprised that the RMT has, once again, decided to take strike action to try to prevent Underground drivers moving to a four-day week on a voluntary basis,” Finn Brennan, Aslef’s full-time organiser on London Underground, said.

He added: “The voluntary four-day week gives Tube train drivers an extra 35 days off every year with rosters based on a 34-hour week in return for some changes to working conditions and moving to electronic, rather than paper-based, systems for booking on for duty.

“We are in discussions with Transport for London about how the final details of this will work in practice.

“Management have agreed that anyone who wants to keep working a five-day week will be able to do so without suffering any detriment, and we will be holding them to that.

“A strike designed to stop people having the choice of a shorter working week and more time off is a strange choice to make.”

Nick Dent, director of customer operations for London Underground, managed by TfL, said: “We have engaged with our trade unions for months about our proposal for a new four-day working week.

“As a result of that engagement, drivers can now choose to remain on a five-day week with a guarantee of remaining at the same depot.

“This will give our colleagues a real, meaningful choice on their working pattern without having to change where they work.

“This will also mean less time at work for Tube drivers, while delivering a more efficient, reliable Tube service for our customers.

“Given that we have provided this new option after their feedback, we urge the RMT to put this proposal to their members.”

News.title: Search for trapped miners increases after flooding kills 13 at Indonesia illegal gold mine
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Rescuers battled high water, darkness and slippery, narrow terrain Thursday searching for 13 more miners believed trapped by flooding in an illegal gold mine where 13 bodies were recovered earlier.

The miners were digging for grains of gold late Monday when heavy rain caused the Ciseureuh River to overflow into a mine shaft in the Bogor regency of West Java province. Several people managed to escape from one section of the excavation before floodwaters filled the shaft, estimated to be about 100 meters (330 feet) deep, in a mountainous area south of the capital, Jakarta.

Authorities said they were not immediately notified because the miners were operating illegally, and local miners and residents initially tried to pump water from the site themselves before the situation became unmanageable.

Police first received reports of trapped miners about 16 hours after the flooding occurred, and nearby state-owned mining company PT Antam forwarded a formal report to the Jakarta Search and Rescue Agency shortly after midnight Wednesday, triggering a full-scale rescue operation.

The search and rescue team used submersible water pumps to suck water from the hole and tried to close off openings where groundwater seeped in.

Thursday’s search operation involving 325 personnel focused on two adjacent mine shafts, using rope-access techniques to reach victims, said Jakarta Search and Rescue Agency chief Desiana Kartika Bahari.

The flooded shaft was near facilities operated by PT Antam’s Pongkor gold mining unit, but the company said the incident was unrelated to its operations.

Informal mining is common in Indonesia, where thousands work in dangerous conditions. Miners face risks including landslides, flooding and tunnel collapses, while gold processing often involves toxic mercury and cyanide with little protective equipment.

News.title: South Korea's central bank raises key interest rate to fight inflation
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

South Korea’s central bank on Thursday raised its benchmark interest rate for the third time since July, aiming to tighten money supply in the face of inflationary pressure driven by the war in the Middle East and the country’s booming semiconductor exports fueled by global demand related to artificial intelligence.

In raising its policy rate by a quarter-percentage point to 3.25%, the Bank of Korea also lifted its growth forecast for South Korea’s economy to 3.9% from 3.3% for 2026, and to 4.1% from 2.9% for 2027, following months of strong exports.

Despite the robust performance in trade, analysts have noted that consumer spending has remained subdued due to rising prices, stagnant wages and the burden of servicing South Korea’s notoriously high household debt.

Consumer prices rose 2.8% in October from a year earlier, above the bank’s 2% target. Core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices to better gauge underlying price pressures, rose 2.7% over the same period.

The bank said in a statement that raising borrowing costs was necessary as inflation was expected to remain above target for a “considerable period” and also cited “persistent risks on the side of financial stability.”

The bank said the global economy was maintaining modest growth despite the conflict in the Middle East, mainly driven by AI-related investments, but price pressures would continue to grow, driven by increasing energy costs.

It warned that the rising house prices in the capital Seoul and the metropolitan area could further aggravate the country’s household debt, which stood at an all-time high of 2,030 trillion won ($1.51 trillion) as of the third quarter, nearly the size of the country's annual gross domestic product, according to the bank’s data. Shin Hyun Song, the bank’s governor, said household borrowing is continuing to rise amid expectations of further home price increases in the greater capital area, making it necessary for policymakers to “remain vigilant regarding the risks of financial imbalances.” He said the rate hike was also a preemptive move to curb inflationary pressures and that consumer prices are expected to remain above the bank’s target until sometime in 2028. Shin said it would take time for the country’s export gains to translate into meaningful increases in consumers’ spending capacities and that the bank’s tight monetary policy should be complemented by fiscal measures to ease the burden on households.

The bank’s decision to raise the policy rate was not a unanimous decision, with two of the seven members of its monetary policy committee arguing to keep the rate at 3%.

News.title: Jannik Sinner ruled out of Australian Open as injury lay-off continues
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Jannik Sinner will miss the Australian Open after undergoing knee surgery.

The world number two has not played since defending his Wimbledon title in July and will now miss the first Grand Slam tournament of 2027.

Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo said in a statement: “We’ve been in regular touch with Jannik’s team and they’ve confirmed he won’t be joining us for the Australian Open in January following his recent surgery.

“Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for the Australian Open in 2028.”

The Italian confirmed on Tuesday he had undergone minor surgery after experiencing ongoing pain in his right knee.

Sinner said in a statement earlier this week: “Over the past few months, together with my team, we’ve tried everything to treat my injury without surgery.

“After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn’t respond as we had all hoped, that’s why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band.

“I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team.”

The iliotibial band is a thick band of fibrous connective tissue running down the outside of the thigh, and injuries associated with it are typically caused by overuse.

Prior to his injury, the 25-year-old had a stellar start to 2026 which saw him win the first five Masters 1000 tournaments of the year, becoming the second man after Novak Djokovic to achieve the Golden Masters.

His absence has allowed Alexander Zverev to overtake him in the world rankings, with Carlos Alcaraz in third place.

Both men shared their well-wishes after Sinner’s surgery.

“The decision of making the surgery, I think his team made a good decision. He’s young, has a lot of years ahead of him. I’m sure he’s going to come back even stronger, even better,” Alcaraz said on Wednesday.

Zverev added: “”We know that he’s mentally strong. I hope that he takes every step serious and that, in three, four months’ time, he can be back to 100 per cent and be back playing.”

News.title: FedEx aircraft overruns runway at Miami airport, closing all but 1 runway
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A FedEx aircraft overran a runway at the Miami International Airport on Wednesday night, forcing all but one runway to temporarily close the day before Thanksgiving, according to the airport.

There were no reports of injuries after the aircraft ran off the runway at about 8:40 p.m., the airport reported. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units have responded. The incident happened almost three months after an Amazon cargo jet overshot another runway in Miami, killing five people on the ground.

The McDonnell Douglas MD-11 was coming from Memphis, and flights will be resuming shortly, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. The administration will investigate.

The airport recommended that passengers scheduled to fly Wednesday night should check with their airlines for the latest flight updates before traveling to the airport.

“We appreciate our passengers’ patience as we work to safely resume normal operations,” the airport said in a statement.

The runway this FedEx plane landed on Wednesday is different than the one the Amazon cargo plane overran in September. But three of Miami’s runways converge at the west end, so the FedEx plane ended up close to where the Amazon plane careened across a road and struck a van filled with a plane cleaning crew.

The MD-11 is the same type of cargo plane that crashed in Kentucky last year after an engine fell off a UPS jet as it was taking off, killing three pilots and 12 more people on the ground. The FAA said it approved Boeing’s proposed fix, and FedEx started flying them again in May.

The National Transportation Safety Board said it had no information about Wednesday's incident.

News.title: US-led consortium agrees to acquire assets from Russian oil company Lukoil
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A consortium of investors that includes a U.S. government lender said Friday that it has agreed to acquire the international energy assets of Russian oil company Lukoil.

The consortium, led by U.S.-based asset management company Eldridge, includes the U.S. International Development Finance Corp., a government lender, as well as Catena Investment Holding, a company based in the United Arab Emirates, and New York-based investment bank Xtellus Capital Partners.

The Russian company said at the beginning of the year that it planned to sell its international assets to an American private equity firm. At the time, Lukoil was looking to divest from its global portfolio in the face of looming U.S. sanctions.

Under the terms of the agreement, the consortium would acquire Lukoil International, which owns non-Russian energy assets, including oil and gas fields, refineries, pipelines and other infrastructure, across 11 countries. Its operations currently produce about 350,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, the consortium said in a release.

The consortium would exchange restricted Russian shares of Lukoil and other Russian companies for all of Lukoil International's liquidity, according to the terms of the proposed deal. This would avoid having the U.S.-led consortium make direct cash payments to Russia in exchange for the assets.

The International Development Finance Corp. would receive an ownership interest on behalf of the U.S. A DFC official positioned the agency's involvement in the deal as a way to protect U.S. interests and reduce the risk of rivals getting involved. The official, who was not authorized to comment publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity, called Lukoil’s assets important to U.S. and allies’ energy security.

U.S. Rep. Gregory Meeks, a Democrat and ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, criticized the proposed deal, saying the Trump administration was circumventing a congressional ban on the DFC investing in Russia, which was aimed at pressuring Moscow to end its war in Ukraine.

The “DFC exists to advance development in emerging markets, not serve as a finance vehicle for President Trump’s wealthy and well-connected friends,” he said.

President Donald Trump has taken a series of steps in recent months to ease up on Moscow, including agreeing to purchase Russian diesel to try to bring down global energy prices, meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin and calling him a friend, and abruptly waiving new sanctions on Russia days before they were to take effect.

The diesel deal met with bipartisan opposition in Congress, where lawmakers argued that any Russian shipments would volate a 2022 ban on energy imports from Russia.

Although the Treasury Department temporarily authorized Russian diesel transactions that would ordinarily be subject to U.S. sanctions, two tankers originally bound for the U.S. changed course after state and federal officials warned port authorities, fuel distributors and banks that facilitating any shipments could bring legal consequences.

Early this year, Lukoil was pursuing the sale of its international assets to the U.S. Carlyle Group. The Treasury Department had given the company until Feb. 28 to sell its foreign assets. Trump announced sanctions on Lukoil and Rosneft, Russia's two biggest oil companies, in October 2025 to push for a ceasefire in Russia’s war on Ukraine.

In September, Trump personally signed legislation aimed at renewing pressure on the Russian economy and disrupting the financial resources fueling the war against Ukraine. But he then signed an executive order last month pausing the sweeping new sanctions package two days before an implementation deadline.

___

Didi Tang in Washington contributed reporting.

News.title: One person had a worse night than United keeper – the wretched referee
News.content:
Few Manchester United fans expected a positive result from Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge at Anfield, but the bar will not be set so low for Sporting in the Champions League this evening.

The manner of the 4-0 defeat against Liverpool, even accounting for Leny Yoro’s early red card, was dispiriting but not unexpected. The next few weeks will reveal how Pochettino intends to get a grip on the job.

When it comes to United’s Champions League prospects, the comeback win over Roma at the tail-end of Michael Carrick’s tenure made their position less perilous, but avoiding outright elimination is the first target.

United are 19th in the table, with the top 24 teams going through. Those between ninth and 24th go into a play-off round before the last 16. After Sporting away, United host RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich before a trip to Villarreal so there are stiff tests to come.

Sporting are well-placed after three wins from four, but their Champions League schedule is rather one-sided: in their final three matches they travel to Roma, before playing Barcelona and Manchester City. They reached the quarter-finals of the competition last season, losing narrowly to Arsenal over two legs.

They are third in their league, having been weakened by the summer sales of Geovany Quenda (to Chelsea), Morten Hjulmand (to Atletico Madrid) and Ousmane Diomande (to Nottingham Forest). The vast majority of goals are scored by Colombian striker Luis Suárez.

Bruno Fernandes, United’s captain, returns to his former club tonight and there is hope Luke Shaw could be back at left-back. Pochettino must decide whether or not to stick with Matthijs de Ligt, who was extremely rusty at Anfield but may need the minutes.

Yoro’s one-game suspension was overturned by the FA, and he would have been available for this one in any case.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Wirtz follows Keegan and Dalglish with defining performance as Liverpool No 7
News.content:
“A knock on the knee and we have to test it,” Iraola said. “That was the worst part of the night. It is very early to tell but it was very painful at that moment. He was better after the game.”

So, too, was Iraola, who was especially pleased that Liverpool recorded their first Champions League clean sheet of the season and, in the process, stopped Brugge – who had scored in 19 consecutive games – from finding a way through.

There were several reasons this was the case: Jérémy Jacquet, for instance, never put a foot wrong – what a smart signing he has proved to be. He more than did his bit to retain order with Virgil van Dijk, who was given the chance to catch his breath before the Merseyside derby.

It was tough for Liverpool in the second period, as Brugge attacked the end of the stadium where their noisy ultras created a cacophony. Yet they handled the situation well, even if Iraola looked ready to combust at one stage, being given a yellow card for protesting too much to the officials.

“I saw the referee beforehand, I know him from Spain and I knew this was coming,” Iraola said.

Perhaps his ire was fuelled by Liverpool squandering a fabulous chance on the hour to kill things off. A move that featured Wirtz and Isak exchanging passes with pinball precision ended with Szoboszlai bearing down on Sommer, but his shot was too close to the veteran.

He had to score and the grimace that followed had nothing to do with heavy strapping the Hungarian had on supporting his right knee. That miss would have been exacerbated in the 69th minute had Alisson Becker not made a superb save to deny Félix Lemaréchal, plunging to avert the danger.

News.title: Mick Harford: ‘My prostate cancer diagnosis was a shock. As a footballer, I’d felt bulletproof’
News.content:
However, an MRI scan and a PSMA PET scan at UCLH, where I had been referred, showed only a little bit of growth on my prostate, and I was told I would be fine. But, while I was symptomless at the time, within around eight months I was getting up three or four times in the night to go to the toilet, and then feeling the urge to go back again only two minutes later. I instinctively knew something was wrong.

Upon my return to UCLH in December, I was told my PSA was now “very high”, at around 48 ng/mL – far more elevated than the 4.5 ng/mL considered healthy for my age group. Advanced prostate cancer was then confirmed with a biopsy. The first person I told was my son, William, in a phone call from the car at the hospital. It was horrible – it was not just me who would suffer, but my family too. I also needed to tell Luton Town, who were amazing and gave me as much time off work as I needed from my role as assistant manager.

Facing the opponent

My brilliant oncology team immediately had a plan for me. They got me on a course of hormone therapy medications called Enzalutamide and Zoladex, in preparation for me to begin radiation treatment from mid-August. I had 49 sessions over the space of about eight weeks, and it was daunting each time I travelled into London on the train from my home in Harpenden to go underground to the hospital’s Radiotherapy Department.

But I got through it, even with a bit of collateral damage. While my ongoing symptoms are not a pleasant conversation, it’s an important one, because it has affected my life in so many ways. My sleep is disrupted because I still need to get up multiple times during the night to go to the toilet so I can avoid an accident in bed. I also have to wear a nappy every day in case of leakage, and need to be careful when I’m out to ensure I’m close to a toilet.

I’m still on a hormone therapy called Triptorelin to block my testosterone, which feeds the cancer, and takes the form of an injection every six months. As a result, I’m going through the “male menopause”, which is not very nice and can cause tiredness, sleep issues and brain fog. It has given me lots of sympathy for women of my generation.

However, as I approach six years since my diagnosis, I’ve tried to stay proactive as much as possible. The discipline and drive instilled in me as a footballer have come in handy. To be a successful player, you need to stick to a routine. In the same way that I worked hard to ensure my teammates and coaches respected me on the pitch, so I’ve adhered to what all the doctors have advised – including trying to be diligent in terms of lifestyle.

News.title: Underperforming Manchester City are an accident waiting to happen
News.content:
Enzo Maresca had two home games in four days to get Manchester City into decent shape for Sunday’s clash against Arsenal, which now feels like a must-win. On Tuesday, however, they ended up being taunted by Rasmus Hojlund on another evening that raised more questions than answers.

It is now one win in seven for Maresca, who cannot keep a clean sheet and has a £327m midfield that have played well individually, but is yet to form a unit. Worryingly, their reliable source of goals, Erling Haaland, had his quietest game of the season. It required Rayan Cherki to rescue a point against Napoli.

Maresca needs to find a solution in the next five days before heading to the Emirates to face the champions in what could be a defining weekend for the season. Defeat would put them nine points off the pace, with Maresca still trying to find his best combination of players to pick.

Club captain Rúben Dias was on the bench here and Josko Gvardiol was left out of the draw against Fulham at the weekend, which also ended as a draw rather than a morale-boosting win to get City out of their slump.

News.title: Arsenal get the best and worst of Gyokeres on frustrating night for Arteta
News.content:
Mikel Arteta may prefer to imagine his Arsenal team as a remorseless winning machine, although on nights such as these they can still demonstrate a familiar unreliability when it comes to the main purpose of it all.

There were 30 shots over the night from the English champions, only four of which were on target, and in the end their winner never came. Even in the 95th minute, Arteta’s players were still conspiring to foul it up. This Champions League game might have been decided in Arsenal’s favour within 20 minutes. By half-time it should have been a formality. Yet, as chance after chance slipped away, there was always a possibility this would end differently.

The leaders of the Bundesliga were traumatised at times by the ferocity of the Arsenal press, and there were times when Borussia Dortmund will likely have no idea how they survived. Even so, they did just that and, liberated in the second half, Maximilian Beier scored an improbable equaliser in his team’s best period. There were still 40 minutes for Arsenal to put this one to bed and they found many ways not to do so.

It was notable that the man who put Arsenal ahead in the ninth minute with a right-footed thump from space on the edge of the Dortmund box was the same striker who would miss the best chance to win it. That is the Viktor Gyökeres dilemma. In the space of a single game he can look like a potential match-winner and also the last man his manager would wish to see arriving on the end of a perfect Martin Odegaard cross.

So it proved after 75 minutes when Gyökeres thrust himself at an Odegaard ball into the box that just needed guiding inside a post, yet planted it decisively wide of the mark. On the touchline Arteta tried very hard to hide his despair and failed to do so.

News.title: Emery unhappy with ‘unfair’ referee but Aston Villa are toothless
News.content:
Aston Villa supporters have happy memories of Istanbul after May’s Europa League final, and they return to face Galatasaray this evening in a fixture which could forecast their Champions League prospects.

It has been par for the course for Unai Emery’s team in Europe so far, with victories over Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking and a defeat at Barcelona aligning with the form book.

Nine points from 12 leaves them inside the top eight at the halfway stage of the league phase, but tougher challenges are ahead with PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come after tonight’s game.

Since a statement victory over Manchester City, it has been a frustrating time for Villa either side of the international break. They were dumped out of the League Cup by Bournemouth, were second-best in a home draw with Fulham, threw away a pair of two-goal leads at Old Trafford, and were held by Sunderland at the weekend.

Though Villa put six past Galatasaray’s city rivals Fenerbahce at Villa Park, away games against Turkish opposition can be different beasts, as Liverpool discovered in the last round of Champions League matches.

Galatasaray’s two major attacking threats, Victor Osimhen and Rafael Leão, are both absent with injuries. Davinson Sanchez and Lucas Torreira are former Premier League players in their squad. Galatasaray have won two of four Champions League games, losing to Barcelona and Sporting Lisbon, but they are top of the Turkish Super Lig.

Villa will be without right-back Matty Cash owing to a concussion sustained during the international break with Poland, but will hope to have Victor Lindelof available again after he missed the Sunderland draw with illness.

Emery’s team were unable to train at Rams Park yesterday in order to give a troublesome pitch maximum recovery time after emergency renovation work.

“If we could have trained in the stadium of Galatasaray, maybe we would have decided for the same situation, but it’s not changing our routine,” Emery said. “How the pitch is going to be tomorrow is important, but it’s not an excuse because it’s [the same] for both teams. Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible.”

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Anthropic falls below stock market listing price
News.content:
Anthropic’s shares dropped below their initial public offering price for the first time, sealing a dramatic reversal of fortunes for the AI giant following its blockbuster stock market debut last week.

The Claude chatbot maker saw its shares fall more than 8pc from their $83 offer price to stand at around $76 as investors appeared to grow sceptical of its valuation.

The slide on the Nasdaq exchange was set to wipe over $200bn from the company’s market value.

Anthropic raised more than $81bn in the biggest IPO on record, with its valuation surging to $2tn as the shares peaked at around $115.

But the company bucked Monday’s huge rally following Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia with the shares slipping from Friday’s close.

Wall Street resumed its slide on Tuesday as underlying fears over the AI trade appear to have outweighed the impact of Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as chief executive.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 was down as much as 3pc, with the benchmark S&P 500 around 1.2 pc lower.

In London, the FTSE 100 closed slightly lower, down 0.1pc, unable to sustain gains made in global markets on Monday.

The ability of AI companies to generate sufficient returns on their massive investment has proved more important than Nvidia’s boardroom drama, according to Goldman Sachs analysts.

Sharon Bell told Bloomberg: “The AI trade really depends on whether companies can make a return on the capex they spend.

“If the answer is yes, then the tech sector should do well over time and if the answer is no, it won’t do so well.”

Ms Bell argued that the management changes at Nvidia would not “make a huge difference either way”.

Glenn Yin at online trading platform ACCM told the Reuters Global Markets Forum: “By the end of ​the day, these businesses need to make enough money to justify investors’ expectations.

“‌My point is: Jensen’s return does not solve this. So, the sentiment is more emotional than sensible, in my opinion.”

Major chipmakers saw their stocks sink on Tuesday as general AI-related optimism faded.

Nvidia, the world’s largest chipmaker, saw its stock fall more than 7pc, while the Philadelphia semiconductor index, which tracks the major US manufacturers of chips, fell 8pc.

Microchip maker AMD’s share price was down as much as 10pc, while shares in Broadcom were down around 3pc.

The dollar eased back from its highest level in almost two years after Jensen ​Huang’s return to Nvidia revived the AI rally and fuelled expectations of more interest rate rises.

The President’s intervention, however, is a “slippery slope”, according to a top Republican senator.

Dave McCormick, the former boss of hedge fund Bridgewater, told Bloomberg: “I am worried about the precedent of the executive branch getting involved in real ownership deals with companies but also in board governance and making these decisions.

“This is a precedent that I don’t think we want to replicate or reinforce.”

Mr McCormick will be one of the politicians grilling the Nvidia boss next week when he testifies before the Senate Banking Committee.

Todd Blanche, the US Attorney General, has labelled Nvidia “a good corporate citizen” despite questions over whether Jensen Huang’s alleged affair could have threatened national security.

Mr Blanche added that if Nvidia was the target of a criminal investigation, “that wouldn’t be the message”.

News.title: Meningitis outbreak triggers epidemic alert in Gaza
News.content:
Cases of meningitis have risen dramatically in Gaza and have triggered an epidemic alert, the territory’s health ministry has said.

At least 272 cases were recorded across the enclave in October, more than eight times the usual monthly rate of 30 to 50 cases, Dr Nidal Ghoneim, a senior health ministry official, told a press conference on Tuesday.

Children under one year old account for 71 per cent of cases, with newborns alone accounting for 13 per cent, World Health Organization (WHO) spokesperson Christian Lindmeier said in a separate briefing.

Dr Ghoneim added that 15 Palestinians had died of meningitis since the start of the year, and that the spread of the disease through the strip threatened the lives of thousands of people, mostly children.

It is thought that most cases are being driven by enterovirus – the leading cause of viral meningitis – which is shed through faeces and can spread rapidly between people in unsanitary environments.

All six wastewater treatment plants in Gaza are currently out of operation, meaning an estimated 150,000 cubic metres of untreated sewage flows into the environment every day, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).

Sports.title: Liverpool cruise to Club Brugge win as Alexander Isak continues to prove his worth
Sports.content:
Liverpool cruise to Club Brugge win as Alexander Isak continues to prove his worth

CLUB BRUGGE 0-3 LIVERPOOL: Reds striker Alexander Isak struck twice either side of a Florian Wirtz effort to seal a comfortable win for Andoni Iraola's side

View 2 Images Isak scored twice as Liverpool breezed past Club Brugge (Image: Getty Images)

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz continued their revivals as Liverpool maintained their growing momentum under Andoni Iraola with an impressive Champions League triumph in Belgium.

‌



‌



Isak scored twice and Wirtz notched an impressive strike as Iraola’s side secured a hard-earned victory at free-scoring Club Brugge to strengthen their claims of direct qualification to the knockout stages.

‌



It was the sixth successive away game in which Isak has netted while Wirtz has six goals in five for club and country, with the duo now consistently delivering on their £100million-plus price tags.

‌



And Liverpool were able to build on their weekend hammering of Manchester United to take further confidence into Sunday’s Merseyside derby at Everton.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Liverpool’s second of nine games in 28 days saw Iraola again rotate his resources with three changes to the side that thumped Manchester United 4-0 on Sunday.

The most glaring omission was skipper Virgil van Dijk, a substitute for the second time in five Champions League games this season having been managing a calf problem that forced him out of international duty with the Netherlands last week.

‌



By contrast, Isak was making his first start in the competition since early September as Rio Ngumoha, star performer in the United rout, made way for Victor Munoz.

Liverpool had won their first European trophy by beating Brugge to the UEFA Cup in 1973 and this was the first meeting between the sides since the Reds beat the Belgian side in the European Cup final five years later.

‌



Brugge have been in good form having gone into the game with 10 wins in their last 11 games and had proven their potency on their own patch by scoring three or more goals in seven of their previous nine home Champions League matches.

View 2 Images Florian Wirtz scored a great goal for Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Van Dijk’s bench duty meant Dominik Szoboszlai wore the captain’s armband for the first time for Liverpool in a midfield where he was joined by promising teenager Trey Nyoni, goalscorer in the Reds’ last Champions League game, the 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahce.

And Szoboszlai played an integral role as the Liverpool went ahead after only 13 minutes. With Brugge attempting to play out from the back, goalkeeper Yann Sommer was pressured by Isak into undercooking a pass out wide. Bradley Barcola intercepted and instantly fed Szoboszlai inside the area for a low cross clinically converted by Isak for his ninth goal of the campaign.

‌



Felix Lemarechal sent a weak header at Alisson Becker as Brugge sought a response but Liverpool’s high-pressing game put the home side under the cosh, Isak later hitting a snap volley wide after good work by Barcola and the busy Florian Wirtz.

A sliding Szoboszlai produced an excellent block to deny Joaquin Seys, and from the counter-attack Munoz ran half the length of the field before a nasty collision with Brugge centre-back Jorne Spileers ended with the Liverpool winger receiving lengthy treatment before being replaced by Ngumoha shortly before the interval.

‌



Brandon Mechele’s poor touch at the near post ended one dangerous Brugge attack but Liverpool were close after the restart with Ngumoha firing wide after superb footwork inside the area fashioned an opening.

‌



Only a superb save by Sommer prevented Szoboszlai doubling the visitors’ lead shortly before the hour after an incisive move between Wirtz and Isak.

Brugge finally began to show in the final quarter and Alisson needed to make a smart stop at his near post to keep out a Lemarechal drive.

Article continues below

And Liverpool’s win was confirmed 11 minutes from time when Ngumoha embarked on a fine run and found Wirtz for a superb finish off the far post before Isak capitalised on Mechele’s failure to deal with Alisson’s long punt and raced on to clip a fine goal over Sommer.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes talks up Sporting return as Man Utd prepare to face his former team
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes talks up Sporting return as Man Utd prepare to face his former team

Bruno Fernandes left Sporting Lisbon to join Manchester United but has talked up a return to the Portuguese capital, underlining how happy he was

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes has spoken candidly about a move back to Portugal

Bruno Fernandes has opened the door to a Sporting Lisbon return as the Manchester United talisman admitted: "I was happy here and I’d like to be again."

The Portguese star spent two and a half years playing for Sporting before his performances prompted the Red Devils to spend £67million to sign him in January 2020. He's gone on to become the most successful signing of the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era.

He recently shelved contract talks and has been heavily linked with a move away in the past. A return to his homeland and the city where he once played is clearly something that appeals.

Whilst on Sporting's books Fernandes scored 64 times in 137 appearances and was named the best player in Portugal in back-to-back seasons. The 32-year-old also insists there were aspects that exceeded football that made him happy in Lisbon.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Fernandes said on the prospect of returning: “The time I spent here makes me think I’d like to come back. There are many things beyond football. If that possibility arises one day, why not? I was happy here and I’d like to be again.”

The playmaker quickly became the main man at Old Trafford after arriving, inspiring them to third and second place finishes in successive seasons. He was just named the PFA Player of the Year and has, for so long, been a rare bright light despite the team's struggles.

He recently decided to halt talks of a new contract with the club, admitting their current struggles are not the right environment for him or the team to discuss prolonging their relationship.

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes was a huge success during his time at Sporting Lisbon

He said: “We ‌spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in at ‌the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but because of the context of the team and the club, I just put that to one side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations."

United and Sporting have not met in Europe since the 2007/08 season, when Cristiano Ronaldo scored the winner in both games as the Red Devils went on to claim continental glory.

The club have won two and lost two of their four Champions League games thus far, winning most recently against Roma at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes’ private thoughts on Michael Carrick sacking after chat with ex-Man Utd teammate
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes’ private thoughts on Michael Carrick sacking after chat with ex-Man Utd teammate

Bruno Fernandes spoke his mind behind closed doors when Manchester United replaced Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino.

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes made his feelings clear over the international break. (Image: Sportsphoto/Allstar, Getty Images)

Rasmus Hojlund has claimed that Bruno Fernandes was left heartbroken by Michael Carrick's dismissal.

‌



‌



The Napoli striker, who departed Old Trafford for the Diego Armando Maradona Stadium during the summer in a transfer valued at £44m, caught up with the Manchester United captain throughout the November international break, when Portugal welcomed Denmark for the penultimate match of the UEFA Nations League group stage phase.

‌



While they were on duty for their national sides, the Reds dismissed Carrick. The next day, mere hours before Hojlund and Fernandes faced each other at the Braga Municipal Stadium, United revealed the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino.

‌



The Reds captain praised the arrival of the Argentine after domestic football resumed, characterising him as someone who delivers 'very good energy' to the squad, while also being 'very strong' and 'strict'.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

During an interview with The Independent, the former United striker disclosed what Fernandes had privately expressed about the managerial change before making public comments.

‌



Hojlund said: "In the international break, when I spoke with Bruno and Diogo, they were all obviously devastated that Michael was going, but also looking forward to some change.

"I am still speaking with Patrick [Dorgu, his Denmark teammate] and I just wish the guys all the best and I am sure they will turn it around this season."

‌



View 2 Images Rasmus Hojlund said, "There's only one club in Manchester," after scoring against City on Tuesday night. (Image: Richard Sellers/Getty Images)

United have managed just a solitary Premier League victory, stretching back to August when they overcame Ipswich Town, and find themselves embroiled in what is shaping up to be a desperate fight against the drop.

‌



Despite an absolutely dreadful start to the campaign, Hojlund has backed his former side to embrace the challenge of turning their fortunes around. The Dane, who netted only 26 goals in 95 appearances across two seasons at Old Trafford, said: "United is a massive club and you can't take anything away from that.

"There are so many people following the club around the world and you can't really escape from it, it is almost too high when it is good and almost too low when it is bad, so it is all about trying to be in that middle and now I think I tried both the highs and the lows there. The pressure is part of the club. It comes with playing for Man United."

‌



Hojlund, who was back in Manchester this week for Napoli's 2-2 draw to Enzo Maresca's side in the Champions League, grew up as a United supporter and continues to follow their results closely.

"I am watching all the games I can," added the 23-year-old. "Especially from the red side of Manchester. It is unfortunate [that United are struggling]."

‌



United currently sit second from bottom in the Premier League, yet Hojlund insists they possess far too much quality to suffer relegation. He said: "It is a temporary picture, I think they will get back to the top.

"The Premier League is like this. I read the other day that Bournemouth were in the relegation zone after a couple of games, now they have won the last five games and are in the top half of the table.

Article continues below

"They have got a lot of quality. I have seen the guys training day by day and I know the players really well and they have got a great squad, good leaders, good professionals, so I am sure they will turn it around. Hopefully they will get it right with Mauricio."

Sports.title: Chelsea urged to sign Virgil van Dijk next summer with Liverpool future uncertain
Sports.content:
Chelsea urged to sign Virgil van Dijk next summer with Liverpool future uncertain

Virgil van Dijk's Liverpool future remains unclear and, with his contract winding down, Chelsea have been told to make a play for the Dutch defender

View 2 Images Virgil van Dijk's future at Liverpool remains unclear (Image: Getty Images)

Jamie Redknapp has urged Chelsea to go after Virgil van Dijk, insisting the Liverpool defender still has two more years left at the top with the Anfield club weighing up whether to offer him a contract extension.

‌



‌



It means the Dutchman, who moved to the Reds back in 2018, could be looking for a new club come the summer. His arrival coincided with Liverpool becoming a trophy-winning force once more and he's remained their defensive leader for almost a decade.

‌



Chelsea have recently shifted their recruitment approach, having previously gone after young talent Xabi Alonso has now looked to get some experienced heads into the building - signing Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson in the summer.

‌



Redknapp hopes Van Dijk will extend his stay at Anfield but, should he pursue a new challenge, believes Chelsea should absolutely look to prolong his spell in the Premier League by bringing him to Stamford Bridge.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



He told Sky Vegas: "I don’t know for sure, he might end up staying. I hope he does. They should try and get Virgil van Dijk in the summer. That’s what I’d do. Just someone there, you’re not going to get five years out of him, but I still think he’s got two years at the top.

"I think he’d be a great signing. He might want to go to the MLS. He might want to go somewhere. But he might fancy London. And if he doesn’t sign a new contract at Liverpool, that’s who they should try and sign."

‌



Redknapp cited how Thiago Silva, who didn't move to Chelsea until he was 35, was a hugely influence figure in their defence despite his age. The Brazilian would ultimately win a Champions League with the Blues.

View 2 Images Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso raised eyebrows with some of his more experienced signings in the summer

‌



Van Dijk admitted in the past week that he himself remains in the dark over his future, but still believes he has something to offer at the top level.

He said: "The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion. Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see. At this moment of time, if anyone says that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.

Article continues below

The Dutchman also added: "If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer."

Sports.title: Arsenal star singled out by Borussia Dortmund coach who saw clear 'advantage'
Sports.content:
Arsenal star singled out by Borussia Dortmund coach who saw clear 'advantage'

Jobe Bellingham and Borussia Dortmund left London with a point after fighting back to hold Arsenal in their Champions League encounter

View 2 Images Borussia Dortmund boss Niko Kovac singled out one of Arsenal's midfielders

Jobe Bellingham admitted that his Borussia Dortmund coach, Niko Kovac, made it clear that he had an advantage over Myles Lewis-Skelly and pushed him to exploit it.

‌



‌



The German side rallied after going behind early on to leave the Emirates with a point, owing to their second-half equaliser. Arsenal were hugely dominant early on and were made to regret missing so many chances in the opening 45 minutes.

‌



Dortmund were much more of a threat in the second-half with Maximilian Beier scoring their leveller. Bellingham himself thought he had completed the turnaround, only for the offside flag to deny him.

‌



But the recently capped England star was told to go after Lewis-Skelly, who was playing alongside Declan Rice in the Arsenal midfield. Bellingham knew he had a height advantage and Kovac urged him to use that to get one over on his compatriot.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



He said on Amazon Prime Video: "One of the coaches pointed out to me that I was against Myles [Lewis-Skelly]. For the long ball – I don’t want to say a mismatch – but I’m obviously bigger.

"You would expect that if I was against Gabriel or Ezri [Konsa] it would be a bit more difficult to win the long balls. I thought that there was a bit of an advantage there in terms of height. I managed to win a few flick-ons and get us up the pitch. We varied it well, we played short, and we retained possession and defended a lot better in transitions."

‌



Bellingham confessed he was "gutted" to see the offside flag go up against him, having reeled away to celebrate in front of the travelling Dortmund supporters.

View 2 Images Jobe Bellingham was urged to take on Myles Lewis-Skelly in the air

‌



The German side sit top of the Bundesliga and have won three of their five Champions League games - their only defeat coming away at Bodo/Glimt.

Mikel Arteta confessed he was frustrated not to see Dortmund lose for a second time given the level of dominance Arsenal enjoyed, insisting they have to do more when they're on top.

Article continues below

He said: "Obviously the feeling is that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance, the amount of chances, the situation, and even shots that are not there. We are three against two, two against one, and the ball doesn't land with the right person. There is an element of luck, there is an element of us finishing the actions better."

Sports.title: Premier League send 'furious messages' as Man City charges meeting disrupted
Sports.content:
Premier League send 'furious messages' as Man City charges meeting disrupted

The meeting was interrupted after the Premier League sent "furious messages"

View 2 Images (Image: UK Parliament)

Premier League chiefs interrupted a Commons select committee session to refute suggestions they have forked out £500million in legal costs on the Manchester City case. The allegations was had been raised by Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee chair Dame Caroline Dinenage as MPs grilled Independent Football Regulator (IFR) chair David Kogan and chief executive Richard Monks.

‌



‌



City were hit with charges in February 2023 over 115 alleged violations of financial regulations covering nine seasons from 2009 to 2018, with the club accused of artificially inflating sponsorship agreements and concealing payments to players and managers.

‌



After a private hearing in late 2024, an independent commission delivered its judgment on September 29, finding City guilty on 114 of the 115 charges. It was determined the club employed "sham" contracts to artificially boost revenues by over £900m.

‌



City have vigorously contested all allegations and submitted a comprehensive appeal on October 1.

The Premier League's legal expenses incurred in this matter were cited at a meeting on Wednesday at approximately £500m. But Dinenage was compelled to intervene, revealing that she had received "furious messages" disputing the figure she suggested.

More than an hour into the session, held in Portcullis House, Westminster, Kogan was addressing the Premier League-EFL backstop when he was interrupted by Dame Caroline.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

MPs had also been interrogating Kogan and Monks on whether the IFR - only established in 2025 - possessed the authority to compel City's owners to relinquish the club and how the regulator would finance a colossal legal battle if taken to court.

‌



She stated: "Can I just intervene and just say that the Premier League is desperate for me to say that they haven't spent £500m fighting the Man City case.

"I'm saying it because I am getting furious messages from the Premier League to tell you that. I would like to see them bring such diligence to the issue of funding so we wouldn't need a backstop."

‌



The assertion was made earlier during the session by Dame Caroline. Kogan responded playfully: "I have to say, I didn't realise this was an interactive session. Are they criticising anything that I've said?" Dame Caroline answered: "To be honest, I haven't engaged with them."

Reports indicate that the sum accumulated by the Premier League in this particular case could reach £50m. This remains unconfirmed, though City may be obliged to reimburse the actual figure depending on how their appeal concludes.

‌



View 2 Images Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee chair Dame Caroline Dinenage (Image: UK Parliament)

The appeal hearing is scheduled to commence mid-way through next month and could span several days. The conclusions from that appeal and whether City's guilty verdict will stand are anticipated to be delivered in the New Year.

‌



Should the appeal fail, a ruling on penalties will follow. The Premier League rulebook grants the independent commission authority to impose any punishment it sees fit, ranging from points deductions to full expulsion from the top flight.

Upon filing their appeal, City claimed the commission's verdict contained "clear material errors of law, principle and fact."

Article continues below

The process is not a retrial, and City must demonstrate legal or procedural failings to succeed.

City also retain the right to launch a further separate appeal against any sanctions that may be handed down.

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres fires clear Man City warning as Arsenal’s title rivals await their fate
Sports.content:
Viktor Gyokeres fires clear Man City warning as Arsenal’s title rivals await their fate

Viktor Gyokeres says future opponents will soon be on the end of a thumping as the Arsenal striker insists he wants to stay and fight for a starting place

View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres insists Man City remain a huge threat to Arsenal in the title race

Viktor Gyokeres insists Arsenal cannot think about any potential punishment for Manchester City - and warned they are still a major threat in the title race.

‌



‌



City face Arsenal at the Emirates on Sunday for the first time since being found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

‌



That will ensure City get a hot reception but it has also meant Enzo Maresca’s men have almost become an after thought in the title race because there is an expectation they will get clobbered with a huge points deduction.

‌



But Gyokeres says despite the looming punishment and City’s inconsistent form - they have won just one of their last seven games in all competitions - Arsenal must be fully focused and ready for a huge test.

Viktor Gyokeres and Mikel Arteta in full agreement as Arsenal frustrated by Borussia Dortmund READ MORE :

Howard Webb shuts down Arsenal v Liverpool penalty debate after Andoni Iraola complaint READ MORE :

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

When asked whether it changes anything for Arsenal as they wait for the punishment, Gyokeres said: “No. It is what it is. We are focused on the game on Sunday.

‌



“We can’t control that. It has nothing to do with us. So, we don’t put any energy into that.

“I think they still have a very good squad, very good players. Of course, they are there and I think they can play well.

‌



“Sometimes, you may have a period where you maybe don’t get the results all the time - which is normal for any club. It is going to be a difficult game on Sunday. But it is always fun with big games. It is going to be good.”

View 3 Images Gyokeres wants to stay and fight for his place in Mikel Arteta's side

‌



Gyokeres has started just one Premier League game this season but there was a reminder of his quality with his wonder strike against Borussia Dortmund.

But despite limited opportunities, the Arsenal striker insists he is not thinking about January or the club being linked to other forwards and the impact that could have on him. Instead, Gyokeres insisted he is happy and will seize his chance when it comes.

‌



"For me, I always focus on the games,” he said. “I want to do well when I get a chance to play. That is my main goal. I really enjoy being here and playing here. That’s always my aim.”

Gyokeres says Arsenal are determined to win back-to-back titles with Mikel Arteta’s men six points clear at the top of the Premier League.

‌



That would show how strong they are but they have been struggling to put games to bed after throwing away leads in their last two games against Dortmund and Newcastle.

Gyokeres says that a team will soon be on the end of a real battering because Arsenal are creating chances - and will soon blitz someone. Incredibly, they had 30 shots against Dortmund but only four were on target.

‌



View 3 Images The Swedish striker got on the scoresheet during Arsenal's draw with Borussia Dortmund

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Gyokeres added: “Of course, we always want to win titles and we know how tough it is in the Premier League with the games and the teams.

“It is always going to be tough. But we have an amazing squad, amazing players, so that’s the aim. We push each other every day to achieve that and we are definitely going to go for it.

‌



“We always go into games wanting to win. I think, overall, we have done really well this season. Obviously, we have drawn two games that we could have won, with the amount of chances that we had in both games.

“But Sunday is another game and we are going to prepare for that one, and we are going to go for it.

Article continues below

“I have been feeling good in the last couple of games. Obviously, we should have probably won against Dortmund with the amount of chances. But overall, I think we played really well and that was good, at least.”

Sports.title: England's All Blacks Tests 'World Cup practice' | 'Ireland still not contenders'
Sports.content:
Head coaches Steve Borthwick of England, Andy Farrell of Ireland and Dave Rennie of New Zealand speak to media ahead of the final weekend of the inaugural Nations Championship.

England, having come into the tournament under a cloud of pressure following the worst Six Nations display in their history earlier this year (four losses, fifth place), have stormed to victories over Australia, Japan and New Zealand this month.

Last week, Borthwick's side secured a record 25-point victory over the All Blacks at Allianz Stadium. With England finishing second behind France in the northern hemisphere standings and New Zealand runners-up to South Africa in the southern hemisphere table, the two sides are now set for an immediate rematch.

England face the All Blacks again at Twickenham on Saturday, with Borthwick viewing the latest clash as valuable preparation for the Rugby World Cup in Australia in 10 months' time.

"The nature of this tournament, it's a new tournament, is the understanding that international games have that level of jeopardy," Borthwick told the media on Wednesday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' James Cole looks ahead to England's upcoming Nations Championship Test against New Zealand

"The consequence upon each of these games. This is an important step.

"It's a real positive step in this competition towards the jeopardy of being involved in World Cup games.

"In the World Cup, you want to be in situations where you're having to back up big games in multiple weeks.

"I think it's going to be an excellent Test match this weekend, a really tough Test match against a super dangerous New Zealand team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England's Fin Smith reflects on his side's historic Nations Championship victory over New Zealand

"We're expecting New Zealand to come hard at the breakdown, and we're expecting them to really challenge us there.

"All our focus this weekend is we're expecting the very best of New Zealand. They're full of so much talent and so much experience. We know this is going to be a fierce Test match.

"We've got a young squad. We've got some players that are very experienced at the end of the spectrum and a lot of players that are young and haven't played against teams like New Zealand that often. So I think it was an important step in our development.

"This Saturday is another very important step. Each and every international experience we have is vital for the long-term development of this team."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Cowan-Dickie tells Sky Sports he's excited for his side's second clash against the All Blacks in just a week

Ireland's Farrell: We still aren't World Cup contenders despite win vs Springboks

Ireland head coach Andy Farrell began this Test window by telling the media that, unlike in 2023, this current Ireland side - based on performances to date - are not Rugby World Cup contenders.

What has followed this month is dominant victories over Argentina and Fiji in Dublin, followed by a stunning 20-17 success over double world champions South Africa last week.

Ireland face Australia at Twickenham on Friday, but Farrell reiterated his point that Ireland are not in World Cup-title conversations.

"No [Ireland are not World Cup contenders]," he said. "We took a step in the right direction last week, but that's got to continue to be that, hasn't it? To make sure that we keep feeling that way.

Image: Ireland put in a stunning performance to beat world No 1 South Africa in Dublin last week

"That's always going to be the challenge [emotional challenge a week after win over Springboks].

"Plus, we have a six-day turnaround, and we play Scotland in the World Cup with a six-day turnaround as well. Getting yourself back up, that's the way you get some consistency in your performance, so it's pretty important.

"You are testing your depth, and you're always going to get that with four quality games over such a short space of time. But the Six Nations is five games, and then the World Cup is seven games if you've got any ambition, really.

"It's not ideal [shortage at No 8], but again, these are things that happen over a tournament, and that's what we've found this year.

Image: Ireland head coach Andy Farrell reiterated his side are 'not World Cup contenders' despite beating the Springboks

"Obviously, from the start having so many experienced players in Caelan Doris and Jack Conan out - played plenty of times for us - and then we've lost a few as we've gone on.

"But you've got to be able to adapt with the squad that you've got, and you've been able to do that so far.

"It is what it is [Dan Sheehan's two-Test ban]. He had a fair hearing, and we move on."

Image: Captain Dan Sheehan is missing for Ireland this week due to a two-game suspension

All Blacks boss Rennie responds to calls for his sacking: 'Nature of the job'

New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie has overseen a first All Blacks defeat to Wales since 1953 and a record loss to England this month.

Such results have led to huge pressure and reports he should be sacked.

"I don't listen to anything. I don't read anything, so that probably helps," Rennie said.

"Look, it's the nature of the job, and it's the expectations of this role too.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News reflects on Wales beating New Zealand for the first time since 1953

"But international rugby now is really tight. You look at the recent results, and I think four years ago heading into a World Cup, Ireland and France were ranked No 1 and No 2, so things can change really quickly.

"It wasn't that long ago South Africa and us were No 1 and No 2. We're well aware of how tough it is, and England are a really good side.

"But we believe if we get our game right, we'll be competitive at the weekend.

Image: All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has overseen a month where his side lost to Wales for the first time since 1953, and suffered a record defeat to England

"We're just excited to wear the jersey again and put on a performance that we're proud of and the country's proud of. We'll talk about fatigue next week.

"You want it to hurt, because we're all hurt after the weekend.

"Sunday's still a bit of a struggle, but you can't afford to sulk because you've got to look forward and think: 'How do we fix things?'

"Our job is to try and bring energy and connection and we're a really tight group. We want to get a result on the weekend for us, but also for the country.

"We're really appreciative of all the support we've got, especially after last week's performance. We're determined to rectify that."

Sports.title: Carra: Lammens confidence worrying but Poch will feel Man Utd were robbed
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher says Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens' confidence is a cause for concern after his howler cost Mauricio Pochettino a first win since taking charge.

It was a nightmare performance for Lammens, who unnecessarily gave away the penalty for Luis Suarez's opener just 75 seconds after saving the Sporting striker's poorly taken first spot-kick.

Lammens, 24, then spilled a routine cross late in the second half which allowed Suarez to equalise for 2-2, denying United a first away win of the season and first away Champions League win for five years.

The Belgium international, signed from Club Brugge last summer, restored calm between the sticks last season after Andre Onana's calamitous spell as No 1, but has had a poor start to his second season at Old Trafford.

Image: Senne Lammens' protests fall on deaf ears after he conceded a second goal to allow Sporting to draw level with Man Utd

Delivering his verdict on Lammens' performance, Carragher said on CBS: "You worry about the confidence of that goalkeeper now.

"That mistake for the equaliser, the 2-2 goal, you say sometimes 'an amateur goalkeeper wouldn't make that mistake'. If that was an amateur goalkeeper you'd be thinking 'that can't happen'. That just can't happen at this level."

Carragher questioned if United had the options in their goalkeeper department to bring Lammens out of the spotlight for a brief while.

Pochettino could call on Karl Darlow if he wanted to make a change at goalkeeper. He was signed in the summer on a free transfer from Leeds, where he was the No 1 for the second half of last season.

"It is getting to the stage with the goalkeeper now," Carragher added. "The focus on a Man Utd goalkeeper is always big if he's making mistakes. I don't think the back-up's even at the level where, no matter how poorly the goalkeeper plays, you change it."

Carra: Poch will feel Man Utd were robbed

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Clinton Morrison watches on in amazement as Manchester United's late winner against Sporting Liston is ruled out

Carragher felt United were "unlucky" to see two goals controversially ruled out but criticised the players for allowing games to spiral out of control when they suffer set-backs.

The Sky Sports pundit said it must frustrate Pochettino but will make for an "unbelievable" watch when the fly-on-the-wall documentary being filmed this season is released.

"Why do they keep shooting themselves in the foot?" said Carragher. "As a manager, what can he really do about the goalkeeper or Tielemans making a stupid tackle at the end?

"He'll be really frustrated because that could have been a really big result for them tonight at 2-1, and there were unlucky with the 3-2 [goal being disallowed].

"He will feel they've been robbed by the referee and he'll say they should have won the game.

"But he'll be looking at isolated incidents and it feels like every game is mad. There's never a normal game where you win 1-0 or you draw 1-1 and nothing really happens. Something happens all the time that you're almost laughing at, or you've got your head in your hands if you're a Man Utd fan.

"There is always madness or craziness. I mean, the documentary is going to be unbelievable isn't it."

Were Man Utd hard done by to have two goals ruled out?

The last thing Pochettino needed after the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool - and Leny Yoro's now overturned red card - was more refereeing controversy. However, there was contention around both goals United had ruled out in Lisbon.

Amad had the ball in the back of the net toward the end of the first half to equalise - but not before the whistle had gone for what was judged to have been a foul by Tielemans, who clearly won the ball with his slide tackle.

The United midfielder received a booking for his follow through on Sporting defender Inacio, who went down dramatically despite receiving the slightest of contact. VAR could not intervene as the whistle had gone.

Morrison, who said Tielemans "won the ball", was adamant that it was the wrong call.

United's second disallowed goal, which was ruled out following VAR intervention, saw Dorgu penalised for making contact with Sporting goalkeeper Kaique before he punched into his own net.

Carragher felt it was "very harsh" for the referee to disallow the goal after being sent to his monitor.
