Sports.title: Super League reveals new format, seven-team play-offs, international games
Sports.content:
Super League has revealed a new format, a seven-team play-off system and Magic Weekend and Rivals Round dates, on the same day London Broncos were confirmed as the competition's 15th team for 2027.

Earlier this month, Super League announced its 14 clubs had voted in favour of a motion to expand to 15 teams for the 2027 season.

Clubs were then invited to apply, with London Broncos - who had made no secret of their desire to be in the top flight - one of those to do so having completed the treble in 2026 during a brilliant season for them in the Championship.

With 15 teams competing, the 2027 Super League fixture schedule will take on a new format with the season starting on Thursday January 28.

Each club will have 13 opportunities to play in front of their home supporters, alongside 13 away fixtures, with 14 clubs competing in the Magic Weekend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League Grand Final between Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity

The structure means each team will face every other club at least once, while there will be one different opponent that each club does not host at home and travel to during the regular season.

The expanded competition will see every club receive two bye rounds during the regular season, while London Broncos will receive an additional bye during Magic Weekend.

Rivals Round will return over the Easter weekend (March 25), bringing some of the biggest rivalries in sport to the forefront of the Super League calendar.

Magic Weekend will remain a key feature of the Super League calendar in 2027, returning to Everton FC's home, Hill Dickinson Stadium, in Liverpool on Saturday May 1 and Sunday May 2 (Bank Holiday weekend).

New-look seven-team play-off system

Under the new play-off format, the League Leaders will earn an automatic home place in the semi-finals, while the remaining six teams will compete in the Eliminators for the opportunity to move one step closer to Old Trafford.

As a result, the runners-up will no longer progress automatically to the semi-finals.

The revised system will create a new dimension to the race for the Super League Grand Final, with seven clubs remaining in contention for the ultimate prize.

Image: London Broncos have been confirmed as the 15th Super League team for the 2027 season

More international Super League fixtures and history in Dublin

The 2027 season will see Super League continue to take some of its biggest games to international audiences, with major events confirmed in Las Vegas and Dublin.

Bradford Bulls and Leigh Leopards will meet at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on Saturday February 27, as Super League returns to the United States.

The competition will then make history in April, with the first-ever Super League fixtures played in Ireland.

Warrington Wolves and Wigan Warriors face-off at Laya Arena in Dublin on Saturday, April 24, before St Helens and Hull FC meet at the same venue on Sunday, April 25.

The Dublin double-header brings four Super League clubs to the Irish capital for a landmark weekend, providing supporters with a unique opportunity to experience the competition in a new setting.-

Magic Weekend fixtures will be announced on Wednesday December 2, while the full 2027 Super League fixtures will be revealed on Thursday December 3.

Sports.title: Poch denied first Man Utd win by Lammens howler at Sporting
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino was denied a first victory as Manchester United head coach by a goalkeeping howler from Senne Lammens in an incident-packed 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League as Youri Tielemans was sent off late on.

United looked to be on course for a first away win of the season after captain Bruno Fernandes scored two goals in the first five minutes of the second half only for Lammens to spill the ball in the box for Luis Suarez to equalise with his second goal of the game.

Pochettino thought United had gone back in front for a second time shortly after Lammens' error when Sporting goalkeeper Kaique punched into his own net at a corner. However, it was ruled out following an on-field review for a foul by substitute Patrick Dorgu.

It was a damaging night for Lammens, who gave away the penalty for Suarez's first goal just 75 seconds after saving the Sporting striker's poorly taken spot-kick. The man brought into replace the error-prone Andre Onana is now beginning to resemble his predecessor.

Image: Man Utd players celebrate as Bruno Fernandes' second goal put them into the lead at Sporting

Fernandes' equaliser three minutes after the restart came from the third penalty of what was a bizarre match. Few moments topped the United skipper's freakish second goal which came thanks a tame effort bouncing up off a divot in the ground and into back of the net.

Tielemans' stoppage-time red will only add to United's frustrations. It was his first booking, for a tame follow-through on Goncalo Inacio, that denied Amad Diallo from equalising late in the first half in one of the more baffling refereeing decisions you will see.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Clinton Morrison watches on in amazement as Manchester United's late winner against Sporting Liston is ruled out

Pochettino's first two matches have seen his side have two players sent off and concede two penalties. If he did not know it before, he certainly knows now that nothing comes easy at United, who sit 19th in the Champions League and Premier League.

Were Man Utd hard done by to have two goals ruled out?

The last thing Pochettino needed after the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool - and Leny Yoro's now overturned red card - was more refereeing controversy. However, there was contention around both goals United had ruled out in Lisbon.

Amad had the ball in the back of the net toward the end of the first half to equalise - but not before the whistle had gone for what was judged to have been a foul by Tielemans, who clearly won the ball with his slide tackle.

The United midfielder received a booking for his follow through on Sporting defender Inacio, who went down dramatically despite receiving the slightest of contact. VAR could not intervene as the whistle had gone.

"It is a terrible decision," said Sky Sports pundit Clinton Morrison. "Tielemans won the ball."

United's second disallowed goal, which was ruled out following VAR intervention, saw Dorgu penalised for making contact with Sporting goalkeeper Kaique before he punched into his own net.

Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher felt it was "very harsh" for the referee to disallow the goal after being sent to his monitor.

Carra: Man Utd 'unlucky' but Lammens error can't happen

Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher to CBS:

"I do think United were a little bit unlucky tonight with the goal disallowed just before half-time. The goal at the end felt very harsh to me, the one where it could have been 3-2...

"The focus on a Man Utd goalkeeper is always big if he's making mistakes. The back-ups aren't even at the level where you could say no matter how poorly the goalkeeper plays, you could change it. You worry about the confidence of that goalkeeper now.

"That mistake for the equaliser, the 2-2 goal, you say sometimes 'an amateur goalkeeper wouldn't make that mistake' and that just can't happen at this level."

Poch praises Man Utd 'personality'

Man Utd head coach Mauricio Pochettino to TNT Sports:

"I'm so proud of the players. It was a tough game. I liked the team we played for 90 minutes, the personality, the character. It's difficult to find a game where you get punished in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions. Today we showed how we want to play after just one week of working together.

"We need to concentrate and focus more, try to recover better. The performance like today's is the best medicine to prepare for the next game."

29: PENALTY TO SPORTING! Martinez fouls Catamo to give Sporting a spot-kick.

31: LAMMENS SAVES IT! Man Utd are spared as Suarez's poor effort is saved by the Belgian.

32: ANOTHER PENALTY TO SPORTING! Seventy-five seconds later, Lammens fouls Araujo in the box to go from hero to zero.

33: GOAL FOR SPORTING! Suarez makes no mistake from his second penalty.

Sports.title: In-form Stoke see off Millwall to make it five wins on the bounce
Sports.content:
George Hirst bagged a brace as Stoke secured a fifth successive Championship win by beating Millwall 2-1 at the bet365 Stadium.

The Scotland international scored just his second goal for the Potters in the 1-0 win over Birmingham on Saturday and doubled his tally for the season to take Stoke back into the automatic promotion places.

Mark Sykes' stunning strike halved the deficit in the final 10 minutes, but Stoke held on to claim an 11th win in their last 14 outings.

The defeat was Millwall's fourth in a row, coming a day after it was announced they had been ordered to play a future match in front of a partially closed stadium for offensive chanting.

Millwall had lost each of their last three league outings without scoring but it was the Lions who created the first chance within the first two minutes.

Tairyk Arconte broke the offside trap and latched on to Camiel Neghli's pass before bursting away down the right and forcing Viktor Johansson to push his low effort away from goal.

Stoke welcomed back star midfielder Ethan Galbraith from illness and the former Manchester United midfielder's spectacular volley crashed against the bar in an exhilarating opening five minutes.

Millwall manager Alex Neil, who was sacked by the Potters in December 2023, could only watch as Jack McGlynn's defence-splitting pass found Hirst, who steadied himself before picking out the bottom corner in the 13th minute.

McGlynn, Stoke's top scorer in the league this season, almost turned from provider to scorer when his long-range shot whistled past the upright.

Stoke had been good value for their lead and grabbed a second five minutes before half-time. Million Manhoef had also been recalled to the starting line-up and was allowed time and space in the Millwall box before picking out Hirst to turn into the corner.

Neil made a hat-trick of changes as the Lions set about trying to get back into the clash.

One of the reinforcements, top scorer Lyndon Dykes, arrowed a long throw into the Stoke box inside the first minute of the second half, which was kept alive by Neghli before fellow substitute Kyrell Lisbie headed goalwards.

Millwall offered much more of a threat after the break as the Potters came under their first sustained pressure of the evening.

Lisbie scuffed his shot when the ball broke kindly to him in the area and Dykes wasn't able to get to the follow-up. Alfie Doughty then saw his powerful effort blocked by Ben Johnson and the rebound was blazed over by Derek Mazou-Sacko.

Stoke earned some respite at the other end when Bae Jun-ho earned a free-kick for the hosts in a dangerous position, which McGlynn forced Lukas Jensen to push to safety.

Stoke manager Mark Robins brought on Sam Gallagher and Robert Bozenik in a double change in attack, and the pair combined for what should have been a Stoke third when Bozenik shot wide after Gallagher's clever cut back.

Millwall halved the deficit with nine minutes remaining as Sykes drifted infield and rifled his left-footed effort beyond Johansson from distance, but Stoke held on to keep their winning run on track.

The managers

Stoke's Mark Robins:

"There's been a little bit said about George that is unfair. I think people want to see him working hard and I think he overthought things.

"It's amazing if you just remember that you love playing football and you just go and do it, and everything else tends to fall into place. It's not as simple as that but it really helps, and he's done that.

"First half was everything I thought we'd be. I thought we were good, we moved the ball well, we looked dangerous every time we had it.

"What we didn't do in the second half was get close to them at the top end of the pitch and that's sometimes when you tire in a game.

"You want your players to not sit in and invite the inevitable but you can't do that. The players will need to learn and understand what happened in the game. You can't rest on your laurels and see the game out.

"Go back to what happened on Saturday when we were down to 10 men, you don't do the same thing, we've got 11 men, matched in numbers and you've got to go and make things happen for yourself and we didn't do that.

"We weren't clinical enough, we didn't make the right choices in the second half, we had two really clear-cut chances. That was the disappointment."

Millwall's Alex Neil:

"First half I didn't think we played with enough belief, enough quality, enough understanding. I thought we lacked loads of things in the first half.

"I thought we got into some good areas and I thought we got into some good pockets but we didn't really do anything as if we believed we were going to score a goal.

"The two goals we conceded were shocking. First half we lacked everything a Millwall team should be, we lacked aggression, intensity, we didn't get close enough.

"Their two lads in the middle of the pitch controlled the game, they were comfortable. The centre backs ate our forwards up.

"It was vastly improved in the second half, but in my opinion it's easy to play a game when you're losing 2-0, to go out and show a little bit more than you showed in the first half.

"We had three or four players in the game that took part, and they showed a bit of personality on the pitch, there was too many hoping that something was going to happen rather than believing you can go and influence a game.

"We had three fresh air shots in the box where the ball comes across and we miss the ball. You can talk about intensity, duels, running, but you also need quality. And if you don't have enough quality, this is a difficult league to win enough games in."

Sports.title: The assist of the season! Remarkable new footage shows moment Bruno Fernandes created the divot HIMSELF before scoring one of the most bizarre goals EVER in Man United's chaotic draw with Sporting Lisbon
Sports.content:
Footage appears to show Bruno Fernandes created the divot in the turf that led to his fortunate second goal against Sporting Lisbon.

The Manchester United captain scored a bizarre goal against his former side on Tuesday night, with his long-range shot taking a fortuitous bobble off the Estadio Jose Alvalade pitch to leave goalkeeper Kaique Pereira helpless.

While fingers were initially pointed at the ground staff, footage shows the divot was actually created by Fernandes himself when he planted his boot into the turf while pressing high up the pitch moments earlier.

Reminiscent of former Liverpool forward Stan Collymore's famous bobbling goal past Blackburn Rovers goalkeeper Tim Flowers in 1996, Fernandes' speculative effort would undoubtedly have been easily gathered by Pereira had it not struck the bump in the turf.

The goal summed up another chaotic evening for United, in which goalkeeping calamities, controversial refereeing calls, three penalties and a red card resulted in a 2-2 draw and left them 19th in the Champions League standings.

United trailed at the break after goalkeeper Senne Lammens saved one penalty before conceding another 75 seconds later that was converted by Luis Suarez after the Belgian's reckless challenge on Max Araujo.

"This is the assist of the season" 😅



Bruno Fernandes created the divot in the turf which led to his second goal of the evening for Man Utd 🪄



📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/c4g2sC33pA — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 25, 2026

Fernandes' speculative effort would undoubtedly have been easily gathered by Pereira had it not struck the bump in the turf

The visitors were left furious when Amad Diallo saw a first-half leveller ruled out after referee Szymon Marciniak blew his whistle too early for VAR to intervene, but United turned the game around shortly after the restart.

Lisandro Martinez, who had given away the first penalty, won one at the other end that Fernandes converted before the former Sporting star fired in the long-range effort that bounced over Pereira and into the net.

More drama followed as Lammens flapped at a cross under pressure from Suarez, allowing the striker to score, before Patrick Dorgu was adjudged to have put undue pressure on Pereira when forcing an own goal from the goalkeeper.

United were left frustrated by what they viewed as a lack of consistency after Marciniak was sent to the pitchside monitor to review the second decision, and their mood darkened further when Youri Tielemans was sent off for a second booking late on.

Former United player Ashley Young claimed that 2022 World Cup referee Marciniak's decision-making during the clash was a 'disgrace'.

Young told BBC Radio 5 Live: 'The referee’s performance was just simply wow. The decisions that he gave.

'Youri Tielemans getting booked to eventually getting sent off later because you booked him when it should never have been a booking and it should have been an equalising goal.

'The third goal that should have stood because he’s saying Patrick Dorgu fouled the keeper. The keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me.

'His decision-making is nothing more than a disgrace.'

Former United player Ashley Young claimed that 2022 World Cup referee Marciniak's decision-making during the clash was a 'disgrace'

Young’s former United team-mate Rio Ferdinand echoed that frustration on X.

Writing alongside a pain image of himself, he said with two emojis indicating angry swearing: 'REFEREE. What have I just witnessed tonight!

'Regardless – individual mistakes again proving costly. Positives to take from tonight, recharge the batteries!'

In what is proving to be an eventful first week in charge, Pochettino was asked to provide his assessment of the game. The Argentine said: 'It depends which way you prefer (to analyse the game). So proud of the players. It was a very tough game. I like the team for the 90 minutes, the personality, the character.

'We showed the way we want to play. We've only been working together one week.'

But, he added: 'Always we need to concentrate more and focus more. Try to recover better. We start to fix. With a performance like today it's the best medicine to prepare the next game.'

United have little time to take stock before their next outing, with Brentford visiting Old Trafford on Saturday.

Sports.title: Frustrated Mauricio Pochettino accuses referee of 'punishing' Man United in chaotic Sporting Lisbon draw after having TWO goals ruled out - as former star Ashley Young labels official's performance as a 'disgrace'
Sports.content:
Frustrated Mauricio Pochettino accuses referee of 'punishing' Man United in chaotic Sporting Lisbon draw after having TWO goals ruled out - as former star Ashley Young labels official's performance as a 'disgrace'

Mauricio Pochettino was left frustrated after Manchester United were ‘punished’ by more controversial refereeing decisions in Lisbon on Wednesday night.

Three days after Pochettino was left raging over Leny Yoro’s early red card at Anfield, United were held to a 2-2 Champions League draw by Sporting after conceding two penalties and having two goals disallowed by Polish referee Szymon Marciniak who also sent off Youri Tielemans.

‘It’s difficult to find a game where you get punished so much in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions,’ said Pochettino.

Asked if the decision to rule out Amad Diallo’s goal before half-time and book Tielemans was particularly harsh, the United manager remained tight-lipped but nodded.

‘It’s difficult to answer because I think everyone knows it’s impossible to understand why that happened on the field,’ added Pochettino before adding sarcastically: ‘I think it's a good welcome for us after seven days! Today it's going to be my first week in charge.

‘Through our experience, if we go back and remember circumstances in different clubs, things like this you will suffer because it's the circumstance that always is against us.’

Mauricio Pochettino gave his verdict on the performance of referee Szymon Marciniak

Marciniak was at the centre of several controversial decisions as United drew 2-2 with Sporting

Pochettino also defended his goalkeeper Senne Lammens who was at fault for both Sporting’s goals despite saving a penalty.

‘Football is about making mistakes,’ he said. ‘I want to support always my player. It's something that happened in that case.

‘It's our responsibility too to provide the best tools. I think in this type of action also our defensive line needs to cover better the keeper because it was very difficult.

‘It's to blame us because I think we need to manage better this type of situation. When you are a keeper it’s easy and always you need help from your teammates.’

Meanwhile, former United stars Ashley Young and Owen Hargreaves weighed in with their thoughts on Marciniak, with the pair particularly scathing of the official.

Speaking on the BBC, Young said: ’The referee’s performance was just simply wow... the decisions that he gave.

’Youri Tielemans getting sent off because you booked him when it should never have been a booking, and it should have been an equalising goal.

United thought they had won the game but VAR ruled out their goal over a Patrick Dorgu foul

’The third goal should have stood because he’s saying Patrick Dorgu fouled the keeper. The keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me.

‘His decision making today is nothing more than a disgrace.’

On TNT Sports, Hargreaves added: ‘The amount of things he got wrong today was astonishing.

'People don’t come to the game to hear you blow your whistle.’

Sports.title: Welcome to the Man United madhouse, Mauricio! Man United emerge from the chaos at Sporting Lisbon with a draw as Senne Lammens joins their band of self-saboteurs in game that had it all, writes CHRIS WHEELER
Sports.content:
Welcome to the Man United madhouse, Mauricio! Man United emerge from the chaos at Sporting Lisbon with a draw as Senne Lammens joins their band of self-saboteurs in game that had it all, writes CHRIS WHEELER

A week into the job and Mauricio Pochettino must be getting used to the madness of Manchester United by now.

If it's not drones flying over the training ground, red card controversies and random divots of grass, it's his own players shooting themselves in the foot.

At least, Pochettino emerged from the craziness in Lisbon with a draw on a night when Bruno Fernandes celebrated his return to the Jose Alvalade Stadium with a couple of goals.

But these are the kind of nights that must drive coaches like Pochettino potty. After the carnage of Michael Carrick's final two games in charge against Roma and Aston Villa, and the rancour of the Argentine's introduction to the Old Trafford circus at Anfield on Sunday, this was another mad, mad spectacle.

Where do we start? The two acts of self-sabotage by goalkeeper Senne Lammens? United's two disallowed goals? The first was harsh on the scorer, Amad Diallo, but also Youri Tielemans who received a booking that led to his sending-off in injury-time. Or maybe that divot, which Fernandes claimed he created and then hit to put United ahead with a bizarre deflected goal?

At the end of all the chaos, United had conceded five penalties in their last five games and picked up four red cards.

Senne Lammens (left) two errors cost Man United a deserving win at Sporting as they drew

New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino comforts Lammens at full-time after his mistakes

That is not something that will sit well with Pochettino. But after venting his frustration with the officiating over Leny Yoro's sending-off at Anfield, which dominated the build-up to this game after it was rescinded, here was another sequence of events that seemed to conspire against him.

It's not as if the Jose Alvalade Stadium was a cauldron of emotion to scramble the senses of the two sets of players and match officials either. Fernandes got a polite round of applause from the fans and a framed memento from his old club before kick-off.

When the teams came out, he was one of three former United players alongside Cristiano Ronaldo and Luis Nani honoured on a tifo of the Sporting Lisbon greats.

It was all very flat until the half-hour mark when United self-imploded again. Geny Catamo picked up the ball on the edge of the United box and teased Lisandro Martinez, playing at left back.

Martinez took the bait and stuck his leg out. He barely caught Sporting's No 10 and it took Catamo a full second to realise he had, before going down theatrically and earning a very soft penalty from Polish referee Szymon Marciniak.

Sporting's top scorer Luis Suarez stepped up and made it easy for Lammens to make the save. It was a let-off for United and potentially a big moment in a difficult season for Lammens.

But he undid his good work 75 seconds later when Maxi Araujo chased a long ball over the top pursued by Noussair Mazraoui. For some reason, Lammens thought it would be a good idea to race 25 yards out of his goal.

Araujo stepped inside the Belgium goalkeeper and went down under his clumsy challenge. Marciniak pointed to the spot again, and this time Suarez made no mistake.

Lammens started positively saving this Luis Suarez penalty before conceding a spot-kick

Yet, minutes later Suarez scored after being given a second penalty following Lammens error

United thought they had eqaulised before half-time but Amad Diallo's header was ruled out for a percieved foul in the build-up by Youri Tielemans that earned him a booking

After all the upset over the officiating at Anfield, United were on the wrong end of another big call just before half-time here when Tielemans stretched to poke the ball through to Diallo and inadvertently caught Goncalo Inacio who went down claiming serious injury.

Goalkeeper Kaique Pereira saved Diallo's first effort and Marciniak blew his whistle for a foul before the Ivorian headed in at the second attempt so there was no opportunity for VAR to review it. The referee booked Tielemans, but there was a strong argument that it wasn't even a foul.

United re-emerged for the second half undeterred and hit back to score twice through Fernandes within five minutes of the restart.

The United captain played the ball through for Martinez and then converted from the spot after his team-mate went down in a tangle of legs with Eduardo Quaresma.

Bruno Fernandes levelled for United just after half-time when they were awarded a penalty

He then put them ahead with this left-footed shot that hit a divot on the pitch before flying in

United's lead was undone late on when Lammens' second major error allowed Suarez to score

United's evening was compounded when Tielemans was sent off late on for a second yellow

Two minutes later, and having made the divot turning in the penalty box 17 seconds earlier, Fernandes somehow managed to hit it with a hopeful effort from 25 yards. Pereira had the ball covered but it took an outrageous deflection just outside the six-yard box and flew through his arms.

But this is United and nothing is straightforward. In the 80th minute, with victory within their grasp, Lammens had all the time in the world to catch a high ball from Ivan Fresneda. Perhaps too long. Unforgivably, he dropped it in front of Suarez who hooked into the net.

There was still time for more drama when United had another goal from a Fernandes' corner chalked off for Patrick Dorgu's foul on Pereira, after VAR sent Marciniak to the monitor, and he then showed Tielemans a second yellow card.

Pochettino looked on frustrated and probably as confused as the rest of us.

Sports.title: Liverpool fans are enjoying watching their team again as they close in on Champions League qualification after Club Brugge victory... now it's time for Andoni Iraola to make it a perfect week at Everton, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola tried to stifle a smirk on Tuesday when it was put to him that he had a fair chance of completing a perfect week by thrashing Manchester United, winning away in Europe and then winning his first-ever Merseyside Derby. The usual responses came back of remaining level-headed and not getting carried away, of course – but Iraola has ticked off two of those three tasks and now goes to Everton with his much-criticised, big-money signings in the form of their Liverpool careers. That is Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, of course, who both scored here to further quash any narratives over them being expensive flops, a debate which had followed them for much of their first year or so on Merseyside. Isak scored a brace to take his season tally to double-figures and make it six away games in a row where he has struck, while Wirtz followed up his best performance of the season against United with a fine strike from distance. Wirtz especially has never been far away from criticism during his time at the club but is silencing his doubters every week and said this week that Iraola had helped him rediscover the player Liverpool thought they were buying for £116million two summers ago. The sentiment spreads beyond Wirtz. After a season of strife, Iraola has brought the feel-good factor back at Anfield and supporters are enjoying watching their team again after a year in which it felt like a chore to do so some weeks. Alexander Isak scored twice as Liverpool beat Club Brugge 3-0 in the Champions League That made it three wins in a row for the Reds as they start to really click under Andoni Iraola Club Brugge 0-3 Liverpool: Match facts CLUB BRUGGE (4-3-3): Sommer 4; Sabbe 5 (Siquet 84), Spileers 5, Mechele 6, Seys 6; Vetlesen 6 (Vermant 75), Potts 7 (Tsawa 84), Vanaken 6; Forbs 7, Tresoldi 6, Lemarechal 7 (Diakhon 75). Subs not used: Jackers, Vanden Driessche, Han-beom Lee, Virgili, Dams, Robberechts, Audoor, Vasovic. Booked: None. Scorers: None. Manager: Ivan Leko 6. LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 7; Frimpong 6 (Van Dijk 73, 6), Araujo 6, Jacquet 7, Kerkez 6; Nyoni 7 (Mac Allister 73, 6), Szoboszlai 7; Munoz 6 (Ngumoha 42, 6), Wirtz 7, Barcola 6 (Chambers 86); ISAK 8 (Koumas 86). Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Tsimikas, McConnell, Danns. Booked: Iraola. Scorers: Isak 13, 82, Wirtz 79. Manager: Andoni Iraola 7. Referee: Alejandro Hernandez (Esp) 6. It is making the Liverpool fans fall for Iraola a little bit more each week. How that feeling would be turbocharged with Derby delight at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday. ‘I was very pleased with the result and the performance overall,’ said Iraola. ‘At 3-0, you can think it was an easy game and I don’t think it was. We were facing a really good team.’ As the 1,000 or so travelling Kop enjoyed their strong Belgian beers and chocolate waffles in this quaint, picturesque city, they were still laughing about poor old Manchester United and Sunday’s 4-0 demolition job. This was a much tougher test against an opposition that had started well in the Champions League with three wins from four, so Liverpool’s performance was never going to be as convincing – but the victory was still important. It helped them take a step closer to cementing a top eight place in this long-winded league phase. That would ease the pressure on a congested calendar by seeing them not only be able to rest players in the latter games of the league stage but also skip a play-off round. Club Brugge are no mugs and they showed that, with energetic winger Carlos Forbs the pick of the bunch. The former Manchester City academy starlet has inherited a certain Cristiano Ronaldo’s No 7 shirt at Portugal and gave Milos Kerkez a testing night here. The Belgian side, like Liverpool, had won three of their first four European games including victory away to Inter. They had won five of the last seven league titles with a brave playing style that Iraola admitted was a pleasure to analyse – which he added was not always the case. Their bold approach was their undoing here, though, with possession tossed away far too easily for Liverpool’s opener after 13 minutes. Yann Sommer, in the winter of his career at 37, passed straight to Bradley Barcola who, via stand-in skipper Dominik Szoboszlai, found Isak. The Swede needed no second invitation to fire home his ninth goal of the season. Isak had been rested for most of Liverpool’s early European outings but was the difference here and loves playing away: he has now netted on his last six games away from Anfield. Liverpool have 12 points from five games and will almost certainly be in the knockout stages Florian Wirtz continued his fine form as he curled in a delightful effort to put Liverpool 2-0 up Iraola will hope to make it the perfect week with victory in Sunday's Merseyside Derby Only Mohamed Salah has done so in seven or more in recent history for Liverpool. Everton would be a fine place to match that record. Despite the scoreline flattering Liverpool, things were far from easy after Isak’s opener. Alisson was needed to deny Felix Lemarechal both sides at half-time and Virgil van Dijk – rested from the start – was called on as a second-half substitute to steady the ship. Winger Victor Munoz limped off in agony after going down before half-time holding his knee. Iraola feared the worst when a stretcher was called but the Spaniard walked off and was feeling ‘optimistic’ after the match, according to the boss. Szoboszlai should have put the game to bed after a sublime team move led to the Hungarian being thwarted by Sommer at point-blank range, while Barcola was also guilty of wastefulness after getting his feet tangled up when in a dangerous position. But Wirtz, in the best form of his Liverpool career, made it three goals in his last three with a fine strike from distance that clipped in off the post. Then Isak raced through on goal and dinked a shot over Sommer for goal No 10 of the season for him. It completed a memorable night for Iraola and his big-money boys. Now to make it a perfect week at Everton on Sunday.

Sports.title: Trinity Rodman breaks her silence after Ben Shelton split as soccer star posts downcast plane selfie
Sports.content:
Trinity Rodman has said it is 'reset time' in her first public post since her split with tennis star Ben Shelton.

As revealed by the Daily Mail earlier this week, Shelton and the soccer sensation have broken up after almost two years together.

They began dating around March 2025, frequently supporting one another at their various events, but have recently decided to call time on their relationship amid conflicting work schedules and constant travel.

Neither Shelton nor Rodman has addressed the split directly but, on Wednesday, the Washington Spirit star posted an Instagram story from aboard a plane.

'Trusting the process,' she wrote alongside a glum selfie. 'Reset time.'

She and Shelton are believed to remain close, despite their split.

Trinity Rodman has said it is 'reset time' in her first public post since her split with Ben Shelton

As revealed by the Daily Mail this week, Shelton and the soccer sensation have broken up

The sporting couple were frequently forced to maintain their romance over long distance, with the tennis star jetting around the globe on the ATP Tour and Rodman playing in the NWSL and for the USWNT.

Hours after their breakup was confirmed, Rodman was ruled out of the CONCACAF W Championship tournament, which serves as qualifying for next summer's Women's World Cup.

The Spirit star suffered a minor shoulder injury in the opening minutes of the Washington Spirit's loss to the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship game on Saturday.

US coach Emma Hayes replaced Rodman on the 23-player roster for the tournament with forward Jaedyn Shaw, who has made 37 appearances for the national team with 10 goals.

The same night that Rodman, 24, and the Washington Spirit lost the NWSL final, Shelton suffered defeat in the semifinals of the ATP Finals, losing 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7-1) to Carlos Alcaraz in Turin, Italy.

The following evening, the American tennis star was spotted at Madison Square Garden for the New York Knicks' game against the Indiana Pacers without Rodman, instead sitting on Celebrity Row alongside a friend and actress Inde Navarette.

The couple first went public with their relationship in March 2025 following speculation from fans.

Mystery surrounded the early stages of their relationship, as they initially dropped a playful hint as part of a TikTok trend last March before 'hard launching' their romance soon afterwards.

Shelton was spotted at Madison Square Garden for a New York Knicks' game without Rodman

Rodman and the Washington Spirit lost the NWSL Championship to the KC Current on Saturday

The sporting power couple went public with their relationship around March 2025

Rodman was a near-permanent fixture in Shelton's box throughout the US Open in September. The USWNT star and the Spirit had played an NWSL game in Washington on the day of the final but Rodman left the capital almost immediately after the final whistle to make the mad dash to New York for Shelton's final.

The forward was captured crying inside Arthur Ashe Stadium in the wake of her boyfriend's loss to Alexander Zverev.

Rodman, the daughter of NBA legend Dennis Rodman, had cheered on the World No 4 at multiple other events, making her Wimbledon debut in May 2025.

Meanwhile, the tennis superstar was every bit the supportive boyfriend when he consoled Rodman after her team lost the NWSL championship game last November.

Sports.title: Sporting Lisbon 2-2 Man United PLAYER RATINGS: Which star is simply not good enough? Who recovered well from Anfield? And how did Senne Lamnmens rate after horror show?
Sports.content:
Sporting Lisbon 2-2 Man United PLAYER RATINGS: Which star is simply not good enough? Who recovered well from Anfield? And how did Senne Lamnmens rate after horror show?

Manchester United were left to rue two abysmal refereeing decisions that meant they had to settle for a 2-2 draw away to Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League.

A contentious decision in each half saw Amad's goal chalked off for an apparent foul by Youri Tielemans – which he was booked for – and a second saw an own goal chalked off due to interference at a corner from substitute Patrick Dorgu.

Mauricio Pochettino certainly wasn't helped by individual errors from Senne Lammens and Noussair Mazraoui, both playing key roles in Luis Suarez's brace.

But United will head for home knowing they did more than enough to win the game and had it taken away from them.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT ran the rule over Pochettino's side on a night of huge frustration in Lisbon...

Manchester United will head for home knowing they did more than enough to win the game

United were left to rue two abysmal refereeing calls that meant they had to settle for a draw

Senne Lammens – 4

A night that started with an enormous penalty save ended in agony as he had a rush of blood to give a second penalty away and even worse in the second half, dropped what should have been a simple catch to gift Suarez his second. Booked.

Noussair Mazraoui – 4

Simply not good enough. Dreadful defending which left Lammens exposed to concede the second penalty. Did little to stake his claim for minutes at the weekend against Brentford.

Leny Yoro – 7

A sign of how strong his mentality is in that he responded brilliantly after being sent off so early at Anfield. Comfortably looks to be the defender Mauricio Pochettino can rely on the most.

Harry Maguire – 7

A steadying presence at a time when United are crying out for a sense of calm at the back. His insertion into the starting XI coincided with a much more organised and solid approach. No coincidence.

Harry Maguire's leadership is absolutely vital at a time when United are crying out for calm

Lisandro Martinez – 6

Could count himself unlucky to give away a first half penalty for loosely dangling a leg but he redeemed himself by winning one at the other end for United’s first goal. Learning on the job at left back but looks much better than whoever lines up on the right.

Youri Tielemans – 5

Staggeringly he was booked for winning the ball at the end of the first half which saw a valid Amad goal chalked off. Then was deservedly booked in the second, as United had a player sent off AGAIN. Will miss the next game versus RB Leipzig.

Kobbie Mainoo – 6

Proves to be so neat and tidy on the ball without being flash that his contribution can sometimes go unnoticed. Kept it simple and boy do United need more players doing that.

Amad – 7

Talk about rotten luck after putting the ball in the net, ending a goal drought for United stretching back to December 2025, it was erroneously chalked off by dreadful officiating. He’s the busy bee-type player that Pochettino is going to love.

Bruno Fernandes – 8

Does what top players do and puts his team on his back at the most crucial of moments. Coolest head in the stadium to convert the penalty and then the help of a fortunate divot two minutes later allowed him to end a 12-game drought for an open play goal.

Bruno Fernandes put the team on his back with a two-minute brace in the second half

Bryan Mbeumo – 6

Started in a less familiar role off the left before shifting centrally when Zirkzee was withdrawn, Mbeumo didn’t have too many opportunities to shine. Made sure he helped Martinez out defensively.

Joshua Zirkzee – 5

Has a new lease of life since Pochettino’s arrival and looks like he will actually get a fair shot at minutes with a focal point key to what his new head coach wants to do. Needs to cut out the silly flicks on the edge of his own box, though.

HEAD COACH: Mauricio Pochettino – 7

Walks away relieved as much as delighted to have kickstarted his tenure – finally. That being said, Pochettino will be tearing his hair out at the egregious mistakes from match officials again threatening to derail his side.

Sporting Lisbon (3-1-4-2)

Kaique 6; Fresneda 6, Quaresma 5 (Ba 76, 6), Inácio 6; Altimira 6; Catamo 7 (Zalazar 68, 6), Andersen 5, Doumbia 6 (Irankunda 76, 5), Araujo 6; Suarez 7 (Ioannidis 86), Guilherme 5

Goals: Suarez (32 pen, 80)

Booked: Quaresma

Head coach: Paolo Fonseca 6

Sports.title: Usman Khawaja reveals he had security protection from Cricket Australia after receiving racial abuse for sandpapergate claims... as he opens up on feeling 'attacked' by Pat Cummins after 'trying to find middle ground' with skipper
Sports.content:
Usman Khawaja was provided with security protection by Cricket Australia after receiving racial abuse for his claims that the whole team knew about the sandpaper plot in South Africa in 2018.

Khawaja has also revealed he tried to ‘find a middle ground’ with Pat Cummins in a bid to ‘squash’ the sandpaper controversy – only to be taken aback when Cummins launched a personal attack on him during his 68-minute press conference in Sydney.

With the furore showing little sign of dying down, Khawaja – speaking for the first time since Fox Sports stopped using him and David Warner as pundits during Australia’s T20 series against England – spoke of the toll the controversy had taken on his private life.

He told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast: ‘I had the security guy with me for me for three days because of the threats and the racial threatening letters I got at Queensland cricket a couple of days before, and Cricket Australia [were] like “Let’s not take the risk, we don’t know who’s out there, what they want.”

‘I get this stuff on my email, my DMs and stuff all the time now. I definitely get a lot of it, particularly a lot of Islamophobic things that come through.’

Earlier, he spoke to The Grade Cricketer podcast about his attempts to reach a consensus with Cummins: ‘I was hoping he’d be able to find a middle ground that brought everyone in together in this, rather than putting the walls up and creating a bigger division.

Usman Khawaja (above) claimed he sent Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg a proposed statement last weekend following his claims about the ball tampering saga

Khawaja (right) said he felt attacked by Pat Cummins (left) during a press conference where he labelled several of Khawaja's accusations 'complete and utter nonsense'

‘This is what I was trying to say in my text: “If we could meet in the middle, we could really squash this. You don’t have to concede everything. Just meet in the middle and this can be all over.”

‘And I think people would have respected him for that. This is my issue: Pat was 24 at the time. This wasn’t a Patrick Cummins issue. This was the CA [Cricket Australia] win at all costs. Anybody in the team could have stood up and said: “Let’s stop doing this.” No one in the team did.’

Instead, Cummins used his Sydney appearance to call Khawaja’s claim that everyone knew about the sandpaper plot ‘complete and utter nonsense’, and doubled down on the statement he and Australia’s three others frontline bowlers from the 2018 tour of South Africa released five years ago, in which they denied all knowledge of it.

And Khawaja expressed surprise at the personal nature of Cummins’s onslaught, which included the accusation that he had been ‘casual with lives and reputations’ in his explosive autobiography, Sabr.

‘I mentioned Pat two or three times in my book, and they were all singing his praises,’ said Khawaja. ‘I’ve always loved him as a person and a leader. I was never expecting him to attack me personally like he did. He kept going and kept going. I’ve never seen that side of Pat before, and that disappointed me.’

Khawaja also said he had been in touch with CA chief executive Todd Greenberg to suggest a form of words that might help share the blame and bring the matter to a close.

It reads: ‘We accept as a group we were ball tampering by artificially altering the condition of the ball in South Africa in 2018. Whether it was sandpaper or any other means is irrelevant. We knew what we were doing and we take full responsibility as a team and squad for our actions, something we should have done eight years ago.

Cummins' (right) gave a 68-minute press conference denying Khawaja's (left) ball-tampering claims

‘Furthermore, we would like to acknowledge that Steven [Smith], Cameron [Bancroft] and David [Warner] paid an enormous price for the sake of the team, for which we are sorry and eternally grateful.’

Khawaja, who is waiting to hear back from Greenberg, continued to insist that what he wrote in his book is ‘the truth’. He added: ‘I’m not going to hide from it. I can sleep very easily at night. I have told the truth. Cameron Bancroft has told the truth. Chadd Sayers has come out and told the truth.

‘The bowlers then went and put the statement out in 2021, and none of us even knew about it. It just happened. They just did it. It kind of left everyone else with our hands in our pockets. It created this separation. They separated themselves from the rest of the team at that point.

‘I talked to Bancroft about this. I was in touch with him all the way from 2018. He said to me: “That was the loneliest I’ve ever felt in my life.”’

Khawaja said the Australian team, under pressure to get results after losing five Tests in a row in 2016, had been tampering with the ball ‘consistently for a long period of time’.

He added: ‘We were winning games as a team through our tactics with the ball. For me, over such a long period of time, we all knew we were trying to reverse swing the ball and we all know how to reverse swing the ball.

‘That’s the context. You can make up your mind on the rest.’

Sports.title: Furious Premier League refs 'SHOCKED' at Leny Yoro's red card at Liverpool being overturned: Row erupts over Man United star's ban being scrapped… despite key panel voting unanimously that decision was RIGHT
Sports.content:
Furious Premier League refs 'SHOCKED' at Leny Yoro's red card at Liverpool being overturned: Row erupts over Man United star's ban being scrapped… despite key panel voting unanimously that decision was RIGHT

Premier League officials are 'shocked and furious' after the FA overturned Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's red card at Liverpool - despite the competition's own independent panel unanimously backing the dismissal.

Daily Mail Sport understands that the Premier League's Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel has returned a 5-0 verdict in support of referee Sam Barrott's decision to send off Yoro. The panel also backed VAR's decision not to intervene. Their findings will be released next Wednesday.

But an extraordinary row has now erupted, with United celebrating a successful appeal while the Premier League and refereeing body Pro Ref stand by the original decision.

United appealed against the red card following Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Anfield - Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge - and an independent FA regulatory commission, consisting of three former players, rescinded Yoro's one-match ban on Tuesday.

The Frenchman was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he ran clear on goal in the eighth minute. United disputed the referee's view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, having taken a heavy touch.

The FA panel appeared to agree, on the basis Yoro did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity, meaning the Frenchman is free to play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Referee Sam Barrott showed Manchester United defender Leny Yoro a red card vs Liverpool

Yoro was sent off for this foul on Alexander Isak - but his red card was overturned on Tuesday

Barrott and his on-field officiating team from Sunday are believed to be angry at the overturn

However, top-flight officials are now understood to be demanding answers as to how this has happened, with Pro Ref chief Howard Webb backing his referees.

'That (the red card) was the referee's call, made on the field,' said Webb. 'Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect - and formed the opinion it wasn't.

'I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.'

United sources have branded this interpretation as 'totally wrong' and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott's decision.

United dispute that it was a subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

The Premier League and Pro Ref did not comment.

Sports.title: Senne Lammens HOWLER costs Man Utd crucial win as Mauricio Pochettino's concerns remain
Sports.content:
A Senne Lammens' howler cost Mauricio Pochettino his first win as Manchester United boss with Sporting Lisbon securing a late draw after more VAR controversy.

The Belgian made a costly individual error in the latter stages, which allowed the Portuguese side to equalise, after Bruno Fernandes' brace had put the Premier League strugglers in front.

Lammens' night to forget saw him give away a penalty, which was converted by Luis Suarez. His blushes looked to be spared by his teammate as he scored twice in three second-half minutes.

But the United goalkeeper dropped the ball at the feet of the Sporting attacker, who slotted into an empty net. United did look to have scored a late winner, but VAR intervened to rule that the hosts' goalkeeper had been fouled, much to the frustration of Pochettino.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Despite offering little in the opening half hour the hosts were award two penalties in less than two minutes. The first came from a clumsy foul from Lisandro Martinez, albeit the Argentine will argue it was a soft decision. Senne Lammens would spare his blushes, saving from Luis Suarez.

The Sporting forward stepped up minutes later when Lammens went from hero to zero, hauling down Max Araujo. Suarez would not make the same mistake, firing into the bottom corner.

‌



Amad thought he had United level shortly before half-time as he headed home, having seen his initial effort saved onto the bar. However the referee pinged Youri Tielemans for a foul in the build-up, which was another debatable decision.

The Red Devils did equalise three minutes into the second-half with Fernandes, against his former side, converting the third penalty of the evening. The skipper completed the United turnaround his a second goal in three minutes - his long range effort hitting a divot in the pitch and evading a shocked Kaique Pereira.

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes' quick fire double had put Man Utd in front

United looked set to see out the game for a much needed win, but Lammens would gift Sporting a late equaliser. The Belgian only need to take a routine high ball, but dropped it under no pressure at the feet of Suarez, who converted from close range.

‌



Adding insult to injury was VAR's decision to disallow their third of the night before Youri Tielemans was sent-off in stoppage time.

No respite for Poch

Two red cards, a goalkeeping howler and two penalties conceded inside two games of football. Pochettino must be wondering what on earth he's dealing with. We all know the manager takes the fall when things don't go right in this game, but even the best manager in the world would struggle to combat some of the errors United continue to make, especially defensively.

Martinez's swipe in the first-half, no matter how soft, was that of a defender lacking in composure. Lammens - where do you start. Just when you thought he may feed off the confidence that stems from a penalty save, he goes and gives away a spot kick of his own.

The Belgian had almost been caught napping with the ball at his feet early in the game. He was in no mans land when he came flying out from a corner, missing the ball completely. His night got even worse with perhaps his biggest error of the season, dropping a looped ball under no pressure, which cost United the win.

‌



View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino's efforts continued to be undermined by defensive mistakes and red cards

Pochettino made four changes from the team who were well beaten at Liverpool, but he'll quickly be realising that the misfortune that exists in this United squad is impacting every player. The ex-Tottenham boss is the latest boss to try and turn this troubled club around. He's barely had a minute on the training pitch with the squad, and it seems he can't even rely on his team to be solid, secure and smart.

VAR kills United hopes - again

Go back to Sunday and Leny Yoro's red card effectively killed United's hopes inside ten minutes and allowed Liverpool to run riot. The biggest frustration for Pochettino will be the FA's decision to overturn it.

Had they had 11 men, who knows how things may have turned out. Well VAR was again not on the side of the Argentine, who saw his side's late winner ruled out for a foul on the goalkeeper.

‌



Martinez was the man pinned as he leapt in front of Pereira, who would punch the ball into his own net. He was quick to run towards the referee and plead for a foul.

It didn't take long for VAR to pop up on the screen and, in Europe especially, that can often spell danger. United were left to digest another decision that had a huge bearing on the result. Pochettino will think the world is against him.

Sports.title: Saffie Osborne detained in hospital overnight after taken ill in Hong Kong parade ring
Sports.content:
Saffie Osborne detained in hospital overnight after taken ill in Hong Kong parade ring

The top British jockey gave up her other commitment after two rides at Happy Valley on Wednesday when she required medical assistance

View 2 Images Saffie Osborne: taken to hospital after feeling unwell (Image: Maureen McLean/Shutterstock)

Saffie Osborne was detained in hospital overnight after she was taken ill in the Hong Kong parade ring on Wednesday.

‌



‌



The 24-year-old history-making rider is in the middle of a short-term contract in Hong Kong where she has been riding since November 8. She has ridden in 38 races and ridden three seconds but has yet to visit the winners’ enclosure during her stay, which is due to last up to December 23.

‌



At Wednesday’s meeting at Happy Valley, Osborne completed her first two rides on Prince Alex and Romantic Fantasy, who finished eighth and last respectively. But she was taken ill in the parade ring as she prepared to ride in race seven. She was replaced by Harry Bentley on Call Me Success who finished fifth.

‌



Aidan O’Brien has four chances to break Group 1 world record in Japan and Hong Kong READ MORE :

According to the Hong Kong Standard , she was seen sitting up on a stretcher with her hand covering her face and then taken to the racecourse medical room for evaluation. A racecourse doctor checked her over and recommended her transportation by ambulance to Union Hospital for overnight observation.

A Hong Kong Jockey Club official told the Standard, “She’ll go to Union Hospital and stay overnight for observation.”

‌



On Sunday at Sha Tin, Osborne was thrown off her mount as she went out onto the track but the pair were reunited to take part in the races and she was able to complete all her rides.

View 2 Images Saffie Osborne with the Betfred St Leger trophy (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

‌



A club official said: “She never complained about having banged her head on Sunday, but she hurt her neck, twisted, and she got stood on. She had an MRI on Monday, so she was checked then for Sunday’s incident, and she’ll have further tests at the hospital to check that she’s A-ok.”

A Hong Kong Jockey Club statement said Osborne had felt unwell on Wednesday and had been taken to hospital. She had remained conscious throughout.

Article continues below

In September this year she became the first female to ride the winner of a British Classic when partnering Highwayman to victory in the St Leger. It was the biggest of a series of landmarks for Osborne who in 2024 became the first woman to ride a winner at Meydan in Dubai in 2024, followed by big race success in Qatar.

Sports.title: Blame Beyonce, NFL, AJ and Spurs - why Saudi-backed Newcastle need even more cash
Sports.content:
News that PIF, Newcastle United's majority shareholders, are looking to sell up to 25 per cent of the club through the issuing of new shares will naturally ring alarm bells with the club's supporters.

After all, from the moment the Saudi Public Investment Fund completed its takeover of the club, alongside the Reuben family and Amanda Staveley, their long-term commitment to the Newcastle United project has been questioned - certainly from the outside.

That has been accentuated this year with Newcastle's results on the pitch regressing and prompting accusations of the Newcastle project stagnating, as well as PIF's decision to pull the plug on funding for the LIV Golf tour.

Indeed, just this month, Chronicle Live reported on comments made by Professor Simon Chadwick, an expert in Afro-Eurasian sport, questioned their long term ambitions for the Magpies.

‌



"Newcastle United fans don't like me, because I posted this before and they've told me - I fail to see what coherence and investment in Newcastle United has with wider Saudi Arabian sporting strategy.

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

"What is clear and what we've all got to learn from what has happened over the last year, two years, is if the Saudi Arabians think, well, you know, we're not making any money out of this, it's too disruptive, it's impacting upon perceptions of us, they will withdraw."

But PIF governor, and Newcastle United chairman, Yasir Al-Rumayyan's presence at the annual Matfen Hall summit provided some reassurance that they remain fully invested in the project. PIF chief Jacobo Solis has been a consistent presence around the club since - both in La Manga in the summer and at the training ground last month - and that was backed up by Al-Rumayyan's appearance at St James' Park.

‌



And it is St James' Park, or more namely, the decision over whether to remain there or move to a new stadium, where this decision for PIF to sell shares in the club centres on, rather than their interest dwindling, clarifies Chronicle Live.

Instead, a reduction in their holding of the club isn't an admission that the club is for sale or they have lost ambition, rather a statement of ambition as they look towards fresh investment to accelerate that key stadium decision.

Sources close to the club say that a minority investor is being sought to help fund some of their major infrastructure projects. Chronicle Live understands that the club are attempting to create liquidity to invest and the issuing of new shares is deemed one way of funding it, although that is just one potential option.

View 3 Images Yasir Al-Rumayyan, Chairman of Newcastle United, at a game (Image: Getty)

‌



The decision to sell up to 25 per cent of the club through the issuing of shares will not see any money paid to PIF, who currently own around 84 per cent of the club. The money would be injected straight into the club and in exchange for providing that cash, any new investor would receive a stake in the club.

It is no secret PIF have been looking for investors to help finance the stadium project and it has never been the expectation they would entirely finance the redevelopment of St James' Park or build a state of the art new stadium at Leazes Park, which would cost more than £1.3billion.

Fresh investment would help finance that project which would allow the club to make a tangible step in reducing the commercial revenue gap between themselves and the 'big six'.

It was earlier this year that football finance expert Kieran Maguire told Chronicle Live that the only way Newcastle can realistically bridge that gap is by building a new stadium that increases their commercial revenue streams.

‌



After Sandro Tonali swapped Newcastle for Tottenham in July, Maguire said: "Blame Beyonce and Coldplay," Maguire joked. "Blame NFL, Anthony Joshua. That's the reason why (Spurs can spend over £200million already this summer despite narrowly avoiding relegation last season).

"Newcastle United, are £100million behind Arsenal, they're £100million behind Manchester United, they're £70million behind Spurs, they're £60million behind Liverpool, when it comes to ticket sales.

"So, St James' Park, again, as an away fan, everybody loves a trip to Newcastle. It's in the centre of town, everybody's so friendly, it's a proper footballing city. All of these positives don't turn into cash for the club.

View 3 Images Newcastle are considering building a new stadium adjacent to St James' Park (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



"Spurs are very good at what they do. And what they are very good at doing is being an entertainment complex. That's how I'd describe them. Whereas Newcastle United is a football club.

"Tottenham made, on average, £83 per fan per seat and that compares to Newcastle at £49 according to the 2024/25 figures. Spurs also have 30 non-football events a year at full capacity.

"As a result of that, their commercial income has gone through the roof. They made £277million from commercial income. That compares to £123million Newcastle netted. So there's £140 million [gap]. You've got £70million more in matchday income. You put those two together, and that's £200million."

"Tottenham made, on average, £83 per fan per seat and that compares to Newcastle at £49 according to the 2024/25 figures. Spurs also have 30 non-football events a year at full capacity.

‌



"As a result of that, their commercial income has gone through the roof. They made £277million from commercial income. That compares to £123million Newcastle netted. So there's £140 million [gap]. You've got £70million more in matchday income. You put those two together, and that's £200million."

And now that PIF's desire to sell those shares is in the public domain and JP Morgan have been appointed as advisors and the process to find that investment is under way, it suggests progress on the stadium decision will be accelerated. And that is the key conclusion to draw from this decision, which should put a pin in any doubts over the owners' long term commitment to the club.

Sports.title: Wesley Fofana accidentally exposed the rotten culture problem at Chelsea - they must sack him
Sports.content:
Wesley Fofana accidentally exposed the rotten culture problem at Chelsea - they must sack him

OPINION: Chelsea must be ruthless and sack Wesley Fofana - because his mentality is poison for a young, fragile dressing room

View 3 Images Wesley Fofana epitomises everything that's wrong with Chelsea in 2026 (Image: Getty Images)

There's no shame whatsoever in hating your job and staying put strictly for the money. In fact, it's practically the load-bearing wall of the British economy.

‌



‌



Every weekday morning, millions of us drag ourselves onto damp commuter trains, stare blankly at spreadsheets, nod thoughtfully on Teams calls, and quietly pray for Friday afternoon.

‌



Premier League football, however, is supposed to be different. When you're living out a fantasy the majority of us would kill for, giving a toss isn't optional. And even if you are a stone-cold mercenary, could you at least have the decency to, you know, pretend not to be?

‌



Enter Wesley Fofana, who seems to be trying his darnedest to become Chelsea's most regrettable transfer blunder of all time - which, given the depth of competition at Stamford Bridge, is really saying something.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Raheem Sterling avoids jail after crashing his Lamborghini while inhaling laughing gas READ MORE :

Alejandro Garnacho takes Aston Villa action with Chelsea transfer now in the balance READ MORE :

In an interview that must have had the club's communications department reaching for the gin before noon, the 25-year-old defender confessed that during Enzo Maresca's reign - having already endured cruciate ligament and meniscus nightmares, followed by two consecutive hamstring strains - he genuinely decided to pack it all in. "That's it, I'm retiring, I'm done playing," he recalled thinking. "I was serious."

‌



Fair enough. Elite sport is brutal, and watching your own legs repeatedly betray you would break even the toughest of characters. So Fofana summoned his agents for a crisis meeting. And here, dear reader, is where the tragedy veers sharply into farce.

Rather than rallying their client with stirring speeches about glory, silverware, or the proud traditions of Stamford Bridge, Fofana's representatives reached straight for the calculator.

‌



"They started analysing the situation with me, talking about contracts and all that," Fofana recounted cheerfully. "'It's simple, you still have several years left on your contract, and there's a lot of money to be made. Even if you really decide to stop playing, you still have to come every day, keep smiling, and even if you're injured, you have to honour your contract for your future.'"

View 3 Images Fofana's interview took place unbeknownst to Chelsea (Image: Zack Nani / Youtube)

‌



You have to admire the sheer, brass-necked clarity of it. Come in every day. Keep smiling. Cash the cheques. It's the corporate philosophy of 'quiet quitting,' except instead of nicking highlighter pens from the stationery cupboard, the Frenchman is pocketing £220,000 every single week... until 2029.

Indeed, Fofana's deal is a magnificent archaeological relic from the wild, giddy summer of 2022, just before BlueCo's spreadsheet-wielding overlords pivoted to heavily incentivised, performance-related contracts. He's the last dinosaur stomping happily around a freshly landscaped theme park, munching on the most expensive foliage while everyone else has to earn their supper.

‌



The problem isn't that he wants his money. The problem is that he has just announced, in glorious high definition, that he is emotionally clocked out - and he seems to find the whole thing rather amusing.

Consider, for example, another gem from the same chat, in which Fofana laughed off a missed penalty against Liverpool last month, and declared that he "couldn't care less" about it. Stop and savour that for a second. Missing a decisive spot-kick against one of Chelsea's most bitterly loathed rivals, and the response is a shrug and a giggle. It's one thing to be privately disillusioned with your body and your profession - it's quite another to broadcast to a paying fanbase that you are essentially rinsing the club while treating its biggest fixtures like a kickabout in the park.

‌



And that is why Fofana has become something much more troubling than an unfortunate, injury-ravaged signing. He has become the rotten core at the centre of Chelsea's great, gleaming, scatter-brained malaise.

View 3 Images Chelsea must be ruthless when it comes to 'poisonous' players like Fofana (Image: Eddie Keogh/Getty Images)

‌



Cast your mind back to 2023, when Frank Lampard returned for his brief, haunted spell as interim manager and looked like a man who had just wandered into an abandoned fair ground. Lampard warned, as politely as his blood pressure allowed, that the atmosphere at Chelsea was broken - that standards had evaporated, that too many players simply weren't pulling their weight or caring enough about whether the club actually won anything. Three years on, those words read less like a failed caretaker's sour grapes and more like a medical diagnosis.

Watch Chelsea today and you see a team that is perpetually on the verge of a nervous breakdown: flimsy, inconsistent, allergic to resilience, and liable to fold like a cheap deckchair at the first hint of adversity. Then compare it to the concrete-and-barbed-wire Chelsea of the Roman Abramovich and Jose Mourinho years. Can you imagine John Terry, Didier Drogba, or Lampard himself giggling about a miss against Liverpool? Can you imagine what Terry would have done if a team-mate had breezed into the dressing room announcing he was only there because his agent told him to keep picking up his pay packet? There would have been a small, localised weather event in the boot room.

‌



Those teams were built on lions - men who treated second place like a personal bereavement, let alone fourth, sixth, or 10th. You cannot build that kind of ruthless, suffocating winning culture when one of your highest-paid senior figures is openly treating the club like a very generous pension fund.

At this point, whether you think Fofana is a Rolls-Royce defender trapped in a porcelain body or a walking defensive liability is entirely beside the point. His mentality is contagious, and in a young, fragile dressing room desperate for leadership, it's pure poison.

‌



Chelsea need to stop being polite and start being ruthless. If nobody will take him off their hands, buy out his contract, hand him his golden parachute, and wish him a long, smiling retirement somewhere far away from west London.

Cutting Wesley Fofana loose won't magically cure everything that ails this club overnight. But you cannot rebuild a fortress while someone is sitting in the middle of the courtyard laughing at the cracks in the walls.

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres sends clear message to Mikel Arteta over Arsenal future
Sports.content:
Viktor Gyokeres has insisted he is fully committed to Arsenal - and warned they will take their goal frustrations out on someone.

Incredibly, Arsenal have won eight games by a one goal margin this season which has helped them go six points clear at the top of the Premier League. But it seems that the familiar 1-0 to the Arsenal scoreline is no longer enough because they have been pegged back in their last two games and been wasteful with their finishing.

Arsenal had a staggering 30 shots against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League but only four were on target and they were held to a draw by the Bundesliga leaders.

Gyokeres says that sooner rather than later there will be a goal rush - and it could be against Manchester City on Sunday. They were also pegged back after going in front in their previous game at Newcastle.

‌



Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

The Gunners striker said: “Yeah, in one way it is a bit frustrating after a game when we don’t win, of course. But, overall, I think the way we attacked - and the amount of chances we have created - it is just a matter of time until there are going to be a lot of goals.

“We always go into games wanting to win. I think, overall, we have done really well this season. Obviously, we have drawn two games that we could have won, with the amount of chances that we had in both games.

“But Sunday is another game and we are going to prepare for that one, and we are going to go for it.

‌



“I have been feeling good in the last couple of games. Obviously, we should have probably won against Dortmund with the amount of chances. But overall, I think we played really well and that was good, at least.”

Gyokeres has started just one Premier League game this season but there was a reminder of his quality with his wonder strike against Borussia Dortmund. Despite limited opportunities, the Arsenal striker insists he is not thinking about January or the club being linked to other forwards and the impact that could have on him.

Instead, Gyokeres insisted he is happy and will seize his chance when it comes.

View 2 Images Gyokeres was on the scoresheet against Borussia Dortmund

‌



"For me, I always focus on the games,” he said. “I want to do well when I get a chance to play. That is my main goal. I really enjoy being here and playing here. That’s always my aim.

“When I get to play, I just try to do my best and that is going to be the case going forward as well. I prepare myself and I am ready.”

Gyokeres says Arsenal are determined to win back-to-back titles with Mikel Arteta’s men six points clear at the top of the Premier League.

That would show how strong they are but they have been struggling to put games to bed after throwing away leads in their last two games against Dortmund and Newcastle.

‌



Gyokeres added: “Of course, we always want to win titles and we know how tough it is in the Premier League with the games and the teams.

“It is always going to be tough. But we have an amazing squad, amazing players, so that’s the aim. We push each other every day to achieve that and we are definitely going to go for it.”

Sports.title: Tyson Fury says money can't make him happy despite million pound bank balance
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury says money can't make him happy despite million pound bank balance

Tyson Fury gave an interview ahead of the release of his Netflix documentary and his fight with Anthony Joshua

View 2 Images Tyson Fury will be back in the ring next month earning even more money. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Honest Tyson Fury says he demanded his management make him more money for his big fights - but the multi-million pound bank balance hasn’t made him any happier in life.

‌



‌



The boxer, 38, will face Anthony Joshua in the ring on December 11 in one of the biggest fights in British boxing history. But reflecting on his multi-million pound wealth from his many big fights, Tyson said: "All of it. It's all useless. All your achievements, all your goals, all your money, all your fame, it's all a load of rubbish, and time's fleeting. That's the most important thing. I sit here today with hundreds of millions in me bank, achieved everything there is to achieve in boxing, won every belt, can go, do, buy anything I want.

‌



“I don't want anything. I don't wanna go anywhere. I live in the Isle of Man, dressed like a tramp. What was it all for? Wasting me youth. I look back at it now, I think, well, what would I have done differently? Nothing. What would I have chose instead of boxing? Probably nothing. And if I would've been successful at anything else, then I probably would be in the same boat.

‌



“We take for granted what the most important things are, and I've been away for most of the most important things in my life, which is me wife and kids and family. Trying to work to get something that doesn't really matter. But if you've got 50 pence on you or you've got 10 million, you can only do the same things as anybody else anyway.”

View 2 Images Tyson with wife Paris and their family. (Image: Instagram/parisfury1)

Appearing on the Louis Theroux podcast, Tyson explained he had told his management for his 2018 comeback he wanted financial security over winning titles.

‌



Tyson explained he told them: “I wanna make as much money as possible for me and my family.

”I've had all the belts and had no money. Now I want all the money and no belts.”

‌



He added: “That was always the plan, to make as much money as possible on the second journey.

“First journey I had 27 fights unbeaten, never really made any money. Couple of million quid here and there. Paid me tax on it, you're left with f*** all anyway.

‌



“Got me brains knocked out for no reason really. No, no real financial gain. Life didn't change at all.”

As well as fighting Anthony Joshua in the coming weeks in Cardiff, boxer Tyson has his own documentary coming out on Netflix on Friday.

‌



In it, he speaks about achieving his life goal at the end of 2015 beating Vladimir Klitschko and becoming heavyweight champion of the world. But the following two years then became a nightmare that saw his mental health spiral out of control.

He was later diagnosed him with mild schizophrenia, depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder and got back into boxing in 2018.

‌



His wife Paris Fury told the Sunday Mirror at the weekend she believes he is “addicted to boxing” and enjoys the routine of training camps which help him keep his life on track.

She also said she thought he was likely to continue to box in 2027 even though he does not need the money. The Sunday Times rich list said Tyson was worth around £162 million in 2026.
