Sports.title: Featured Comment: Herta deserves credit for trying to make the switch from IndyCar | Brief
Sports.content:
Colton Herta’s bold attempt to make the leap from IndyCar to Formula 1 – via Formula 2 – appears to be over with yesterday’s news he won’t return to the feeder series this year.

It was always a risk, one I’m glad he took and sorry it didn’t work out. I’ve loved the cross overs when they’ve happened.

I loved it when Jacques Villeneuve turned up with his day-glo helmet, gangsta rap overalls and bleached hair. Juan Pablo Montoya ‘effing and jeffing’ and going out of his way to not show Michael Schumacher any respect. Nigel Mansell just being in Milwaukee, let alone winning. Alex Zanardi leaving and winning in that beautiful Target-liveried Reynard then coming back and doing nothing with Williams. Sebastian Bourdais being a winner and also very much not a winner…

It’s a risk, and one that seldom pays off on both sides of the Atlantic. Though Hill, Clark, Fittipaldi, Andretti prove it’s possible, and I guess Villeneuve also if we ignore Sauber, Renault and most of what he says.

It didn’t work for Colton, but he wanted to make the jump and I hope this doesn’t dissuade others from giving it a go in the future. You never know unless you try and most drivers end up not succeeding somewhere in their career, it may as well be because of a leap into the unknown.

@Bernasaurus

Sports.title: British Fans Rip Weak Fury vs. Joshua Undercard Lineup
Sports.content:
Turki Alalshikh revealed the full card for the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua event on December 11 at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, and the fan reaction has been negative, particularly among Brits.

With the Fury vs. Joshua fight being billed as the biggest domestic heavyweight bout in years in the main event, fans are hopping mad that the undercard looks like it’s been thrown together without any care about quality.

Fans are finally realizing they’re basically paying for the Fury vs. Joshua fight and getting nothing else worth watching.

Virtually all the undercard bouts, including the co-feature pitting Deontay Wilder vs. Martin Bakole, have been bashed as pure 100% garbage. Fans who subscribed to Netflix just to see the event aren’t happy about it. I’m not surprised.

We saw the same thing with Floyd Mayweather Jr. vs. Manny Pacquiao and Canelo Alvarez vs. Terence Crawford. All the effort and dough went into the main events for those two mega-events, and man, did the undercards look like junk of the highest kind.

Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn got one of his fighters, former two-time super featherweight champion Joe Cordina, onto the card. The kicker is that Cordina, 35, has been placed on the preliminary portion of the card, fighting Mauricio Lara, out of sight, out of mind.

If Hearn thought this was Cordina’s big chance to win back the fans he lost when he was knocked out by Anthony Cacace in the eighth round in May 2024, he can forget it.

“What about Joe Cordina?” Hearn said when discussing the lineup. “What about a two-time world champion from Wales? Absolutely mental.”

Hearn had been banging the drum about wanting Cordina to fight on the main card against Manny Pacquiao, WBO lightweight champion Abdullah Mason, or Sam Noakes. Instead of fighting one of them in a highly visible fight, Cordina will be hidden away on the prelim card that will be shown on Netflix, TikTok, and The Ring social channels.

Hearn has got to be hopping mad, seeing his fighter fail to make the grade for the main card. I can totally understand the organizers’ decision to place the Cordina vs. Lara fight on the prelim card. Neither of these two fighters has beaten anyone halfway decent since losing. Cordina beat a fringe contender in Gabriel Flores Jr. and a lower-level fighter in Jaret Gonzalez Quiroz since losing to Cacace.

As for Lara, he’s won his last five fights against obscure opposition in confidence builders after fighting to a draw against Daniel Lugo in February 2024 and losing to Leigh Wood by a 12-round unanimous decision in May 2023.

The main card is just as abysmal, with Deontay Wilder facing replacement opponent Martin Bakole in the chief support bout after Jai Opetaia’s injury pullout, Zuffa heavyweight Da’Mazion Vanhouter battling Michael Essomba, and Moses Jolly fighting Igor Adiel Macedo.

Hearn blasted Zuffa promoter Dana White and Zuffa’s influence for the poor undercard, and British fans are replying in droves to Turki’s undercard lineup, echoing Hearn’s thoughts. The people who paid good cash for tickets to see the event live in Cardiff are harping about the scarcity of UK fighters, the 1:30 a.m. local start time for the headliner, and the lack of quality fights beyond the Joshua vs. Fury fight.

The rest of the preliminary lineup is filled with obscure prospects and names that even hardcore boxing fans won’t recognize, aside from Tyson’s younger brother Roman Fury. If you’re tuning in on December 11, you don’t need to set your alarm until right before the main event.

Sports.title: WBA Sets 75-25 Split for Teofimo Lopez Against Jack Catterall
Sports.content:
It’s not looking good for Teofimo Lopez to dodge his mandatory obligations at welterweight. Today, the WBA called a purse bid for December 4 in Cypress, Texas, for a fight between WBA welterweight Super Champion Teofimo and Jack Catterall with a slanted 75/25 purse split.

Financially, that should make Teofimo happy. Even with three-quarters of the money guaranteed, he’s shown no eagerness to sign to fight the mandatory he inherited after his win over WBA champion Rolando ‘Rolly’ Romero by majority decision on August 22. Lopez needs a special permit from the WBA to avoid Catterall (33-2, 14 KOs), but he may not get his wish. It’s understandable why Teofimo doesn’t want to fight Catterall. It’s a style that he’s struggled with, and it’s unlikely he would win.

Teofimo (23-2, 13 KOs) wants to face WBC welterweight champion Ryan Garcia in what would be a lucrative unification, where even if he loses, he’d still do well financially. He needs the WBA title for purse negotiations more so than it being a valuable chip to create more interest in a fight with Ryan.

Teofimo’s title isn’t why fans are interested in seeing the fight. For him, it’s just a negotiation tool to get a better deal, because he lacks Ryan’s popularity to get an even split. Even with a title, you can argue that Teofimo doesn’t rate a 50/50 purse split.

Catterall Risk Explains Lopez Delay

If this were an easy mark, Lopez would be overjoyed at receiving a 75/25 gift split from the WBA. Catterall’s style is similar to Shakur Stevenson’s, which left Teofimo baffled and helpless in a unanimous decision loss over 12 rounds earlier this year at Madison Square Garden on January 31. Teofimo looked embarrassingly bad in that fight. The judges scored it 119 to 109 on all three cards, and he was outlanded 165 to 72.

Defensively, Catterall isn’t as sharp as Shakur, but he’s close enough to be the same kind of nightmare for Teofimo. On offense, Catterall is superior to Shakur, and coupled with his defensive ability, he would be a difficult problem for Teofimo to try and figure out. Besides all that, the pressure that Teofimo would be under would be severe if he needs to defeat Catterall to get to the lucrative payday fight against Ryan Garcia.

If he gets beaten by Catterall, he can forget about fighting Ryan for the time being. Unlike his loss to Shakur, Teofimo wouldn’t be given a straight title shot immediately after. He’d have to rebuild and get in line, which is what he should have had to do after losing to Stevenson instead of being given a crack at Rolly’s WBA title.

Catterall captured his WBA regular welterweight title by beating former mandatory Shakhram Giyasov by a wide 12-round unanimous decision last May. Giyasov was the mandatory challenger that Rolly was avoiding. Now, we’re seeing the new WBA champion Teofimo trying to give Catterall similar treatment. The WBA can stop this cycle by rejecting Teofimo’s request for a special permit.

It’s easy to predict what Lopez’s next move will be if the WBA rejects his appeal. Vacating the WBA belt will be the easiest way of getting Catterall out of his path to a fight with Ryan. Teofimo will still get a nice payday against Ryan, but probably not as nice as it would be if he still had his WBA title.

Sports.title: Brian Mendoza Replaces Keith Thurman in Weak Vergil Ortiz Jr. Co-Feature
Sports.content:
PBC and Golden Boy Promotions made it official today with Brian Mendoza replacing Keith Thurman as Vergil Ortiz Jr.’s opponent for his 10-round co-feature middleweight bout on December 5 at the Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona.

Ortiz Jr. and Mendoza will be fighting on the undercard of WBA and WBO cruiserweight champion David Benavidez’s unification bout against WBC champion Michal Cieslak on DAZN PPV and Prime Video.

The addition of Mendoza (23-5, 17 KOs) has received mixed views from fans. Many of them view the 32-year-old as a poor replacement, given his 1-3 record in his last four fights. That’s not exactly top shelf unless losing is the benchmark requirement used to get enlisted as a fill-in opponent for Vergil Ortiz Jr.

Back in Mediocrity Since Fundora

What Mendoza has got going for him is that he knocked out Sebastian Fundora in the seventh round in April 2023 in a huge upset at the time. Fundora was beating the living daylights out of Mendoza for the first six rounds until he got careless in the seventh and got clipped. Since then, Mendoza’s career has slipped back to what it was before that win. That was his textbook Cinderella night, where he got lucky in a fight that he was getting beaten up in.

What’s interesting is that fans online see this as an upgrade over 38-year-old Thurman, just because of his win over Fundora. If you look at Mendoza’s results since that upset, he’s a major downgrade, and that’s saying a lot because Thurman was not a great opponent. He’s not a middleweight, and definitely not young.

Tim Tszyu beat Mendoza by a wide 12-round unanimous decision in October 2023. That fight was an example of Mendoza being brought back down to earth. It wasn’t even slightly a close fight. It looked like Mendoza wandered into the ring from the crowd, and Tszyu took advantage by beating the stuffing out of him. Serhii Bohachuk did the same thing to Mendoza in a clash for the interim WBC junior middleweight title in March 2024.

The only win for Mendoza in the last three years came against journeyman Jesus Antonio Rojas (12-11-2, 10 KOs). It took that level of opponent for Mendoza to snap his two-fight losing streak. In Mendoza’s last fight, he returned to his losing ways, getting trounced by Yoenis Tellez by a one-sided 10-round unanimous decision in March 2026.

Basically, what we’re seeing here is not a dangerous threat being used as a replacement opponent for Ortiz Jr. (24-0, 22 KOs), who recently looked like pure gold in wins over Israil Madrimov, Bohachuk, and Erickson Lubin.

A Cheap Showcase for Ortiz Jr.

Yanking Mendoza out of his fight with Eric Priest enabled Sampson Boxing, TGB Promotions, and Golden Boy Promotions to save money on finding a quality opponent. It’s a showcase fight for Ortiz Jr. Ideally, they should have spent some money to enlist a quality middleweight contender like Yoenli Hernandez to put Ortiz Jr. in a sink-or-swim fight.

What Mendoza does have going for him is a strong chin, as he’s never been knocked out in his career. So if the idea is for Ortiz Jr. to get some rounds in to sharpen up after a year on the shelf, Mendoza is the guy for the job. However, the referee may step in and halt this fight anyway because of the likely one-sided nature of it.

Entertainment-wise, Mendoza eating hard shots from Ortiz Jr. is not fun to watch in a PPV co-feature slot. Fans want competitive fights, not slaughters.

Ortiz Jr. is 28 years old, making the move up to middleweight, and has still accomplished little in his career. It’s got to bug him that he sees fighters like Jaron ‘Boots’ Ennis taking the express route to superstardom, leaving him behind. The difference is, Ennis has been a risk-taker from day one, hasn’t feasted on weak opposition, and has stayed active. In contrast, Ortiz Jr. hasn’t fought the best, and he’s missed a lot of time in his career due to health and promotional issues.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder Gets Worst Possible Replacement In Martin Bakole
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder is facing the worst possible replacement opponent for him in his December 11th fight in Cardiff against the heavy-handed Martin Bakole. It’s not the type of opponent that the 41-year-old Wilder’s legs can deal with at this stage of his career.

Boxing analyst Sergio Mora pointed out this week that Wilder no longer has the mobility at his age to avoid being walked down by a big puncher like Bakole. He feels that Wilder will have problems keeping Bakole off of him and will be forced to slug it out right off the bat from round 1 on December 11th.

“If you don’t fight him off the right way, he’s going to mow you down. And you got to have legs to do that,” said Mora on Chris Mannix’s podcast.

Wilder never really had great leg movement. If you look at his earliest fights against Harold Sconiers and Bermane Stiverne, he wasn’t a mover. He was winning by unleashing his right hand on them. Back then, before the two later shoulder surgeries on that side, Wilder’s right hand was lethal. It made up for his lack of mobility and boxing skills.

After his originally scheduled opponent, Jai Opetaia, dropped out due to a hand injury, the former WBC heavyweight champion Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs) wanted a rematch with Derek Chisora or a fight with Jarrell Miller. Neither was selected, which is good news for fans. Both are long in the tooth and don’t have the kind of power that could erase Wilder the way Bakole can.

For what Wilder is aiming for, a world title shot in his next fight, he should have to fight and beat the likes of Bakole to get his wish. It would look pathetic if Wilder is given a title shot after beating an old war horse like Chisora a second time or getting past Miller.

Why Bakole Is A Dangerous Gamble

Despite Bakole being held to a draw against Efe Ajagba in his last outing, and knocked out in the second round by Joseph Parker in a short-notice fight in 2025, Bakole still has power in both hands. He’s dangerous up close when he lands cleanly.

In those two fights, Bakole wasn’t in the best shape in terms of his weight. For this one, he’d been training to fight Solomon Adebayo on the December 11th undercard. Being in shape for this fight means Bakole will be a constant threat to Wilder in the early rounds.

If Wilder’s right hand is back to full strength, he could stop Bakole. However, Wilder hasn’t shown his once-devastating power since 2022, when he knocked out Robert Helenius in the 1st round. Mora and Mannix agreed that Jarrell Miller would have been the better choice to sell the matchup without carrying the same threat as Bakole. The organizers made the right choice because the card needed a high-drama matchup. We don’t see that in the main event or any of the undercard fights.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Picks Safe Money Fights Over Young Sharks
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) is already looking past his December 11 clash against Anthony Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) at a 1:30 AM UK start in Cardiff to map out his final two retirement fights. The early morning start time for the Joshua fight is to satisfy American viewers on Netflix, and it’s obviously not ideal for the aging 38-year-old Fury.

Staying up late will be hard on his body and could lead to another off performance, as we saw in his two defeats against Oleksandr Usyk. The last thing Fury needs is to look slow and lose to Joshua, setting a bad start to his three-fight retirement plan.

Today, the Cardiff Council’s licensing sub-committee granted a special variation, extending the stadium’s operating hours until 3:00 AM. This move made it possible for the Fury vs. Joshua fight to begin at 1:30 AM local time in Cardiff.

Also today, Fury revealed his schedule on OOOSCH TV, saying he will fight only two more times after Joshua. He wants a rematch with Joshua if the first fight is competitive, followed by a trilogy bout against Oleksandr Usyk.

“I’m interested in fighting Anthony Joshua, maybe rematch him if it’s a good fight, and then maybe [have] a trilogy with Oleksandr Usyk if it makes sense and if I get a fair shake,” Fury told OOOSCH TV. “There’s nobody else, really, that I’m interested in fighting.”

It’s not a coincidence that the two fighters Fury plans on facing to end his career, Joshua and Usyk, are the biggest money heavyweights in the division. Even if Fury loses to both, he’ll be paid far better than if he were to face another top contender, like Filip Hrgovic, Daniel Dubois, or Agit Kabayel.

Ideally, it would be better for the sport if Fury faced one of those heavyweights or Moses Itauma to serve as a springboard to make a star out of one of the younger contenders or champions. Fighters in the past were willing to do that, yet we see it less and less in an era where fighters are more protective, selfish, careful, and money-focused. As such, you see Fury aiming for 37-year-old Joshua and 39-year-old Usyk for his final two fights instead of the young guns, Dubois and Itauma.

Fury Overlooks His Recent Form

What we saw of Joshua and Fury in recent fights was lackluster performances, showing that both fighters are long in the tooth ahead of their December 11 fight. Those outings may be one reason why there is so little interest in their clash next month. They both looked so feeble that fans can’t get excited about a fight between two faded heavyweights.

To make it interesting for fans, it would have been more appealing to see Fury and Joshua walk the plank against one of the big four: Itauma, Dubois, Kabayel, or Hrgovic. Fans would tune in just to see how the older heavyweights hold up. Putting them in together is not appealing in the least, because there’s no real gain for the winner in a battle of shot fighters. It only gets interesting if you throw Joshua and Fury in the ring with one of those ravenous sharks to see how they fare.

Fury looked terrible stopping 46-year-old Mariusz Wach in seven rounds in Thailand on July 24. One day later in Jeddah, the 37-year-old Joshua was surprisingly dropped by what was supposed to be a soft opponent, Kristian Prenga, before coming back to stop him in the second round.

That fight was very strange, as Prenga didn’t throw any punches in the second round after having Joshua on the verge of being halted as the first round ended. Why not go for the kill? I’ve never seen anything like it, and Joshua got lucky. If Prenga had thrown anything, he likely would have finished Joshua at the beginning of the second round.

Interestingly, the December 11 fight contract doesn’t include a rematch clause for their vacant WBA heavyweight title. That leaves it up to Turki Alalshikh and Netflix to decide whether they wish to finance a second fight between Joshua and Fury. It would be perfectly understandable if they pass. If both look poor or if the card bombs in bringing in subscribers to Netflix, I don’t see why they would want to pay for a second fight.

That goes for putting the winner or the loser in with Usyk. A fight between Fury or Joshua and Usyk would be expensive and wouldn’t produce the numbers or entertainment needed to make it worthwhile. Putting them in with Itauma and watching the timer to see how long they last would be far more fun to watch.

Usyk already beat Fury twice in 2024, and he’s talking about moving down to cruiserweight to fight champion David Benavidez instead of waiting for Fury. You can respect that.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder Claims Martin Bakole Win Earns Title Shot
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder believes a victory over his replacement opponent, Martin Bakole, on December 11 in Cardiff will pave the way to a world heavyweight title shot. As wacky as this sounds, it wouldn’t be a shock if it actually happens. The division is starved for recognizable names, and if nothing else, the 41-year-old Wilder is well known.

Turki Alalshikh confirmed that Bakole (21-2-1, 16 KOs) would replace the injured Jai Opetaia as Wilder’s opponent for their co-feature fight on the undercard of Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua at Principality Stadium.

Bakole is a decent opponent for Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs), but hardly the type of contender that would erase six years of repeated losses. Definitely not good enough to vault Wilder into a world title fight.

“We’re going to be fighting Martin Bakole. He is next, and then after that it’s going to be crazy,” said Wilder in a social media video. “Once I beat him, I’m not going to move forward with the information I’ve received, but once I beat him, you’re looking at the new heavyweight champion of the world. And the new two-time heavyweight champion. Martin, here we come. I appreciate you for accepting the opportunity. Let’s give the fans and the people something to talk about for the rest of their lives.”

Instead of Wilder hoping for a shot at one of the other heavyweight champions, he should be campaigning for the winner of the Fury vs. Joshua WBA title fight. That’s the bigger payday by far.

If Joshua and Wilder both come out victorious, promoters can finally make their long-awaited fight, as long as Fury doesn’t push for an immediate rematch.

How The Title Path Works

Deontay has been beltless since Fury knocked him out in February 2020. Beating 42-year-old Derek Chisora by a 12-round split decision in April and stopping little-known Tyrrell Anthony Herndon in June 2025 in his last two fights aren’t enough to overcome being stopped in five rounds by Zhilei Zhang and beaten by Joseph Parker by a 12-round decision.

Still, Wilder’s commercial leverage gives him an edge over more deserving contenders in the division who have been grinding hard and winning fights. His long 18-year pro career has given him plenty of opportunities to be seen by fans, and that should help when it comes to being picked by one of the current champions.

It’s still asking a lot of Wilder to defeat Bakole. If Bakole comes in near 300 lbs, his punching power could still take out Wilder if he lasts long enough to land something. Wilder’s advantage is that Bakole hasn’t looked good since beating Jared Anderson in 2024. If the ‘Bronze Bomber’ doesn’t take Bakole out early, he can forget about his dream of fighting for a world title.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Threatens to Smack Rayo Valenzuela in Leaked DMs After Walking Away From Zuffa
Sports.content:
Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela posted a screenshot of an Instagram message exchange between him and Shakur Stevenson on Tuesday, showing the bitterness on Rayo’s part after Shakur left Zuffa without accepting an offer to fight him.

Rayo (16-3, 10 KOs) had hoped to fight Shakur (25-0, 11 KOs) while they were briefly teammates, but Shakur rejected Zuffa’s offer.

Posting the exchange on X, Valenzuela captioned the image, “Saying everything but ‘let’s fight!'”

Valenzuela’s post comes after he was interviewed by Ring Magazine and called Shakur “weak” for leaving Zuffa Boxing instead of being a team player and agreeing to fight him in an in-house contest. Stevenson signed with Zuffa on July 9th of this year, but the two mutually parted ways three months later in October, with Stevenson failing to fight once while signed.

The comments from Valenzuela clearly bothered Shakur, causing him to slide into Valenzuela’s DMs.

“Say bh ass n* watch how loose you is with yo words, All that calling me a p*y st watch that.. Ion play them type of games,” said Shakur.

“Shut yo ass up and fight!” said Valenzuela.

“U a b*h, That’s why u clout chasing. I thought u was more solid then that, But look u using them disrespectful ass words stand on that st when u run into me!!” said Stevenson.

“You a b***h and ain’t nobody scared of you. We can fight next and settle it!” said Valenzuela.

“Just know I will smack the holy st out of u if u keep disrespecting me,” said Stevenson.

“I used to look at you and be like I’d beat tf outta dude!” said Valenzuela.

The interaction shows the bad blood between Rayo and Shakur from the brief period when they were both with Zuffa Boxing. It was a logical fight to make, but Shakur was aiming higher, wanting a bigger money fight. Being dismissed as inadequate has likely gotten on Valenzuela’s nerves because this is a fight that could have easily happened. Stevenson turned it down.

Stevenson would have been better off if he had taken it because he’s just been sitting inactive. At least he would have gotten the opportunity to be seen by fans while showing he’s a team player by fighting one of Zuffa’s fighters. Turki Alalshikh owns 60% of Zuffa, and it would have worked well for Stevenson’s career to fight one of his fighters instead of wasting time trying to get a fight with Devin Haney (31-0, 15 KOs) while insisting on a weight handicap.

In Valenzuela’s interview with Ring Magazine, he was critical of Shakur for trying to get a catchweight against Haney and Raymond Muratalla (24-0, 17 KOs), viewing that behavior as showing weakness.

Shakur is now a free agent and has a purse bid scheduled for November 30th for his mandatory defense against Muratalla. No one has signed Stevenson, and it may not be worth it if he’s going to price himself out and waste time trying to get weight advantages for fights.

Valenzuela is still with Zuffa Boxing and is in negotiations for a fight against WBA lightweight champion Floyd Schofield (19-0, 13 KOs). The two have a December 11th deadline before a purse bid is called.

If Stevenson wanted to smack Valenzuela, he had the perfect chance to do that when he was signed with Zuffa. They wanted the fight, but he turned it down and left the company.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Has Earned His Shot at Usyk
Sports.content:
Oleksandr Usyk is still the best heavyweight in the world, and Agit Kabayel is the man I’d most like to see him fight next. Usyk has already beaten Tyson Fury, Anthony Joshua, and Daniel Dubois twice apiece. Kabayel brings a different test. He does his best work to the body, and he’s stopped heavyweights who were supposed to make him pay for coming forward.

Kabayel makes his first defense of the WBC title against Nelson Hysa on Saturday in Düsseldorf. He was elevated after Usyk vacated the belt in June, but the wins that make his case came before the promotion. Kabayel stopped Frank Sanchez and Zhilei Zhang, then took out Damian Knyba in three rounds in January. Sanchez has since knocked out unbeaten Richard Torrez Jr. in two rounds, a result that makes Kabayel’s win over him look even better.

What Kabayel would ask of Usyk

Kabayel went downstairs against Frank Sanchez and Zhilei Zhang and stopped them both. Against Usyk, I’d watch what he does after the first body shot. Can he stay close enough to land a second, or does Usyk turn him and make him walk in all over again? I’d pick Usyk, but that’s the exchange I’d want to see in the eighth or ninth round, when Kabayel has had time to slow him down.

Dubois has had the best year of the other champions. He got up twice in May to stop Fabio Wardley in the 11th and take the WBO belt, then finished the rematch in two rounds in October. There’s a better fight for him in a rematch with IBF champion Filip Hrgovic, whom he stopped on cuts in 2024. Hrgovic has since stopped Moses Itauma in nine rounds to win his title. He entered the ring after Dubois beat Wardley and asked him about fighting in March. That rematch would put two belts on the line and give Hrgovic a chance to answer for his only defeat.

Fury and Joshua will get more attention in Cardiff on December 11 than any of those fights. British fans have waited years to see them settle it, and the winner will have a big win to sell. Usyk has already fought both men over 24 rounds each. Kabayel has spent the past two years earning the opportunity to show what he can do with twelve.

Ghana News.title: Heritage series: BoG must explain selection of personalities on new cedi notes – Walewale MP
Ghana News.content:
The Minority in Parliament is demanding full disclosure of the cost and decision-making process behind the Bank of Ghana’s (BoG) newly introduced heritage series banknotes, insisting that taxpayers deserve answers about the exercise.

The Member of Parliament for Walewale, Dr Tiah Abdul Kabiru Mahama, said the central bank must account for the expenditure, explain how the personalities featured on the new notes were selected and clarify the circumstances surrounding changes to the original design.

He said the issues raised about the currency upgrade could only be resolved through transparency and a comprehensive explanation from the BoG.

Speaking on Joy FM’s PM Express on Wednesday, November 25, Dr Mahama said the Minority wanted the circumstances surrounding the redesign examined to establish whether the cost was justified by the work undertaken.

He identified the amount spent on the exercise as one of the critical issues requiring clarification, arguing that the project was funded with public resources.

“We ought to know the cost because it is being paid for by the taxpayers’ money,” he said.

The MP also questioned the circumstances under which a personality initially expected to feature on the notes was reportedly replaced by another person, whom he identified as her sister.

He said the BoG needed to explain how that decision was reached and whether the appropriate consultations had been conducted before the final designs were settled.

Dr Mahama said the controversy was not about opposing the recognition of the individuals featured on the new currency but about ensuring that the process was fair, inclusive and reflective of Ghana’s history.

He maintained that several other Ghanaians had made significant contributions to the development of modern Ghana and deserved recognition for their sacrifices.

According to him, the individuals whose images appeared on the new notes deserved the honour, but the selection process should not create the impression that other deserving contributors had been overlooked.

He said the people of Ghana were entitled to know the principles and considerations that informed the choice of personalities, particularly given the historical significance of national currency.

“Every single person in that particular currency, in the new currency, deserves a place,” he said, while questioning whether the decision-making process had adequately considered other contributors to the country's development.

Dr Mahama said convincing explanations from the central bank could help address public concerns and bring the controversy to a close.

He stressed that the Minority wanted the matter subjected to scrutiny so that questions about the expenditure, consultation and selection of personalities could be answered satisfactorily.

The controversy follows the unveiling of the Heritage Series by President John Dramani Mahama on November 12, 2026. The redesigned notes feature eight prominent Ghanaians, including Dr Kwame Nkrumah, former United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan, Justice Annie Jiagge, Dr Ephraim Amu and Mrs Theodosia Salome Okoh.

Questions have particularly centred on the GH¢50 note bearing the portrait of Mrs Okoh, the designer of Ghana’s national flag, after concerns were raised that the image resembled her sister, Dr Letitia Obeng.

The Bank of Ghana subsequently clarified that the portrait was developed from different photographs of Mrs Okoh and not from a photograph of her sister. It attributed the perceived resemblance to artistic adjustments made to meet the technical and security requirements of banknote production.

The new notes, which have enhanced security features and are printed on reinforced cotton paper, are scheduled to enter circulation on December 1, 2026, alongside the existing banknotes.

Ghana News.title: BoG failed to adequately consult Parliament on new cedi notes — Tiah Mahama
Ghana News.content:
The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has been criticised for failing to adequately engage Parliament in the process leading to the introduction of the new heritage series cedi banknotes.

The Member of Parliament for Walewale, Dr Tiah Abdul Kabiru Mahama, said although the central bank had indicated that consultations on the currency redesign had been ongoing for two years, lawmakers were not sufficiently involved in the discussions.

He said the limited engagement with Parliament was a major shortcoming in an exercise involving the country's national currency, which represents its sovereignty and heritage.

Speaking on Joy FM's PM Express on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, Dr Mahama argued that the Bank of Ghana should have made a greater effort to involve MPs, given their responsibility to represent their constituents and help educate the public on national policy decisions.

“I think that members of Parliament have not been brought along in terms of the cost and even the consultation,” he said.

He acknowledged that the BoG had explained that it had undertaken consultations over the past two years before settling on the new notes but, questioned why elected representatives had not been sufficiently involved.

“For me, the takeaway from this whole exercise is that the people's representatives were not fully immersed in this consultation,” he said.

Dr Mahama said engaging Parliament would have provided an effective channel for reaching citizens across the country, since MPs could convey information to their constituents and help explain the rationale for the changes.

He also stressed that decisions concerning the national currency should be approached without partisan considerations, given their importance to the country's identity and economic sovereignty.

“Anything to ensure the sanctity of our currency, anything to ensure that our currency in fact has all the security features of international repute, or our currency is able to stand the test of time and durability - our currency marks our sovereignty and heritage,” he said.

The MP, who is also a member of Parliament's Finance Committee, said he only gained a better understanding of the currency redesign after an opportunity to discuss the matter with officials of the Bank of Ghana on the sidelines of an IMF meeting.

He maintained that the committee established to oversee the exercise could have done more to engage Parliament.

Under Parliament's revised committee arrangements, operational matters relating to the Bank of Ghana fall under the Economy and Development Committee, while the Finance Committee retains responsibility for matters concerning the central bank's budget and appropriation.

Dr Mahama distinguished the new currency redesign from the routine printing of banknotes to replace worn-out notes and maintain adequate currency in circulation.

He said the central bank had traditionally briefed Parliament on the recurring costs associated with currency replacement, usually through its budget or expenditure reports.

However, he considered the introduction of the new heritage series a more extensive exercise that required broader engagement with lawmakers.

The Bank of Ghana has introduced the heritage series as part of efforts to reflect Ghana's history and identity through its national currency. The redesign has generated public discussion, including questions about its cost, consultation process and the reasons for the changes.

Ghana News.title: Mahama donates GH¢600,000 towards funeral of Agogomanhene
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has contributed GH¢600,000 towards the funeral of the late Agogomanhene, Nana Kwame Akuoko Sarpong, in recognition of the traditional ruler's long service to the Agogo traditional area and the country.

The donation was announced by the Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr Frank Amoakohene, who represented the President at the funeral observances in Agogo on Wednesday, November 25, 2026.

Dr Amoakohene said the President had initially donated GH¢500,000 on Tuesday, November 24, before adding another GH¢100,000 the following day, bringing his total contribution to GH¢600,000.

He conveyed the President's condolences to the bereaved family and the people of Agogo, while paying tribute to the late chief's contributions to national development.

President Mahama also joined traditional rulers, family members and other mourners on the second day of the three-day Dɔte Yie observance to honour the memory of the late traditional leader.

The lying-in-state, which began on Tuesday, has drawn mourners from different walks of life, including chiefs, religious leaders, public officials and members of the public, to pay their final respects.

Nana Akuoko Sarpong, who ascended the Agogo stool in 1975, died on March 26, 2026, bringing to a close a 51-year reign marked by both traditional leadership and public service.

His contribution to national life extended beyond the traditional council. During the Provisional National Defence Council (PNDC) era, he held several government positions, including Secretary for Health, Secretary for Internal Affairs and Secretary for Chieftaincy Affairs.

He later served on the Council of State under the late President John Evans Atta Mills and was also associated with the formation of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

The funeral observances are scheduled to end on Thursday, November 26, 2026, in Agogo in the Ashanti Region.

Ghana News.title: BoG needs no parliamentary approval to upgrade currency – Dr Atuahene
Ghana News.content:
Dr Richmond Atuahene, Banking Consultant

Banking consultant Dr Richmond Atuahene has dismissed suggestions that the Bank of Ghana (BoG) requires parliamentary approval to upgrade the country’s currency.

He maintains that currency upgrades fall within the central bank's operational mandate and should not be confused with redenomination, which requires a different approval process.

His comments follow the controversy surrounding the Bank of Ghana’s Heritage Series banknotes, amid concerns over errors on some notes and questions about the level of consultation before their introduction.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Wednesday, Dr Atuahene argued that the debate over parliamentary approval was misplaced.

Drawing on his experience as a member of the team involved in Ghana’s previous currency redenomination exercise, he explained that the two processes have different requirements.

“Everything had to go to parliament, and it had to be approved. But when there is a currency upgrade, you don't go there.”

Dr Atuahene explained that the central bank’s budget captures expenditure on currency upgrades and submits it to its board.

He said the cost of introducing the Heritage Series should appear in the Bank of Ghana’s 2026 financial report, allowing scrutiny.

“If you get to the 2026 financial report, you will see the cost in it, and that has been the practice.”

The banking consultant maintained that the lack of prior parliamentary approval does not exempt the central bank from accountability.

He explained that Parliament can scrutinise the expenditure after the central bank’s audited accounts are published.

“It is when the thing has been published, and the accounts are audited, and the budget made provision for it, so you can track it there.

“And that is why they come to Parliament to tell you what they did that year.”

Dr Atuahene also challenged critics to examine previous currency upgrades to see whether parliamentary approval was required.

“And let them check the records,” he said.

While defending the central bank’s authority to undertake currency upgrades, Dr Atuahene expressed concern about the controversy over the Heritage Series errors.

He described the situation and the ensuing public debate as worrying, distinguishing between the central bank’s authority to upgrade the currency and concerns about how the exercise was carried out.

Ghana News.title: Frustration reigns for Pochettino in chaotic start to Man Utd job
Ghana News.content:
Two games, no wins. Two red cards, two goals scored. One goal disallowed, six conceded. Is it possible for Mauricio Pochettino to have learned anything from a crazy first week as Manchester United boss?

United and Pochettino went on the warpath before the Champions League encounter with Sporting, furious at Leny Yoro's dismissal at Liverpool which they believe was unjust and shaped the eventual 4-0 defeat.

Club officials were seething after the 2-2 draw in Lisbon as well.

This time it was 2022 World Cup final referee Szymon Marciniak in the firing line. Blowing before Amad's first-half header went into the net meant VAR had no chance to assess whether the Polish official was right to rule Youri Tielemans had fouled Goncalo Inacio before prodding the ball through to the Ivorian.

Former United winger Ashley Young didn't think so. He called Marciniak's performance "a disgrace".

That Tielemans picked up a booking that eventually led to his late red card – the Old Trafford outfit have now had four players sent off in their past five games, meaning the Belgian will miss the Old Trafford clash with RB Leipzig on 8 December - just compounded the situation.

Then, in a matter of minutes, Marciniak decided neither Manchester United keeper Senne Lammens nor Sporting counterpart Kaique had been fouled as they conceded. Their respective defences complained bitterly. Marciniak was only asked to go to the pitchside monitor by VAR for the latter incident, which he overturned.

United insiders felt the Tielemans incident was clearly not a foul and Amad's goal should have stood. They also felt any foul on Kaique by Patrick Dorgu was marginal and did not warrant their goal being disallowed.

Pochettino trod a fine path, knowing if he said something too controversial, it could land him with a fine.

A nod of a head in agreement was his initial reaction in his post-match news conference, when asked if he felt Marciniak had got it wrong.

A few minutes before, he was more expansive when he spoke to TNT.

"It's difficult to find a game where you get punished [so much] in one game," he said. "We were punished a lot in key actions."

Pochettino searching for first Man Utd win

Not for the first time this season, United controlled extended periods of a game they ended up not winning.

The goals they conceded at the Jose Alvalade were bizarre.

Seventy-five seconds after superbly saving one penalty, goalkeeper Lammens suffered a rush of blood and conceded another, which was scored.

Lammens was at fault for the second, when he dropped the ball into the path of Sporting striker Luis Suarez, who scored with an overhead kick.

"I think we dominated and we deserved to win the game, but we didn't for different circumstances," he said.

"All the teams make mistakes, but for these mistakes the punishment (for us) is too big in every single mistake. Many other clubs make mistakes or tilt in a different circumstance, in a more positive way. But that is in the way we are. We need to take responsibility."

United are still to win away from home in any competition this season. They have now won once in their last 13 matches. In the Champions League, they are 19th, two points in front of Roma, who are just below the top 24, which guarantees passage to the next phase.

Pochettino defends Lammens over error

Young said Lammens may be one mistake from being dropped.

The Belgian's performance was not good and errors are beginning to mount.

It is not what Pochettino needs right now. United showed faith in the Belgium international this summer by bringing in 36-year-old Karl Darlow as his understudy.

Darlow did end last season as first choice at Leeds but started just 30 league games in his three seasons with the Elland Road club. Tom Heaton, 40, who was also on the bench against Sporting, has not played in a senior game since February 2023.

Could Pochettino contemplate leaving Lammens out.

"This type of thing happens," he said. "That is football. Football is about making mistakes.

"I always want to support my player. I think we need to talk about responsibility. In this type of action our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult.

"It's not to blame the defensive line, but it's two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on. We need to manage his type of situation better."

Image caption,Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens (left) and head coach Mauricio Pochettino applaud the away fans after the 2-2 draw at Sporting

It has been a whirlwind week for Pochettino, who last Wednesday morning UK time was still United States boss.

There have been a few blows to absorb, and lessons are having to be learned quickly.

But despite the clear frustrations, the 54-year-old is glad he accepted the challenge.

"I am happy to be here," he said. "I'm so excited to be the face representing this club.

"We are here because the situation wasn't the situation all the fans and people expect. We are here to take the responsibility from one week, and we are going to improve for sure.

"It's going to be tough, of course. Nothing is easy. But we have the energy and I think we have the capacity, and, most important, we have the players and the power and the energy from our fans, which is massive."

Ghana News.title: Gordon scores twice as Barca ease past Sabah
Ghana News.content:
Anthony Gordon scored twice as Barcelona cruised to a Champions League victory over Sabah in Azerbaijan.

The England winger opened the scoring just past the half hour with a tap-in after Sabah goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov pushed Karim Adeyemi's cross into his path.

Gordon doubled the visitors' lead early in the second half, again finding himself in the right place to pounce after Gabriel Jesus' shot was saved.

Barcelona kicked on and put the game to bed as Adeyemi slid in to convert Alejandro Balde's teasing low cross before Jesus bundled the ball in from a corner.

Having conceded three goals in nine minutes, Sabah responded well and pulled one back through Joy-Lance Mickels' cool finish after Christian Nwachukwu's good work.

It was no more than the hosts deserved having caused Barcelona problems prior to Gordon's opener, with Ivan Lepinjica's sliced effort looping up and over visiting keeper Joan Garcia, only to bounce back off the bar.

But, even without the injured Rodri and Lamine Yamal, and with top-scorer Raphinha among those rested from the start, Barcelona's superior quality told and the three points were never really in doubt.

A fourth victory in five European games keeps Barca firmly in the top eight and on course for automatic qualification for the last 16, while Sabah's fourth loss in the competition leaves them 32nd of the 36 teams.

Ghana News.title: ‘All coming together’ – Isak repaying Liverpool faith
Ghana News.content:
Alexander Isak is set to leave Newcastle United after three years at the club

Liverpool fans have needed to be patient to see the best of Alexander Isak after an injury-hit start to his career, but the striker is now proving the wait has been worth it.

By scoring twice against Club Brugge in the Champions League, Isak took his tally for the season to 10 - more than double his total for his first season at the Reds.

Of course, that campaign was disrupted; he had no pre-season because of his protracted £125m move from Newcastle and then suffered a broken leg in December.

But Isak is now on a hot streak, having scored four goals in his last four games for Liverpool.

Asked whether fans were now seeing his full capabilities, Isak told TNT Sports: "It is always difficult to say exactly where you are and how good you are but I can definitely say I feel good, I am in a good place and the team is in a good place which is the most important thing.

"Hopefully it just gets better."

Isak joins Liverpool greats as scoring run continues

When Isak scored his opener against Club Brugge, it marked a sixth consecutive away game in which he has struck.

That meant he joined an exclusive club of just eight players to have achieved that feat, following in the footsteps of Dick Forshaw, Sam English, Gordon Hodgson, John Evans, John Aldridge, John Barnes and Mohamed Salah.

Isak has now scored the joint-most away goals across all competitions this season (eight – level with Erling Haaland).

His total is also already more than any Liverpool player managed away from home in the 2025-26 campaign (six by Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk) and it is only November.

Isak looks to be brimming with confidence, exemplified by his second goal as he latched on to a pass from Alisson to go through one-on-one and then chipped a confident finish past the goalkeeper.

But for Andoni Iraola, Isak's performance offered much more than goals, and the Liverpool manager also praised the striker's overall contribution.

"He is in a great moment right now," he said.

"In the first half especially he helped us with the link up. In the second half, it was more about defending a little lower."

Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock agreed that Isak had shown he has more to his game than the goals.

"There were a lot of questions about Isak last year, about his price tag and what Liverpool paid for him," he said.

"There were a lot of people saying he doesn't take people on, but now he looks fitter and looks sharper and we are starting to see the quick, nimble feet again that we saw at Newcastle, with his nice touches and link-up play.

"So we are starting to see a different side of him. My big question in this system would be - can he press? Can he close down, can he affect the game in the other way that Iraola likes to do? Now we are starting to see that.

"All of it is coming together, which is great for him."

Isak and Wirtz get best out of each other

It is not just Isak who is looking the part in the Liverpool attack.

Florian Wirtz continued his impressive run of form with a goal that means he now has eight goal contributions in his last five games for Liverpool and Germany.

"Both are now in a good place," Iraola said of Wirtz and Isak.

"When the team overall is playing well and we are getting good results everything looks a little better.

"The important part if they help the team to play well and get results. Alex and Florian right now are in a good moment."

But the Liverpool attack as a whole is looking dangerous, regardless of who plays along with Isak and Wirtz.

In Wednesday's 3-0 win, it was Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola who completed the front four, while in Sunday's 4-0 defeat of Manchester United it was Rio Ngumoha who played in Munoz's position.

"We have so many good players in our team," Wirtz told TNT Sports.

"Even when we can substitute some wingers, midfielders or strikers in the 60th minute or later it gives us a lot.

"It shows how good our team is and it is important for a top team to have a strong bench."

Liverpool's win against Club Brugge was their seventh from their last 10 games across all competitions.

"I spoke to Wirtz at the weekend, after the [Manchester] United game, and we were talking about his form - and he said 'well it helps that the team are playing well'," Warnock added.

"It's true because if you try to influence a bad team or a team that's not playing well, then it is much harder.

"With a fitter Isak, Wirtz looks a better player because now he is playing balls in behind that Isak is getting to, and getting in on goal on the back of.

"It has a knock-on effect, which is obviously like Wirtz said, he is playing in a team which is better equipped to suit him."

Ghana News.title: US$10bn and the audit trail: Ghana’s New Economy needs auditors from the start, not the end
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s 2027 Budget promises to assess every New Economy project for value for money and report spending commitments transparently. The first test of that promise comes when a payment is due: what evidence should the officer authorising it have in hand?

The 2027 Budget sets out a US$10 billion programme for 2027 to 2030, covering eight priorities from commercial agriculture to energy, pharmaceuticals and technology. The government says support will be “transparent, time-bound and linked to verified results”. To keep that promise, the agencies running the programme need to decide early what counts as proof, who checks it and what happens when the evidence falls short.

1. How do we know it was made in Ghana?

A public tender that favours locally made uniforms can help Ghanaian manufacturers win orders and expand production. But a supplier can be registered in Ghana and still import the finished uniforms. A business registration certificate cannot tell a procurement officer where they were made.

The tender should spell out what qualifies as locally made and what suppliers must show to claim the preference. Procurement officers can check production records, visit selected suppliers and compare prices across eligible bids. That gives local manufacturers a fair chance and helps the government judge whether it is getting value for money.

2. What earns the next payment?

An advance can help a contractor buy materials and get workers on site. It can also leave the public exposed if work stalls. The Auditor-General’s report on the District Assemblies Common Fund found that the fund’s administrator had paid GH¢10.7 million in advances across 13 contracts. At the time of the audit, work had not begun on any of the 13 projects, and the guarantees covering the advance payments had expired.

The agency should verify the guarantee before releasing an advance and track its expiry while work is under way. Later payments should depend on evidence that the contractor has reached the agreed milestone. If the contract says payment is due when a facility is ready to operate, the officer authorising payment should have a test or inspection report showing that it works.

3. What counts as a job created?

The government’s New Economy programme document projects about 20,000 direct and indirect jobs under its pharmaceutical and biomanufacturing pillar. To judge whether the programme delivers on that promise, Ghanaians need to know which jobs are counted and how those numbers are verified. A worker hired to build a production line and a worker hired to run it both earn wages, but only the second job is expected to continue once construction ends.

The programme should report temporary and ongoing direct jobs separately and say how long workers remained employed. Payroll and social security records can help verify direct jobs where those records are available. Indirect jobs should be reported as estimates, with an explanation of how they were calculated. The public can see the totals without seeing workers’ personal records.

Let the public follow the money

The Ministry of Finance should publish a quarterly register showing, for each project, how much was approved, how much the government committed and paid, who received the money, what was delivered and who verified it. If a milestone is missed, the register should say who is responsible for the next step and when it is due. Using existing procurement and financial records would give Parliament and the public one place to follow projects across agencies.

The agencies running the programme should set the conditions for payment, check that they have been met and answer for their decisions. Internal auditors should assess those controls before spending begins and test whether officials follow them once work is under way. The Auditor-General can independently examine the programme and report findings to Parliament. Keeping those roles distinct allows auditors to challenge spending decisions without having made those decisions themselves.

A local manufacturer should be able to see who won a public contract and how much it was worth. A farmer should be able to check whether an irrigation project is on schedule. And when the government reports job numbers, Ghanaians should be able to distinguish verified direct jobs from estimates of indirect employment. That is why the audit trail must begin with the first contract and the first payment.

The Finance Minister has asked Ghanaians to choose production. Let us also choose proof.

About the Authors

David Anopong Mintah is a PhD student in Accounting at the Rawls College of Business, Texas Tech University. He is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants, Ghana (ICAG) and the Chartered Institute of Taxation, Ghana (CITG), and previously worked as an auditor at Deloitte. World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Anthropic CEO Amodei denies wanting humanity to ‘surrender’ free will to AI
World.content:
Dario Amodei’s remarks come amid predictions that AI may soon match or surpass human intelligence.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has denied believing that humanity should “surrender” control to artificial intelligence amid predictions that models potentially far exceeding human intelligence are imminent.

In a lengthy post on X on Wednesday, Amodei said he does not support surrendering “human free will” to AI and has long argued that the frontier technology should be subject to “legitimate democratic processes”.

“If I thought any of this was a good idea, I would be advocating for it in public, just as I have not been afraid to advocate for many, many unpopular views over the last few years,” Amodei said, responding to an Axios report about a purported “consensus” inside Anthropic that some decision-making authority should be passed to the technology.

“But I am not advocating for it, because I think turning over governance to AI is a terrible idea.”

Amodei’s remarks come amid a flurry of commentary by top industry executives suggesting that AI will soon match or surpass human intelligence.

The prospect of AI that equals or outperforms the best human minds – referred to as artificial general intelligence (AGI) and artificial super-intelligence (ASI), respectively – has fuelled intense debate in Silicon Valley and beyond about whether such technology can be harnessed for good without exposing humanity to catastrophic harm.

AI safety advocates have raised fears that models being developed by firms such as Anthropic, which made history last week in the biggest initial public offering of all time, could slip out of human control, particularly once systems start improving without human input, a process known as recursive self-improvement.



In his X post, Amodei criticised commentary he said conflated the idea of AI taking over specific tasks with surrendering control in a “grand sense of global governance”.

“This is not AI ‘running the world’, but AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing software end-to-end,” Amodei said.

“Here, my view is mixed. AI doing more complete or larger tasks is economically valuable and can drive important advances in software, medicine, transportation, energy, etc.”

“It is clearly desirable in many cases and will save a lot of lives,” he added. “But it has downsides as well, and in some areas it may not be worth it.”

Citing unnamed sources, Axios reported on Wednesday that Amodei and other Anthropic executives believe it would be irrational “or even unethical” not to hand over authority to AI for tasks it can do better than humans, such as curing diseases.

‘We’re getting close now’

David Krueger, the founder of Evitable, a nonprofit that campaigns against the development of ASI, said Anthropic should pause its work if Amodei is genuinely concerned about humanity losing control of frontier models.

“We don’t have to consciously surrender control to AI to lose it. As AI becomes increasingly capable, there will be mounting pressure to push humans out of decision-making roles across society,” Krueger told Al Jazeera.

“Meanwhile, researchers at Dario’s own company are warning that AI capabilities are advancing faster than our ability to control them. We need an immediate, indefinite, international moratorium on frontier AI development.”

While there is no universally agreed-upon definition of AGI or ASI, key tech industry figures have over the past week suggested that the milestones are near.

Google DeepMind’s chief AGI scientist and cofounder, Shane Legg, said on Wednesday he believes there is a more than 50 percent chance that “minimal” AGI arrives before 2028.

“We’re getting close now,” Legg said on X.

On Sunday, Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, said ASI is “arriving”, pointing to the announcement that an Anthropic employee had used Claude to solve the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most difficult problems in mathematics.

“How humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence on what future world we live in,” Wang said on X.
