World.title: Kim Jong Un says North Korea should widen deployment of tactical nukes
World.content:
Kim warns attempts to deny North Korea’s nuclear status will be seen as “an open declaration of war”.

Share Kim Jong Un says North Korea should widen deployment of tactical nukes on social media

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has urged his country to focus on deploying tactical nuclear weapons “across multiple domains for different missions”.

Kim said North Korea’s nuclear material production capacity was being systematically expanded on Thursday, according to state media KCNA.

Maintaining North Korea’s status as a nuclear-weapons state was “absolutely inviolable”, Kim said during an inspection of nuclear material production and weapons research facilities. KCNA did not identify the facilities or their locations.

The country’s status would not change because of what he called “denuclearisation rhetoric from forces that ignore objective reality and failed to recognise the changed situation”.

“Our nuclear capability is now a reality,” he said, calling recent achievements in nuclear weapons production a major success in carrying ⁠⁠out the country’s nuclear policy.

Any attempt to deny North Korea’s nuclear status, which it enshrined in its constitution in 2023, would be regarded as “an open declaration of war”, he said.

Kim said diversified use of tactical nuclear weapons was an “important and urgent task raised from tactical nukes’ military value in modern warfare and from the inevitable reality facing the border with the most dangerous enemy state”.

DMZ tensions

Kim’s statements come during a growing border dispute with South Korea over a landmine explosion that injured three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), a heavily fortified territory between the two countries, on September 21.



Seoul demanded an apology from Pyongyang in October after a joint South Korea-United Nations investigation found that North Korea had planted the landmines more than a year ago.

Pyongyang sent a letter to the UN Security Council in response, accusing Seoul of fabricating the explosion, and fired about 10 short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast into the Sea of Japan less than a week later.

South Korea estimates that North Korea possesses between 80 and 120 nuclear warheads.

World.title: Photos: Storms and an El Nino-charged king tide batter California’s coast
World.content:
California and other parts of the United States West Coast have experienced record-high water levels, causing flooding, destruction and dangerous waves.

On Wednesday, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) announced that the fishing community of Charleston, Oregon, notched its highest-ever coastal water level, roughly 1.12 metres above the mean high water level.

It was as high as 3.4 metres above the mean low water mark.

Other NOAA stations recorded some of their highest water levels on record, including San Diego, Los Angeles and Santa Barbara, all on the southern California coast.

Further north, the L-shaped municipal pier in Pacifica, a city south of San Francisco, crumbled into the surf after a wave as tall as its platform crashed into it.

In a video on social media, bystanders could be heard voicing astonishment at the sight. “Oh my god, it’s gone. Oh my god,” one person said.

The pier had faced multiple closures in recent years, as seawater weakened its concrete structure, but experts say this week’s conditions were more dangerous than normal.

The high coastal water levels were spurred by a combination of factors, including a phenomenon popularly known as king tides.

The term is applied to the highest tides of the year, created when both the sun and the moon are aligned to create a larger-than-normal tidal bulge, pulling the water with their combined gravitational force.

The king tides have been exacerbated by the El Nino weather pattern as well as human-fuelled climate change.



While El Nino is a regular occurrence, this year’s edition is projected to be stronger than normal, according to forecasters, leading to record-warm waters off the Pacific coast. That warming, in turn, helps churn up powerful storms that contribute to waves battering the shoreline.

San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie announced on Wednesday that his city had made it through the worst of this week’s surge with flooding and waves up to 9 metres, but he warned of more king tides to come.

“The last two weeks have been an important reminder to get prepared for the rest of El Nino season. We’re expecting more king tides in December and January,” he wrote on social media. “We need to take these events seriously, prepare ahead of future storms, and stay alert.”

World.title: Ukraine attacks Russian military base, says five planes struck
World.content:
The Ukrainian General Staff says its forces struck an airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region east of Moscow.

Ukrainian forces have hit a major Russian military base east of Moscow, damaging five aircraft used to launch missiles and bombs, according to the Ukrainian General Staff.

Ukraine struck the Savasleyka airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region, the General Staff said on Wednesday, adding that three MiG-31 jets were used to fire hypersonic missiles and two Su-34 fighter-bombers were damaged.

Russia did not immediately comment on the report by the General Staff, which said the Savasleyka airbase had been hit in the latest long-range attacks aimed at crippling Moscow’s war effort.

The operation followed a series of high-profile strikes by Ukrainian forces in recent days in which two Russian ships were hit in Libyan waters and a Russian vessel was struck in the Gulf of Finland.

Last week, Ukraine destroyed the road portion of Russia’s prized bridge to the Crimea peninsula after consecutive attacks.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and fighting has continued despite a renewed US-backed push to end what has become Europe’s worst conflict since World War II.

Kyiv is trying to dent Moscow’s military might as it struggles under a renewed campaign of attacks on its energy system and mounting Russian strikes on front-line cities.

Ukrainian forces are hunting Russian ballistic-missile launchers used to carry out many of those attacks, striking 16 over the past several months, Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said this week.

Renewed Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian oil refineries’ processing volumes by 45 percent since late October, industry sources said this month. Kyiv has said it will stop striking Russian energy targets only when Moscow does the same.

World.title: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
World.content:
The US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs as President Donald Trump pushes ahead with his signature trade policy.

The new taxes charged on imports to America are set to hit many of the country's biggest trading partners - China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions, including Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.

The White House began investigating the trade practices of other countries in March after the US Supreme Court ruled Trump's previously announced Liberation Day tariffs were illegal.

China is facing the highest tariff rate of up to 40%, followed by Vietnam at up to 35%, with others facing either 20% or 25%.

The US Trade Representative (USTR) announced the proposed tariffs together with extensive reports of how each jurisdiction's trade practices purportedly impact American commerce.

The new duties are not expected to take effect until next year and have to go through rounds of public consultation and, potentially, hearings.

Tariffs are taxes levied on imported goods. The amount is typically calculated as a percentage of a good's value and paid to the government by businesses importing products.

Some of these rates will be effectively reduced because of caps on tariffs Trump has agreed to. Individual countries also face different levies.

The proposed tariffs will affect goods from China, the European Union, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan, and India.

The USTR's Jamieson Greer said the latest tariffs issued would "level the playing field for American workers and chart a new, more sustainable course for the world economy".

World.title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater
World.content:
The first images of an asteroid that Nasa deliberately crashed into have revealed a stadium-sized crater on its surface.

The extensive damage was caused when a Nasa spacecraft hit the asteroid Dimorphos in 2022. The asteroid posed no threat, but this was a test of our planetary defences to see if it was possible to knock a space rock off course.

Four years on, a European Space Agency (ESA) spacecraft called Hera is scouring the scene to fully assess the aftermath of the collision.

"The crater is almost as large as the body itself, which is really, really spectacular," said Dr Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist, who is on the Hera science team.

"It's hard to describe in words all the excitement to actually finally see what happened. And as a crater person, I can also say it's beautiful."

The original 2022 crash test was carried out by a Nasa spacecraft called Dart which hurtled into Dimorphos at 14,000mph (22,000km/h).

It was such a big smash-up that the trail of debris, measuring about 6,200 miles long (10,000km), was spotted by telescopes on Earth and in space.

Dimorphos is about 150m (500ft) wide and was partly chosen as the target because it is one of an asteroid pair - it orbits around a larger space rock called Didymos, which is about 730m (2,400ft) wide.

The crash showed it was possible to change the path of the smaller asteroid.

Before the collision, it took Dimorphos 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit around Didymos. After the crash, the duration of its orbit had shrunk by about 33 minutes.

World.title: Thirty-one killed in massive fire as fuel tanker crashes on Cairo highway
World.content:
Thirty-one people have been killed and 21 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says.

Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening.

Footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched.

Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the tanker had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol.

The regional public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the incident and asked that DNA samples be taken from bodies of the dead.

The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, had been travelling along the highway when a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, prompting the driver to lose control, Al-Ahram reports, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation.

It then crossed the central reservation, overturned and caught fire, the state-owned newspaper says.

Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years, with informal residential areas and often run-down infrastructure making incidents more common, the response to which is often complicated by slow emergency response times and locally improvised rescue efforts, even in the sprawling Egyptian capital.

Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished, as emergency services blocked off entry routes.

World.title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?
World.content:
The debate over which path to follow is also taking place within JNIM's leadership, according to Wassim Nasr, a France 24 journalist and jihadism expert.

He says one camp favours the Taliban's approach of taking power through force with minimal concessions. The other, which he says currently has the upper hand, favours an approach closer to that of Syria's HTS - making compromises and building wider alliances to gain power more quickly.

Nasr believes JNIM may borrow from both models, but that a break with al-Qaeda is inevitable as a result of its political evolution.

Like JNIM, al-Shabab in Somalia appears willing to make deals with former enemies.

According to Abdullahi Guji, BBC Monitoring's Somalia specialist, al-Shabab reached a truce in October with a powerful Somali tribe, the Ma'awisley, whose fighters had been at the forefront of the fight against the group.

The tribe has since withdrawn its fighters from the front line, dealing a serious blow to the government's campaign against jihadists, says Guji.

Guji believes the group may soon have a chance to test whether it can seize power and establish itself as an alternative government across wider parts of the country.

African Union forces are withdrawing from Somalia amid funding cuts and the approaching end of their mandate in December. Meanwhile, the Somali government is facing political crises and rebellions, creating vulnerabilities al-Shabab could exploit, he adds.

There's another reason some jihadists may see an opportunity to expand: they believe Western governments have bigger fish to fry.

With the war in Ukraine, US-Iran conflict in the Middle East and growing rivalries with China and Russia, fighting jihadists is no longer the priority it was after 9/11.

The US withdrawal from Afghanistan in 2021 and the Taliban's return to power, followed by Sharaa's rise in Syria, have reinforced that belief.

World.title: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
World.content:
Judges in Israel have suggested prosecutors drop bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu, potentially handing the caretaker prime minister a boost as he fights for his political survival.

The judges told the attorney general that there was little chance of conviction in the first of three cases he is facing, in which he is accused of granting government favours in exchange for positive media coverage.

They also questioned whether his actions amounted to criminal conduct in a second corruption case, and suggested prosecutors seek a plea deal in a third.

Netanyahu has consistently denied the allegations against him and called on Wednesday for the trial to be ended "immediately".

"Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my family, my son," he said in a televised statement.

"Ten years of incitement to hatred that wounds the soul."

Netanyahu was first charged in 2019, but court proceedings have been prolonged in part by the recent Israel-Gaza war.

The case now under serious doubt, known as Case 4,000, concerns an alleged "reciprocal arrangement" between Netanyahu and the controlling shareholder in Israel's biggest telecoms company. Both denied any wrongdoing.

In a highly unusual step, a judging panel at the Jerusalem District Court summoned Israeli Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara on Wednesday to express their concerns.

"The chances of conviction are low â to an extent that warrants reconsidering the matter," Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman told her, Israeli media reported.

The judges also cast doubt on whether Netanyahu's actions, which are subject to a second case â concerning another alleged quid-pro-quo with another media baron, known as Case 2,000 â met the threshold for criminality.

While they left open the possibility of a conviction in the third case: Case 1,000, which alleges Netanyahu acted for the benefit of an Australian billionaire after being gifted cigars and champagne by him.

World.title: US stocks fall further as fears over AI intensify
World.content:
Big technology firms connected to AI continued to see share prices fall on Wednesday, with stock in Nvidia and Anthropic dropping sharply in early trading.

The surge in Nvidia shares after boss Jensen Huang was reinstated was temporary, and the general stock sell-off continued, with all three main US stock market indices down by closing time. The tech-dominated Nasdaq closed 0.6% lower.

The declines came amid concerns over the level and sustainability of AI investment, which has rattled investors in recent weeks.

Shares in other major tech firms, including Amazon, Tesla and Microsoft closed the day lower, though Meta and SpaceX were in positive territory by the end of the trading day.

Nvidia's share price was down 8% in early trading on Wednesday, extending Tuesday's slide as the boost from Huang's return eased. At close, it ended up 3.4% lower.

The resignation and subsequent reinstatement of Nvidia's CEO after revelations of his extramarital affairs has seen the market value of the world's premier AI chipmaker fluctuate wildly.

Given Nvidia's position as both supplier and financier of many other firms involved in the AI rollout, its rocky fortnight has had a wider impact.

The US government also announced a raft of new tariffs on countries and trading partners on Wednesday as part of President Donald Trump's flagship trade policy.

The value of big tech companies have sheltered the US economy from global economic shocks, including tariffs.

But share prices in recent weeks have been volatile in response to the US midterm elections and other events in the AI industry.

World.title: US Army says controlled blast of explosives in Iowa was 'huge success'
World.content:
Middletown Mayor Rodney Johnson told the BBC he felt "relieved" after the detonation.

He watched the blast from his job at a manufacturing plant eight miles (12km) away from the blast - and monitored a camera at his two-bedroom home just one mile from the detonation site.

"We did not feel anything. We did not see anything," Johnson said.

Also eight miles away from Middletown, Sandy Mabeus closed the windows and the garage at her home, brought their outdoor cat inside and hunkered down.

The family watched three separate live streams on iPads and televisions of the explosion as it happened.

"We did not feel or hear a thing here," she told the BBC, adding that she checked the videos to confirm it had actually happened.

"The waiting and wondering has not been a good thing for anybody in the area," she said. "Hopefully they had a very good result and we can just get on with things."

Iowa farmer David Vandenberg lives about 20 miles from the blast site and said he first learned of the detonation around two weeks ago. The Army Corps of Engineers took samples from his yard and pond on Tuesday.

"I was listening this morning, and I did hear a rumble about nine o'clock," he told the BBC on Wednesday, but didn't see or smell anything.

Vandenberg expects officials to return to take more samples but "was happy to see that the blast was relatively contained. "I think the effects will be minimal"

Illinois Governor JB Pritzker said on X that his state was "seeing little to no impact" from the blast. In a press release, he said he was directing state agencies to remain on standby for any "unanticipated impact".

The Iowa site is only 10 miles (16 km) from the Illinois border.

World.title: California warns of flooding as King Tides peak over Thanksgiving
World.content:
Coastal areas of California are bracing for potential flooding as king tides peak in the state during the US Thanksgiving holiday.

Water levels across the US state's vast coastline could reach over 8ft (2.4 metres) in some areas on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the National Weather Service (NWS) - breaking records set just last month.

The NWS has warned parts of California could face major coastal flooding, which is likely to be significant in low-lying areas. There have already been some reports of flooding.

Meanwhile, storms are also forecast for the Pacific Northwest, including the Canadian province of British Columbia, and eastern parts of the US.

Portions of a pier in northern California came crashing down into the ocean on Wednesday as high tides and strong waves battered the structure, video showed.

Beachgoers have been advised to stay away from the water's edge as large waves could suddenly form. Such waves could be damaging to piers and jetties, and could capsize small vessels, the NWS warned.

Flooding has already been reported in the San Francisco Bay Area.

In San Diego, a high tide of 8 ft 11in was recorded on Wednesday morning local time - potentially breaking the record for highest tide measured in the area, which was just set late last month at 7.98ft.

In Los Angeles, the tide on Wednesday was thought to be as high 8.19 - the record for the city that was set only weeks ago 27 October when parts of the California coast experienced flooding.

Recently set high tide records were also broken in Santa Barbara and La Jolla, according to preliminary data.

King tides are the highest predicted tide of the year and are above the highest water level reached at high tide on an average day.

While they typically occur once or twice a year in most coastal areas, they are happening more frequently in some as sea levels rise. These king tides are being strengthened by the strongest El NiÃ±o weather pattern on record.

World.title: Beyond the Monday Lines: Lasisi Olagunju and our national memory, By Toyin Falola
World.content:
… one cannot help but note that the presentation of the books highlights how prolific the author is and the importance of journalism in the intellectual debates in society. Olagunju’s books are characterised by explanations of national challenges, as well as the use of culture for understanding contemporary reality. This is an opportunity to introduce these works to a wider audience, inspiring new generations of readers and writers to appreciate the importance of public discourse and be challenged by the boldness of a public intellectual who has carved his name into the sands of time.

The “Monday Lines,” a weekly column by Dr Lasisi Olagunju, is not merely writing based on the happenings in politics each specific week. The column is also an ongoing analysis of the country’s successes, situations, leadership, institutions, histories, contradictions, and failures. Using his writings, he has succeeded in providing a platform where political criticism and history can be analysed together using Yoruba proverbs, idioms, and mythologies, as well as the life situations of ordinary citizens regarding the direction of the nation. The public presentation in Ibadan gives us the chance to formalise and archive for posterity the body of writings that dissects power relations, describes the Nigerian situation, and engages Yoruba thought in public discourse.

Olagunju’s corpus of writings got a more durable platform on Tuesday, 24 November when he released six-plus books at the International Conference Centre, University of Ibadan, Ibadan. These books constitute collections of his columns, book reviews, lectures, and writings in general, which provide the reader with the opportunity to come face-to-face with his intellectual prowess, even beyond his weekly newspaper penmanship. In addition to being an editorial feat, it provides good grounds for contemplating the place of journalism in the preservation of national memory and accountability. It becomes more evident from the significance of the launch of his works when one considers the intellectual interests I have shown towards the person and work of Olagunju. I have studied his courage, politics, eloquence, and critical thinking. This kind of assessment becomes crucial since it moves the discourse from mere glorification of a successful journalist to an intellectual tradition, rarely associated with popular writing. What was showcased were serious works made for deep intellection and not just a broad, everyday audience that focuses on entertainment, accessibility, and strong commercial appeal.

In a previous piece, I referred to Olagunju as an evaluator of Nigerian society. This is because the act of evaluation is one of the many characteristics that define his journalistic activities. An evaluator does not just report facts but also evaluates situations that led to the emergence of the facts, identifies trends, and asks what these trends mean concerning the situation of society. A society needs to have people who keep on evaluating situations and reporting on their evaluations to diagnose the situation of that society.

Such an understanding forms a handy basis for grasping the significance of Olagunju’s writings. These constantly revisit issues that have been problematic in Nigeria: political leadership, governance of institutions, insecurity, economic hardships, ethnic and religious conflicts, and the increasing gap between the hopes of the citizens and the performances of their leaders. His issues may be current, but his concerns are timeless. What does leadership mean in a society that remains insecure and in economic distress? Why is politics always divorced from results? What becomes of a country whose institutions no longer cater to the needs of its citizens? This is not something that will stay within the bounds of the news cycle. These are issues within the discussion regarding the political development of the nation and the role of the citizen. The value of Olagunju, in part, stems from his commitment to addressing these types of questions, even when they have faded out of the public eye and when many in his profession are either afraid to face such matters head-on or are already desensitised, sometimes compromised with regard to such matters in question.

Olagunju is gifted in problematising issues. Parables and aphorisms are among the tools he invokes in this regard. Take, for example, in his parable of the noble, he recalls the well-known story of the mice that knew that a cat was a problem for them but found no one bold enough to put a bell around its neck. He effectively used this tale to discuss the issue of trying to deal with the powerful people of the state. Recognising an issue is easy; doing something about it is much harder. This becomes a demonstration of the difficulty of dealing with powerful people when political elites are hard to hold accountable. Olagunju, in this respect, is the committed voice ready to address powerful people, regardless of their political affiliations. This is an essential distinction within a democratic society. Political power should never be immune to criticism because of its power, popularity, or success at the ballot box. The press has the right and responsibility to challenge politicians, analyse government policies, and point out the ramifications of political failure. While a columnist does not have the power to make policy, he or she can assist in laying out the issues that need to be addressed when making policy.

This relevance of such journalism can be seen from the Nigerian example, where political debate may be coloured by considerations of political affiliation and personality politics or politics of convenience. In this context, criticism will be judged more in terms of who criticises rather than the strength of the arguments. Olagunju draws the very significant conclusion that political activity should always be viewed in terms of its implications for society. Accountability can never be selective.

However, political commentary is not all that Olagunju’s journalistic career involves. One of the peculiar things about Olagunju’s writings is the way he uses the richness and depth of Yoruba history, culture, and language in analysing contemporary political events. Stories, proverbs, literature, history, and idioms do not serve only as stylistic devices in his essays. It is an essential element of Olagunju’s intellectual strength, by means of which he uses cultural knowledge in interpreting contemporary politics and moral dilemmas of the modern world. This is a clever combination of public intellectualism and cultural anthropology. Olagunju is, indeed, a polymath.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In this context, it is essential to take into consideration these distinctive features of Olagunju’s works. He realises his ability to shift from English to the rhetoric of the Yoruba tradition. This writing style allows combining cultural authenticity with the popularity of the text among a broader audience. Not only is such a writing style very important for literature, but it is also significant to the contemporary political and social situation, because it reveals the timeless relevance of Yoruba and African intellectual traditions.

Olagunju’s written columns allow us to participate in an important discussion concerning language, knowledge, and culture. Many African writers write in colonial languages; however, they draw inspiration from their own culture and the oral tradition of their nations. It is obvious from Olagunju’s columns that it is possible to use proverbs of the Yoruba, folktales, and even references from history to make a political statement, to comment on the actions of the officials, and to expose their mistakes in the nation.

Olagunju’s flair for language and interpretation of politics helps us understand why his columns are worth reading not only for those who read newspaper commentaries but for the students of literature, history, political science and journalism. National experience is raised as an even greater concern in Cowries of Blood: Essays on Herdsmen, Banditry and Nigeria’s Endgame Politics by Olagunju. This book brings together articles that appeared in the Nigerian Tribune from March 2012 to August 2021. These essays deal with issues such as insecurity, political leadership, the impact of violence on individuals, and the many failures that have made Nigerian citizenship a harder endeavour. My review of this work brings out the heavy toll that citizens of the country have been paying because of insecurity, politics, and the failures of the institution.

In addition to the benefit of preserving historical materials in more accessible formats, there is also an advantage that comes with the transformation of columns into book form: they become yet another historical document to be studied in the years ahead. The documents and other records provided by the government are essential in the research on the history of any state, but the historical records need to include more than just the official ones: they should also reflect what people asked, discussed, questioned, and debated. And when such writing survives, it becomes part of the historical record, as well as of the academic canon, allowing future generations to understand the intellectual climate of their times.

In presenting his six-plus books, Olagunju raises a larger issue concerning the preservation of Nigeria’s intellectual history. Nigeria has a lot of journalists, authors, intellectuals, and columnists whose works contribute immensely to the national discussion. But much of their work is scattered across the newspapers’ archives, the Internet, and private computers. Putting together these works of writing is both an act of preservation and an invitation to engage anew with them. The books could be used by universities, research organisations, journalism schools, and individual readers as research tools for studying Nigerian political development, media history, culture, and the developing dynamics of the relationship between citizens and the government. In the end, the importance of these books would not just depend on their being written, but rather on how much they are read, discussed, and analysed.

Moreover, one should bear in mind the importance of the event in the context of changes happening in the media industry. While digital media technology has made it easier to publish and expand the scope of people involved in the process of discussions, one should bear in mind that speed and abundance do not always imply depth. There is always a risk that the need to act quickly and to provide an immediate response may dominate over research, analysis, and context. The long public career of Olagunju makes one think again about such features of journalism as consistency, preparation, language, and editorship. However, it doesn’t mean that journalism cannot develop and the columns in the newspapers cannot be criticised. The point is that journalists should keep on fighting for the features of journalism which make it valuable: independence, accuracy, courage, context and public interest. The evaluation of the column should be done in relation to the argument, not language.

Nonetheless, there is yet another factor associated with this event specifically because of its location. The city of Ibadan is known to be the intellectual capital of Nigeria. It is known for having the University of Ibadan, which is famous for its intellectual debates and global impact. Thus, the holding of the presentation at UI’s International Conference Centre is justified since this will help study the links between journalism, scholarship, language, and the development of the nation. In addition, it is well suited to the culture of the city where much of Olagunju’s writing takes place.

To sum up, one cannot help but note that the presentation of the books highlights how prolific the author is and the importance of journalism in the intellectual debates in society. Olagunju’s books are characterised by explanations of national challenges, as well as the use of culture for understanding contemporary reality. This is an opportunity to introduce these works to a wider audience, inspiring new generations of readers and writers to appreciate the importance of public discourse and be challenged by the boldness of a public intellectual who has carved his name into the sands of time.

Toyin Falola, a professor of History, University Distinguished Teaching Professor, and Jacob and Frances Sanger Mossiker Chair in the Humanities at The University of Texas at Austin, is the Bobapitan of Ibadanland.

This is the text of the chair’s remarks at the public presentation of Dr Lasisi Olagunju’s books on Tuesday, 24 November, at the International Conference Centre, University of Ibadan.

World.title: Security operatives assault lawmaker’s aide attempting to access 2026 budget review meeting venue
World.content:
Security operatives on Wednesday injured an aide to a senator while attempting to prevent him and another aide from gaining access to a closed-door meeting of the Senate Committee on Appropriations at the National Assembly in Abuja.

Members of the committee began deliberations on reducing the size of the 2026 budget and revising some of its components, as requested by President Bola Tinubu.

The lawmakers commenced consideration of the president’s request barely 24 hours after it was submitted. The meeting, however, was held behind closed doors.

For the budget, the total expenditure was reduced from N68.3 trillion, as earlier approved, to N65.1 trillion. Government revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, is projected at N33.7 trillion, while aggregate capital expenditure stands at N26.2 trillion.

The revised budget also retains the government’s borrowing plan at N29.2 trillion, comprising N18.4 trillion in domestic borrowing and about N10.8 trillion in foreign borrowing.

The Senate Appropriations Committee was mandated to scrutinise the budget revision as proposed by the president and expected to report back to the Senate whether to approve or recommend otherwise.

While the committee members were deliberating, security personnel attached to the committee chairman, Adeola Olamilekan (APC, Ogun West) were stationed at the entrance to prevent journalists and other non-lawmakers from accessing the meeting room.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

However, pandemonium broke out at the entrance a few hours after the meeting began when two aides to Allwell Onyesoh, the senator representing Rivers East Senatorial District, attempted to enter the room but were stopped by the security personnel.

Multiple sources who witnessed the incident told PREMIUM TIMES that the aides, a personal assistant and a legislative aide, identified themselves and insisted on entering the room because their principal was already inside the meeting.

The senator’s personal assistant was identified as Dr Kingsley, while the other aide identified himself as Kingsley Wali.

Eyewitness accounts indicated that an argument ensued between the aides and the security personnel, with the aides allegedly attempting to force their way into the meeting room.

In the ensuing confrontation, the security personnel allegedly assaulted Mr Wali, leaving him injured, and pushed Mr Kingsley against a wall.

Shortly after the incident, journalists rushed to the scene to ascertain what had happened.

Speaking with journalists, Mr Wali, whose clothes were soaked in blood, said he and his colleague had attempted to enter the meeting room after their principal had gained access but were stopped by the security personnel.

He said that while they were arguing with the operatives, the personnel pushed his colleague, Mr Kingsley, against a wall.

He added that he attempted to explain to the operatives that they were aides to a senator and not outsiders seeking unauthorised access.

Mr Wali alleged that while he was explaining, the security personnel grabbed Mr Kingsley by the neck and began beating him.

He further alleged that the operatives held him and pushed him down a staircase, causing him to fall and sustain injuries. He also claimed that when he attempted to get up, the personnel grabbed him again and struck him on the head with the butt of a gun.

After the security personnel left, Mr Kingsley reportedly took photographs of his injured colleague lying in a pool of blood and sent them to their principal via WhatsApp. The photographs prompted Mr Onyesoh to leave the meeting briefly to check on his aides.

On seeing Mr Wali covered in blood, the senator reportedly took him into the committee room to show other lawmakers the extent of his injuries.

The committee members subsequently directed the committee clerk to ensure that Mr Wali received urgent medical attention. He was taken to the National Assembly Clinic for treatment.

NASS to investigate

Reacting to the incident, Kayode Odunaro, media adviser to the committee chairman, confirmed that a confrontation occurred but said it happened without the chairman’s knowledge.

“There was a misunderstanding between aides of some senators trying to forcefully gain entrance to Senate Committee Room in a closed session with state security aides at the entrance of the Committee Room.

READ ALSO: Senate approves loan requests Tinubu withdrew

“The incident happened without the knowledge of the Senate Committee Chairman, Senator Solomon Adeola, already presiding inside the Committee Room and other members of his committee, including Senator Allwell Onyesoh, whose aide was injured,” he said.

Mr Odunaro said the National Assembly management had commenced an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

“It was only when Senator Onyesoh came out briefly that he saw his blood-soaked aide, and it was directed that the Clerk of the Committee take the injured to the National Assembly Clinic, where he was treated and discharged.

“The incident is currently under investigation by the Management of the National Assembly to ascertain the facts that led to the ugly incident,” he said.

World.title: INEC sets up AI unit to combat election misinformation ahead of 2027 polls
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has established an Artificial Intelligence (AI) division within its Information and Communication Technology Department to tackle misinformation and digitally manipulated content ahead of the 2027 general elections.

INEC Chairman, Joash Ojo Amupitan, disclosed this on Wednesday at the Nigeria Election Risks and Readiness Summit 2026 organised by the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) in Abuja.

Mr Amupitan, who was represented by his Chief Press Secretary, Adedayo Oketola, said the commission was strengthening its capacity to detect and respond to emerging forms of digital manipulation, including deepfakes, synthetic voices and fabricated videos.

He warned that such content could undermine public confidence in the electoral process, discourage voter participation and trigger panic or communal violence, particularly when circulated through coordinated online campaigns.

He noted that INEC is strengthening collaboration with media organisations, fact-checkers and civil society groups to ensure that accurate information reaches the public promptly.

The concerns raised by INEC come amid growing attention to the use of digital platforms and artificial intelligence to influence political narratives ahead of the 2027 elections.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, commended CJID and its fact-checking initiative, DUBAWA, for investigating and exposing emerging threats to electoral integrity, including foreign information manipulation, AI-generated disinformation and coordinated online campaigns.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Disu warned that fabricated videos, doctored audio recordings and coordinated false narratives could distort political participation, erode public trust and provoke violence. He added that an election could be attacked through false information even without the use of firearms.

INEC steps up preparations for 2027 elections

Beyond addressing misinformation, Mr Amupitan said the commission was taking steps to improve the efficiency of election-day operations, including procuring about 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and replacing batteries in existing machines.

He added that INEC was also providing climate-controlled storage facilities across states to ensure the proper preservation of election materials.

According to him, the commission reduced the number of voters assigned to each BVAS device from 1,250 to 850, while allocating more devices to polling units with larger voter populations. The adjustment is expected to reduce accreditation time to between one and two minutes.

The commission said it would recruit about 1.41 million ad hoc personnel for the 2027 elections. Approximately 700,000 will be deployed for the presidential and National Assembly elections, while another 700,000 will serve during the governorship and State House of Assembly elections.

The commission also said it had extended the registration period for ad hoc staff from two weeks to two and a half weeks.

The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for 16 January 2027, while the governorship and State House of Assembly elections will hold on 6 February 2027.

Mr Amupitan urged journalists and other stakeholders to complete their accreditation within the stipulated period, explaining that the deadlines were guided by the Electoral Act and could not be arbitrarily extended.

He said INEC is working with security agencies and political parties to identify potential election flashpoints and improve security deployment.

The commission, he added, is using its Election Risk Management tool to identify areas vulnerable to violence and other disruptions. The tool would also guide targeted security deployments during the 2026 Osun governorship election.

Stakeholders discuss election violence, security

The summit also featured a panel session titled “Preventing Electoral Violence and Strengthening Election Security Ahead of 2027”.

The session featured Gloria Korang, programme manager at the West Africa Network for Peacebuilding (WANEP); Bukola Idowu, executive director of Kimpact Development Initiative; Raphael Mgbaegbu, head of social research at NOI Polls; and Safiya Bichi, senior manager at YIAGA Africa, moderated by Tolulope Adeleru-Balogun of News Central Television.

The panel’s focus on electoral violence and security formed part of broader discussions at the summit on election preparedness and the protection of those involved in the electoral process.

Mr Amupitan condemned political violence and attacks on journalists, election officials and party supporters, warning that such incidents could undermine democratic participation and the credibility of elections.

He said INEC is engaging the police, political parties and other security stakeholders through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security to address threats before, during and after the elections.

The commission also called for responsible political communication, urging political parties and their supporters to avoid inflammatory statements and actions capable of escalating tensions.

READ ALSO: INEC selects 520 polling units for mock election in Enugu

Earlier at the event, the European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, said credible elections required more than the conduct of voting and the announcement of results. He said they also depended on a fair pre-election environment, access to reliable information and transparent resolution of electoral disputes.

Mr Mignot noted that the credibility of Nigeria’s elections had implications for democratic stability across West Africa.

Similarly, Norway’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Svein Baera, called for the protection of journalists, fact-checkers, editors, election officials and observers, saying those working to safeguard electoral integrity must be able to perform their duties without intimidation and commended CJID and its partners for supporting media development and efforts to strengthen accountability and democratic processes in Nigeria.

World.title: Delta Killings: Assembly demands justice for slain ex-lawmaker, five others
World.content:
The Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, Dennis Guwor, called for a thorough investigation into the killing of a former lawmaker, Moses Anaughe, and five others in Ughelli North Local Government Area.

Mr Guwor made the call during the House’s plenary on Wednesday, condemning the violent incident that occurred at Uduere Community.

The incident, which occurred during a campaign rally organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress on Monday, claimed six lives.

The speaker described the incident as “shocking” and condemned political violence, thuggery, intimidation and lawlessness ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He urged security agencies to investigate the attack thoroughly and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.

“As we approach the 2027 general elections, politics should be about ideas, service and democratic engagement, not violence and the destruction of human lives.

“No political ambition is worth the life of any citizen,” Mr Guwor said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He also admonished political parties, leaders and supporters to embrace peace, tolerance and respect for the rule of law throughout the electoral process.

On behalf of the lawmakers and management of the Assembly, Mr Guwor extended condolences to the bereaved families, Uduere Community and others affected by the tragedy.

The House observed a one-minute silence in honour of the deceased, particularly Mr Anaughe, a former member.

The News Agency of Nigeria reports that Mr Anaughe, who represented Ughelli North I State Constituency in 2019, was removed by the court shortly after his inauguration.

World.title: Delta Assembly passes 2027 appropriation bill of N1.272trn
World.content:
The Delta State House of Assembly on Wednesday passed the state’s N1.272 trillion Appropriation Bill for the 2027 fiscal year.

The bill passed through a voice vote at a plenary presided over by the Speaker, Dennis Guwor, in Asaba.

Its passage followed the presentation of a report by the Chairman of the House Committee on Finance and Appropriation, Marilyn Okowa-Daramola (Ika North-East).

On 16 November, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori presented a budget proposal of N1.23 trillion to the Assembly for approval.

Presenting the committee’s report, Ms Okowa-Daramola said N430 billion was retained for recurrent expenditure, as proposed by the governor, while capital expenditure increased from N806.8 billion to N842 billion.

She said the additional N35.2 billion in capital expenditure was to accommodate priority projects aimed at accelerating infrastructure development and improving residents’ living conditions.

Ms Okowa-Daramola said the adjustment would help strengthen infrastructure delivery, stimulate economic activities and promote inclusive development across the state.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She noted that the fiscal framework aligned with the administration’s development priorities, particularly in education, agriculture, healthcare, industrialisation and youth empowerment.

Ms Okowa-Daramola added that the budget emphasised agricultural production and processing, food security, access to quality healthcare and skills development for young people.

According to her, investment in education, training and capacity building will equip youths with relevant skills to contribute meaningfully to the state’s economic growth.

The Majority Leader of the Assembly, Emeka Nwaobi (Aniocha North), moved the motion to adopt the bill, seconded by Festus Okoh (Ika South).

READ ALSO: Reps urge Tinubu to consider emergency measures in Delta over recurring political violence

Mr Nwaobi also moved the motion for the third reading, which Perkins Umukoro (Sapele) seconded, before the bill passed through a voice vote.

Mr Guwor subsequently directed that the clean copy of the bill be forwarded to the governor for assent.

He commended the governor for his commitment to the state’s continuous development, describing the bill’s passage as a demonstration of the legislature’s commitment to its constitutional responsibilities.

“I wish to thank the governor of Delta for his commitment to the continual development of our state,” he said.

The speaker also praised the Chairman and members of the House Committee on Finance and Appropriation for their diligence, and other lawmakers for their contributions to the bill’s successful passage.

(NAN)

World.title: 2027: Mbah commissions projects in Oji-River, pledges more development
World.content:
Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, has assured the people of Oji-River Local Government Area of sustained development, promising the completion of critical roads, improved water supply, 24-hour electricity and expanded empowerment programmes.

Mbah gave the assurance on Tuesday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) tour of Mmam River and Oji-River Central Development Centres and commissioning of several Smart Green Schools and Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres built by his administration.

The projects inaugurated were Smart Green Schools at Umuagu and Umuome, Inyi, as well as Primary Healthcare Centres at Umuagu, Enugu-Inyi, Agbadala Achi and Amamkpunato Achi.

Addressing separate gatherings of the people at Central School, Inyi, and Achi Court, after meeting with the electorate, polling unit by polling unit, Mbah appealed to them to bear with him for limiting the inauguration to a few projects, noting that even if he spent the entire remaining part of his administration commissioning projects, it would still not be enough, as they were in their thousands.

He said the important thing was that the projects were serving the needs of the people, promising to redouble his administration’s efforts.

“If we had continued on our commissioning spree today, we probably would not have made it here today. But we only stopped at just two Smart Green Schools and three Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres. We could have gone all the way to commission the rest of the projects, but we saw that we needed to come here to meet with you.

Mbah said his administration’s investments in education, healthcare, infrastructure and human capital development were not by accident, but designed to transform the state’s economy and improve living standards.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

At Inyi, he disclosed that, besides the Smart Green Schools, the government was robustly upgrading the Enugu State College of Health Technology, Oji-River, into a nursing college, with new classroom and hostel blocks and an improved curriculum.

He also announced plans to commence the construction of a 660-megawatt coal-fired power plant, saying the project would guarantee 24-hour electricity supply and support round-the-clock economic activities.

On water supply, the governor said the Oji-River Water Scheme was being upgraded, with the installation of new pumps complete to enable it to produce up to 60 million litres of water daily. He stressed that host communities must enjoy adequate water supply.

Mbah further announced plans to empower 260 women in every ward with business grants, while women operating in cooperative clusters would receive agro-processing equipment and additional financial support. Petty traders and vulnerable households would equally benefit from grants, foodstuffs and cash assistance.

On education, he said the Smart Green Schools were exposing children to modern technology, robotics, artificial intelligence and innovation, while developing their critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.

“No longer will our children be limited by lack of modern skills. They will compete with their peers from every part of the world and also guarantee the sustenance of all that we are building today,” he stated.

At Achi, the governor said the critical roads requested by the people, including the Amakpunato-Amoli Road, had already been awarded and funded by his government, expressing optimism that they would be completed before the next rainy season.

“We recognise road infrastructure as essential to connecting communities, farmers and businesses to economic opportunities. So, for us, it is not a favour. It is not also for acclaim. It is a necessary economic enabler,” he added.

Mbah also cited improvements in Enugu’s fiscal performance, saying the state had moved from 30th position nationally in the National Bureau of Statistics’ internally generated revenue (IGR) ranking before his administration to third, behind Lagos and Rivers states.

He said the Smart Schools and Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres were designed to expand access to quality education and healthcare, adding that the health facilities would be adequately staffed and provide free services.

The governor urged residents to sustain the development gains recorded in the state, describing the ongoing transformation as irreversible.

He also called for support for President Bola Tinubu and APC candidates in the 2027 general elections, noting that, besides addressing the challenges of strategic infrastructure and appointments in the South East before now, his administration would not have been able to execute the numerous landmark projects in the state without the president’s reforms, which had made more resources available to state governments.

In their remarks, the Senator representing Enugu West, Osita Ngwu; Member representing Awgu/Oji-River/Aninri Federal Constituency, Engr. Anayo Onwuegbu; and Member representing Oji-River State Constituency, Hon. Osita Eze, commended the administration’s projects and engagements in the area.

They assured that political mobilisation and public enlightenment would continue beyond the present tour and project commissioning, saying that the projects executed in Oji-River had provided tangible evidence of the administration’s interventions.

The Director-General of the Enugu APC Campaign Council, Chief Charles Mbah, said the campaign train was in the area to appreciate residents’ support and seek their continued commitment ahead of the elections.

A major stakeholder in Oji-River LGA, Hilary Abaratu of GOWASK Construction Limited, reiterated that Mbah had delivered more than was expected of him in his second term, reminding the people that the governor remained their sure path to more infrastructural development, political relevance and prosperity. He said they must not allow anyone to deceive them.

Earlier, Oji-River Local Government Chairman, Hon Gregory Anyaegbudike, attributed the turnout at the rallies to residents’ confidence in the governor, assuring that the people would support APC candidates across the ballot.

The governor was accompanied by APC Deputy National Chairman, South, Dr Ben Nwoye; the party’s South-East Women Leader, Dr Oby Aji; members of the state party leadership, State Executive Council, government officials and other stakeholders, including the Commissioner for Children, Gender Affairs and Social Development, Mrs Ugochi Madueke, and the Commissioner for Human Development and Poverty Eradication, Prof Benedette Ekwutosi Okoli.

Also on Mbah’s entourage, the Commissioner for Culture and Tourism and an indigene of Oji-River also featured prominently during the ward and polling unit consultations by the governor.

World.title: NEC appeals ruling ordering Adebutu‘a inclusion in 2027 Ogun governorship election
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has appealed a judgment of the Federal High Court in Abuja directing it to include the Peoples Democratic Party’s Ogun State governorship candidate, Hon Ladi Adebutu, on the list of candidates for the 2027 election.

INEC filed its notice of appeal on Wednesday, asking the Court of Appeal to review the ruling that ordered the commission to recognise Adebutu as the PDP candidate for the forthcoming Ogun governorship election.

The dispute centres on Adebutu’s nomination and recognition as the party’s candidate. Its resolution will determine whether his name appears on INEC’s final list of candidates for the election.

The appeal means that implementation of the Federal High Court’s directive may remain subject to further proceedings and any orders issued by the Court of Appeal. The appellate court is expected to consider INEC’s arguments and determine whether the lower court was right to order Adebutu’s inclusion.

The case has attracted significant political and legal attention in Ogun State, where political parties, aspirants and voters are preparing for the 2027 election. It could also affect the PDP’s internal dynamics as the party consolidates its position ahead of the campaign season.

INEC is responsible for preparing and publishing the final list of candidates, subject to applicable court orders and the provisions of the Electoral Act. Until the appeal is resolved, Adebutu’s candidacy and inclusion on the final list remain unsettled.

The Court of Appeal’s decision will determine whether the Federal High Court’s directive stands or is overturned.
