World.title: Musician Michael Eckert killed in attempted Toronto home invasion, police say
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Police have identified the victim of a shooting during a home invasion in midtown Toronto Wednesday as Michael Eckert, 39. As CBC’s Dale Manucdoc explains, police are seeking at least one suspect.

A man killed in a midtown Toronto home invasion early Wednesday is being remembered as a talented musician who "always led with his heart," according to a longtime friend.

Police have identified the man who was fatally shot as Michael Eckert, 39.

Emergency crews responded to reports of a shooting at a residence in the St. Clair Avenue West and Poplar Plains Road area at around 2:40 a.m., according to a Toronto police news release Wednesday afternoon.

An unknown number of suspects forced entry into the residence, police said. One of the suspects was confronted by Eckert, shot him and fled the home, police said. Eckert was taken to hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

Staff Sgt. Shain Griffin with 53 Division told CBC News early Wednesday morning the victim was the homeowner's son.

Police identified the victim of a shooting during a home invasion in midtown Toronto Wednesday as Michael Eckert, 39, of Toronto. (Toronto Police Service)

Toronto police Det. Sgt. Alan Bartlett said at a news conference earlier Wednesday that there is no evidence to suggest the family was targeted.

"I understand and recognize how deeply troubling this must be, not only to the residents of that community, but to the residents of the city of Toronto as a whole," Bartlett said.

There were four residents inside the home at the time but no one else was injured, he said.

This is Toronto's 37th homicide of the year, according to police.

Bartlett said Toronto police Chief Myron Demkiw assured him that every resource available will be provided to investigators and "no expense will be spared."

He said police do not yet have details on the number of suspects, any descriptions or what vehicles may have been used.

He urged anyone with surveillance video or anyone who saw anything between 2 a.m. and 3 a.m. to contact police.

WATCH | Residents on edge after man killed during attempted home invasion: Residents on edge after man killed during attempted home invasion | Duration 0:25 Neighbours are reacting after a man was killed during an attempted home invasion near Casa Loma early Wednesday.

Victim was a 'loving and caring person': friend

Galen Pelley, a friend of Eckert, said he knew him for about 20 years after they met studying music at Humber College. He said they made music together ever since they met and he felt Eckert was like a brother to him.

"We're all still in shock," Pelley said Wednesday. "We can't believe that this would happen to anyone, let alone someone that we all cared about and who cared for so many himself."

Pelley said Eckert, the youngest child in his family, had two sisters and two brothers and did more than his share of taking care of others. He was also an uncle, he said.

"Mike always led with his heart, both on stage and off stage," he said. "He had an affinity for drummers and I always thought guitarists wrote the best songs."

WATCH | Friend of fatal home invasion victim says Michael was ‘chosen family’: Friend of fatal home invasion victim says Michael was ‘chosen family’ | Duration 1:22 Police have identified Toronto musician Michael Eckert as the victim of a shooting during a home invasion in midtown Wednesday. Galen Pelley, a friend of Eckert, said he knew him for about 20 years after they met studying music at Humber College. Pelley described Eckert as "chosen family" and an important part of the music community in the city.

Pelley described Eckert as a "gentle giant" who was an avid reader and a humble, "loving and caring person."

"He spoke louder through his music than he ever would off stage or in person," he said.

Eckert's instrument of choice was the pedal steel guitar, he said.

Eckert performed at the 113th Grey Cup in Calgary as back up for Blue Rodeo this month, Pelley said, adding: "He's gone too soon and that was a real moment for him to flourish."

'Far too many' home invasions in Toronto: city councillor

Coun. Josh Matlow told reporters outside the home Wednesday there have been "far too many" home invasions in the city and that it needs to be a top priority to address residents' concerns.

"There's a feeling amongst Torontonians that far too often people go to bed at night worrying about whether or not they'll wake up to somebody in their home," Matlow said, adding there's work to do in the community to support "very scared" residents.

He said he has offered Demkiw his "complete support" during the investigation. He urged people to not jump to conclusions.

MPP Stephanie Smyth, who joined Matlow, said police do what they can to investigate incidents, but that more needs to be done to address the fear residents feel.

Coun. Josh Matlow and MPP Stephanie Smyth spoke to reporters outside the scene of a fatal home invasion on Wednesday. They shared their condolences for the victim's loved ones and reassured residents they will do their best to address fears. (Paul Smith/CBC)

"They can talk about the stats all they want, but the bottom line is people are afraid. And the one place you should not feel afraid is in your own home," she said.

Matlow added that "it's shameful" to hear that many residents in the neighbourhood and nearby areas have hired private security to safeguard their homes. Smyth said there needs to be stronger deterrence for such crimes, such as harsher penalties.

"People have to do what they feel is the right choice to ensure the safety of their family," Bartlett said in regards to some people hiring private security.

When asked what tips he had for residents regarding a potential home invasion, he said people should call 911 immediately and that Toronto Police Service "provides the best that it can in terms of public safety services."

"Oftentimes we can't provide the why, we simply don't know. What my promise has been to the victims' family is that we'll do our very best to provide the who."

Incident follows Bridle Path home invasion last month

The incident comes nearly a month after a home invasion and shooting sent a family of four adults in Toronto's Bridle Path neighbourhood to hospital. Police arrested one suspect in Ottawa last week and are looking for two others.

Police have been investigating and patrolling to deter home invasions in parts of the city after seeing a rise in incidents earlier this year, Demkiw said in remarks to the Toronto Police Service Board back in July.

He said the service launched the initiative in areas that saw the largest increase in home invasions, which includes 22, 32 and 53 Divisions. The 22 division covers neighbourhoods in central and southern Etobicoke, 32 operates in central and western North York, and 53 Division covers central and midtown Toronto.

"We continue to put our people and our resources where we see challenges, and where we hear concerns from our communities," Demkiw told the police board.

Home invasions hit a 10-year high in 2024, before dropping in 2025 and then rising again at the beginning of this year in Toronto, according to CBC News analysis of Toronto police data. Affluent areas with large detached houses and driveways were among the hardest hit.

World.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dead at 65
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, has died. He was 65.

Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.

"From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music," the band said.

"His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed."

On the night he was inducted in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.

"I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band," he wrote. "You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible."

The band's huge pop hits include Hungry Like the Wolf, The Reflex and Rio. Their rise up the charts was inextricably linked to the launch of MTV.

The two-time Grammy Award winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Visionary Award recipients.

Andy Taylor, second from right, poses with his Duran Duran bandmates in 1983. (Express Newspapers/Getty Images)

Fashion, synthesizers and glam-pop

The band's imperial stage occurred with a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983, with such dance-floor barnburners as Girls on Film and Union of the Snake and the moody ballads The Chauffeur and Save a Prayer. Other hits in the coming years included The Wild Boys, New Moon on Monday and Come Undone.

Their popularity was cemented when they recorded the James Bond theme song A View to a Kill and earned a slot at Live Aid in 1985.

Mixing fashion, pioneering synthesizers and glam-pop swagger, the telegenic band were all over radio and young people's walls, with bassist John Taylor and singer Simon Le Bon becoming heartthrobs and the band being labelled part of the New Romantics. Princess Diana was known to be a fan, which meant a lot to the band.

"Andy never took the easy musical route. His overdrive, overdrove us into being the only funk/rock/punk band in the New Romantic movement, with songs that still survive, decades later when his own life is cut so short," Le Bon said in a statement Wednesday.

The band's success was due in large part to their videos, including their Antigua-set song Rio, which featured shots of the band in pastel suits sailing confidently on a yacht.

WATCH | Duran Duran plays Calgary during peak of their fame: From the archives: Duran Duran plays Calgary at the height of their fame | Duration 3:28 On Feb. 4, 1984, CBC's The National reported on the popularity of the British group Duran Duran, and the frenzy they put their fans into.

For the album Rio, they shot three music videos in Sri Lanka — including Save a Prayer, for which bass guitarist John Taylor was sprayed by an elephant — and two in Antigua, feeding MTV's need to have a stream of visuals, something classic rock didn't have.

"A lot of the success of the album is down to the power of the videos and the way it made the band omnipresent around the globe," Le Bon told the Daily Beast in 2012.

Andy Taylor agreed: "I don't think we could have done it without MTV."

Taylor was the first of the Duran Duran boys to get married, tying the knot with Tracey in 1982 and having four children — Andy, Georgie, Bethy and Izzy, and a grandson, Albie. He is survived by all of them, and they credited his devotion to them in a family statement.

"For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first. Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home," the family statement said.

In 2023, he released the album Man's a Wolf to Man, his first solo release in over 30 years. On the title track, he sang: "Last night/I dreamt someone loved me/And life was not surreal/Someone's souvenir."

World.title: Montreal mayor walks back 'clumsy' Kraft Dinner comment after major tax hike
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A day after the City of Montreal unveiled a budget that featured a property tax average increase of 9.8 per cent — about three times the inflation rate — the mayor is once again on the defensive.

This time, it's over comments she made about Kraft Dinner.

The tax increase announced on Tuesday was the talk of city hall, as it meant that Montreal homeowners will need to spend an average of $515 more on taxes.

Soraya Martinez Ferrada has insisted the tax increase is necessary to get the city's finances in order and to catch up on much-needed infrastructure work.

During an interview with local media outlet Urbania, the mayor talked about the city's financial struggles and made a comment that has sparked lots of social media backlash.

"We're going through every service to see what we can save. It's like when you make your personal budget: if you know you'll have less money one year, then, you have to make choices," she said.

"Sometimes, you'll have to eat a little more Kraft Dinner because you can't afford filet mignon."

Many comments online suggested the mayor and the city should've found alternative solutions to the city's financial problems instead of imposing such a hefty tax on residents.

WATCH | Montreal mayor responds to backlash: Montreal mayor eats her 'clumsy' words after KD faux pas | Duration 1:19 While speaking to French media outlet Quatre95 on Tuesday about the city’s 2027 budget, Soraya Martinez Ferrada tried to draw a parallel between municipal and household budgets, saying, "We might tell ourselves sometimes that we’re going to eat a little bit more Kraft Dinner, because we can’t afford filet mignon." The comment has garnered a lot of online reaction.

In an Instagram story posted on Wednesday, the mayor acknowledged her comments were "clumsy."

"What I wanted to say is the city will have to make choices: Build new parks or fill potholes. I'm going to focus on filling potholes."

A large chunk of the 9.8 per cent average property tax increase will generate money for a new infrastructure fund that will help the city make more cash payments for maintenance and repair work, rather than relying on credit.

This increase means Martinez Ferrada has broken her campaign promise about limiting tax increases to the rate of inflation.

She was sworn in as mayor in November 2025 and this is her administration's second budget.

The leader of Projet Montréal, Ericka Alneus, said the city's tax increase will have a major impact on renters. (Cassandra Yanez-Leyton/CBC)

A proposition from the opposition party

Speaking with Radio-Canada on Wednesday, the leader of the Official Opposition at city hall says the backlash online captures a sense of shock and frustration from Montrealers over the tax hike.

"Beyond this Kraft Dinner story, it's a taxation rate that is difficult to swallow for a lot of people," said Ericka Alneus, leader of Projet Montréal. "They're mad and they're profoundly worried."

Projet Montréal is urging the Martinez Ferrada administration to allow Montrealers to pay their next tax bill across 12 payments — as opposed to two — without accumulating interests.

Alneus pointed out that the mayor's party, Ensemble Montréal, promised a similar reprieve on tax payments for low-income seniors.

"If she stands by her decision, she should give some tools to Montrealers to deal with it," she said.

World.title: Colombia’s special forces liberate hostages from Cartagena supermarket
World.content:
Colombia’s security forces liberated some 20 people who were held hostage inside a supermarket in the northern city of Cartagena after a 15-hour stand-off.

The operation ended a tense situation that began around 8AM on Tuesday when the armed kidnappers entered the Exito supermarket in La Castellano, a residential neighborhood.

According to President Abelardo de la Espriella, who led the liberation operation, the kidnappers meant to rob an armored car that had already left with the proceeds of the day before.

The kidnappers subsequently kidnapped a group of 30 people, and demanded COP7billion ($2 million) and the possibility to escape the supermarket.

Throughout the day, at least five of the hostages were released from the supermarket cafeteria, whose windows had been covered with papers. One video showed a row of hostages sitting behind the window.

Riot police was deployed around midnight after family members and onlookers became restless.

The situation took a quick turn after 1PM when explosions were heard and special forces entered the building.

The security forces killed one of the kidnappers and detained the remaining four, De la Espriella said in a social media video.

Images that were shared on social media showed special police forces securing the Exito’s cafeteria and removing the paper from the windows.

De la Espriella said that all the hostages were released in an “extraordinary joint operation between the National Police and the military forces.”

One agent would have been injured in the rescue operation, reported Caracol Radio.

The kidnappers “were given the opportunity to surrender and release the hostages, but they rejected that opportunity, so we took decisive action,” said the president.

In the morning, the prosecution said the kidnappers’ arms and explosives were fake and former hostages said the hostage takers spent most of the day getting drunk.

World.title: 22 injured after car bomb strikes central Colombia governor’s office
World.content:
Twenty-two people were reportedly injured and more than 80 buildings were damaged in a car bomb attack on the Governor’s Office of Meta in Villavicencio, central Colombia.

According to Meta’s Security Secretary, Franklin Olivos, the car that exploded carried approximately 100 kilograms of explosives and caused damage to buildings that were located more than 100 meters away from the blast.

Among the injured are five private security guards. One of them needed surgery, according to his employer.

Olivos blamed the attack on the 39th Front, a unit of the FARC dissident group EMC, which has opposed the peace process that started 10 years ago on Tuesday and controls large swathes of jungle territory in the south of Colombia.

In an initial response, President Abelardo de la Espriella said that “narcoterrorism is desperate because we are confronting it head-on. It seeks to intimidate us and force us to back down so we seek another sham peace process.”

De la Espriella, an opponent of the peace process, has been advertising an “iron fist” policy against organized crime and illegal armed groups.

The president’s alleged offensive has failed to produce any results and guerrilla groups have continued to attack State security forces and infrastructure.

World.title: Colombia strips key critics of security details
World.content:
Colombia’s National Protection Unit (UNP) has withdrawn the security details of journalist Daniel Coronell, a major critic of President Abelardo de la Espriella, after vowing to protect the freedom of the press.

Coronell’s local security detail was removed because he lives in the United States, which would make it impossible for the UNP to reassess his protection plan.

The Miami-based journalist frequently travels to Colombia for his work and was in Bogota to receive a lifetime achievement award from the national journalism prize.

While receiving the prize, Coronell sharply criticized De la Espriella for promoting self-promotion over governance. using state resources to censor critics, restricting public information to “friendly media,” and leveraging a history of aggressive lawsuits against reporters.

The journalist’s criticism triggered a clash with Interior Minister Alejandro Ordoñez, who accused Coronell of being angry for having State subsidies pulled.

After press freedom foundation FLIP responded to defend Coronell, Ordoñez claimed that “the freedom of the press enjoys full protection and guarantees from the government.”

We value and defend freedom of the press as a cornerstone of democracy. The press is free, but it is also responsible. It is not a license to abuse, slander, defame, fabricate stories, spread misinformation, or engage in politics. Nor is it a license to destroy democracy or its institutions with lies. Interior Minister Alejandro Ordoñez

Coronell played a key role in Colombian journalism since the late 1980’s and was forced to flee Colombia in 2005 after reports on the ties of former President Alvaro Uribe and paramilitary groups escalated death threats.

The journalist currently works with Noticias Uno and Caracol Radio, and has more than 700,000 subscribers on YouTube.

The UNP previously stripped former President Gustavo Petro and former presidential candidate Claudia Lopez of their security details.

World.title: Illegal armed group carries out first urban drone attack: three injured in northeast Colombia
World.content:
A couple and their 18-month-old baby were injured in a drone attack on a police station in Cucuta, the first major city to be struck from the sky by guerrilla explosives.

The attack damaged more than 60 homes near the Norte de Santander Police Department in the Tasajero neighborhood in the north of the regional capital, the province’s security secretary, George Quintero, told press.

As of now, the situation is as follows: more than 60 damaged homes located just 20 meters from the police headquarters, and three people injured. Security secretary George Quintero

The homes were hit because the police department’s signal-jamming systems reportedly caused the drones to miss their target.

An unknown number of drones were able to reach the interior of the Police Department’s compound, leaving only minor damage.

Guerrilla group ELN has been carrying out multiple drone attacks in Catatumbo, a nearby region with major coca cultivations, and exercises control in the peripheral slums of Cucuta.

The group was accused of attacking the same police department with home-made mortars in August. This attack injured seven policemen.

In a response to the guerrilla attack, President Abelardo de la Espriella in October ordered the militarization of the border city, which has been struggling with security issues for years.

De la Espriella vowed that he “will not allow narco-terrorism to continue sowing fear and threatening families” in Cucuta and the surrounding Norte de Santander province.

According to the authorities, the militarization of the city sought to “strengthen territorial control, protect citizens, and confront” the illegal armed groups that operate in and around Cucuta.

The president’s offensive against illegal armed groups and organized crime has been hampered by an increase in the use of drones that are equipped with explosives.

All kinds of illegal armed groups use the relatively new technology to push back the authorities from areas under their control.

World.title: Colombia asks X to suspend Petro’s social media account
World.content:
Colombia’s communications ministry said Sunday that it had requested social media platform X to suspend former President Gustavo Petro for “possible incitement to violence.”

In a statement that was published of X, the ministry said it reported Petro’s account to X’s Public Affairs, Safety, and Rules Enforcement Team.

According to the statement, the request to suspend the leftist former president, who has more than 9 million followers, was due to a November 21 post in which Petro asked “the people of Colombia to demand Abelardo’s resignation now.”

Petro has been trying to promote popular opposition against De la Espriella, who he has called an illegitimate president.

According to the ministry, Petro’s call to “take action in the streets” could constitute a call for violence against the government.

In a response, the former president said the De la Espriella administration sought to impose censorship on him, which is “expressly prohibited by the Constitution.”

The ministry’s request “demonstrates the extent of the current government’s illegitimacy,” added Petro.

The former president is now the leader of the Historic Pact (PH) opposition party and has actively been promoting a general strike in response to his successor’s controversial policy decisions.

Petro is a member of the PH’s more radical wing and can still count on a significant following among Colombia’s population.
