World.title: Extreme weather threatens Thanksgiving festivities in US
World.content:
A major storm is forecast to move up the US East Coast and is likely to cause travel delays. Weather warnings were enough to postpone Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade for the first time in its 100 years.

New York's iconic Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed for the first time in its 100-year history as extreme weather threatens to disrupt the plans of tens of millions of Americans.

The parade has now been pushed back to 8:30 a.m. EST (1330 GMT) Saturday.

"Our team is now working through the complex operational logistics required to bring the Parade to life on Saturday, and we will share additional details as they are finalized," the company said.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mandani said: "I know that this change of plans will cause inconveniences, yet safety has to come first."

"This will be a heavy storm. We are expecting sustained winds between 30 and 40 miles per hour, with gusts as high as 60 to 65 miles per hour possible," he added.

NBC, which broadcasts the parade, said it will instead show a rerun of the 2025 edition on Thursday.



NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani said 'safety had to come first' Image: Yuki Iwamura/AP Photo/picture alliance

Transport disruptions expected

Despite gale-force winds on the East Coast, coastal flooding in the West and snow in the Midwest, travelers flocked to airports, roads and railways Wednesday for one of America's busiest travel periods of the year.

A major storm developing on the Eastern Seaboard could bring heavy rain, coastal flooding, high winds and power outages to the Carolinas on Wednesday. It is forecast to move to the northern Mid-Atlantic and Northeast on Thanksgiving and is expected to affect air travel at airports in the region.

Already on Wednesday, the security line at New York City's John F. Kennedy International Airport topped one hour.

Thanksgiving is one of the busiest travel periods of the year in the US Image: Lokman Vural Elibol/Anadolu/picture alliance

In the Midwest, winter storm warnings and watches were posted for parts of Missouri and Illinois, with up to 13 inches (33 centimeters) of snow expected in the St. Louis area by Thursday afternoon.

Meanwhile, on the West Coast, king tides were to continue to inundate some coastal areas.

World.title: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies at 65
World.content:
Andy Taylor first revealed he was battling cancer in 2022 when Duran Duran was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. The band had numerous hits in the 1980s, including "Girls on Film" and "Hungry Like The Wolf."

Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor died after "a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer," his family announced on Wednesday. He was 65.

Taylor was responsible for 1980s new wave hits like "Girls on Film," "Hungry Like The Wolf" and "Rio."

The band's pioneering music videos helped drive early success, including through airtime on MTV.

"From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music," the band said in a statement.

"His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed."

A career atop the charts

Duran Duran accumulated a slew of accolades including two Grammys, six platinum records, two Ivor Novello Awards and the MTV Video Visionary Award.

Taylor parted with the band in 1986 to pursue other projects.

Duran Duran were new wave icons Image: Sammlung Richter/picture alliance

The band was due to reunite when they were inducted into Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022.

However, Taylor was unable to be present. He revealed that he had been battling stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years.

"I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band," he wrote at the time. "You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible."

World.title: Egypt: At least 31 dead after fuel truck overturns on highway
World.content:
The accident occurred on the packed Ring Road in Giza near Cairo. Dozens of ambulances responded to the crash, and Egyptian health authorities say the death toll could rise.

A fuel truck overturned on a packed highway in Giza, Egypt, on Wednesday, killing 31 people and injuring 21 more, according to Egyptian authorities.

What do we know so far?

The fuel tanker crash ignited a massive blaze on Ring Road in Giza's Waraq district. The Ring Road encircles the greater Cairo metropolitan area.

Egyptian Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the injured were transported to nearby hospitals and added that the death toll could rise further. He said 39 ambulances are responding to the accident.

Cars were seen burned out after the accident Image: Mahmoud el-Khawas/AFP

A massive fire broke out after the accident, with rescue workers pulling people from their vehicles. A large crowd gathered in the densely populated Waraq neighborhood amid the rescue efforts.

The blaze left at least 27 vehicles, including cars and motorcycles, charred.

An investigation has been launched into the crash, according to Egypt's public prosecutor. DNA tests are being carried out to identify badly burned victims of the blaze.

Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi expressed his deepest condolences and sympathy to the victims and directed relevant authorities to provide necessary support to the families of the victims and the injured.

Italy, Algeria extend condolences to victims

Other countries also reacted to the crash in Giza.

Italian Foreign Affairs Minister Antonio Tajani said he extended his "deepest solidarity to the victims' families," Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty "and to the Egyptian people, whom I count as friends, at this tragic time."

Algerian Ambassador to Egypt Mohamed Sofiane Berrah also said the Embassy of Algeria in Cairo extended "its deepest condolences and heartfelt sympathy to the sisterly Arab Republic of Egypt."

Car accidents are frequent in Egypt due to poor road conditions, reckless driving and lax enforcement of safety rules.

World.title: Nigeria detains 5 Mexicans, confiscates over $220 million of meth
World.content:
Nigeria's anti-drug agency said Mexican experts were allegedly recruited by a Nigerian national to run a meth laboratory in the southeastern state of Enugu.

Nigeria's National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLA) said Wednesday it had arrested five Mexicans and confiscated over $220 million (around €200 million) in methamphetamine as part of a significant drug bust.

What do we know about the drug bust?

The agency said the Mexican experts were allegedly recruited by a Nigerian national to run a meth laboratory in the southeastern Nigerian state of Enugu.

"A total of 1,512 kilograms of methamphetamine, finished and in production, with an estimated value of $226.8 million was recovered from the clandestine factory," NDLA spokesperson Femi Babafemi said.

Nigeria first rejected the entry of the Mexicans into the country in August. They later entered Nigeria again in September via neighboring Benin using forged passports, with authorities then putting them under surveillance.

On November 11, the Mexicans were taken into custody at the Enugu lab after their movements were tracked by the Nigerian government. A Nigerian was also arrested in a nearby hotel.

Nigerian authorities inspected the Enugu facility and seized industrial equipment along with chemicals Image: NDLEA/Handout/REUTERS

The latest drug bust comes after Nigerian authorities in May also detained 10 people in a anti-meth operation in the southwest, including three Mexicans.

Why do Mexican cartels find African countries desirable for drug production?

The arrests raise concern that Mexican cartels are getting a foothold in Africa for international drug trafficking. In addition to Nigeria, South Africa is another country where Mexicans have been arrested for being involved in a meth lab.

According to Vanda Felbab-Brown, an expert at the Washington DC-based Brookings Institution, Mexican cartels such as the Sinaloa Cartel and the Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generation (CJNG) have expanded their operations into other continents such as Africa.

How drug cartels expand their reach across West Africa To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In a June testimony to the US Senate Caucus on International Narcotics Control , Felbab-Brown said the cartels find "desirable partners" for production in countries such as South Africa and Kenya due to factors such as "limited law enforcement capacities and entrenched criminal and corrupt networks."

According to the UN Office on Drugs and Crime, criminal networks often take advantage of porous borders in the West and Central Africa region to carry out activities such as illicit drug trafficking.

"Many countries in the region have vast territory and borders are located either in very remote or densely populated areas, thus making law enforcement activities particularly difficult to conduct in an efficient manner," the office said. "The porous nature of the borders in West and Central Africa is a major factor of insecurity: the borders are neither demarcated or sufficiently controlled."

World.title: Peter Magyar meets Volodymyr Zelenskyy: Hungary and Ukraine make a fresh start after the icy relations of the Viktor Orban era
World.content:
After years of frosty and hostile relations under Hungary's Kremlin-friendly former PM Viktor Orban, his successor, Peter Magyar, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy seek to reset their countries' ties.

The location and the gesture were carefully chosen: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stood side by side, laid flowers and bowed their heads at the military cemetery in the center of the Ukrainian city of Uzhhorod.

One of those buried there is an ethnic Hungarian who was one of the first soldiers killed in Russia's full-scale war of aggression against Ukraine.

Magyar intentionally chose not to begin his first visit to Ukraine as prime minister at a government building. Instead, his Tuesday afternoon visit began at a place where he could demonstrate his solidarity with Ukraine more clearly than anywhere else.

Uzhhorod, known as Ungvar in Hungarian, is the capital of Ukraine's Transcarpathia region, which is home to around 80,000 members of Ukraine's Hungarian minority. Thousands of ethnic Hungarians are fighting Russian occupying forces on the front lines.

For Hungary, where ethnic Hungarian minorities in neighboring countries traditionally play an important role, the war is therefore closer to home than it is for other European countries.

Magyar described his visit to Ukraine as a "historic day" in a Facebook post. Before the ceremony at the cemetery in Uzhhorod, he said: "I bring with me the solidarity of the Hungarian people. We stand with Ukraine against the Russian aggressor."

Zelenskyy responded on X, saying "We appreciate this gesture of respect toward those who sacrificed their lives for Ukraine's independence."

From low point to fresh start

The meeting between Magyar and Zelenskyy marked a turning point in Hungary's approach to Ukraine.

The two leaders repeatedly shook hands throughout the day. Such scenes would have been unthinkable just a few months ago. The propaganda of Magyar's pro-Russian predecessor, Viktor Orban, portrayed Ukraine as a "mafia state" and "lawless country" on an almost daily basis.

Under Orban, relations between Hungary and Ukraine reached a historic low.

Now the two countries are seeking a political reset, which is important not only for Hungary and Ukraine but for Europe as a whole. After all, Orban's repeated obstruction of support for Ukraine drove the EU to the brink of despair.

Closer economic cooperation

During talks in Uzhhorod, the two leaders also agreed to closer economic cooperation.

Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar (left) and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy laid wreaths and flowers at a ceremony commemorating the Ukrainian defenders who fell during the Russian invasion Image: Janos Nemes/MTI/AP Photo/picture alliance

The talks centered on Hungarian diesel supplies to Ukraine, greater use of Ukrainian gas storage facilities by Hungarian companies, and joint infrastructure projects, including the opening of new border crossings and a direct rail link between Budapest and Kyiv.

Nevertheless, no formal agreements were signed on Tuesday.

At a subsequent news conference, journalists asked questions about sensitive issues between the two countries: minority rights, Ukraine's EU integration and a new EU loan for Ukraine.

Throughout the day, the two men were visibly keen to avoid any discord.

Magyar, for example, described his angry outburst over Ukraine's "Carpathian Eight" initiative in parliament in late September as a "misunderstanding" and suggested that Hungary might, after all, take part.

Zelenskyy's cautious replies to journalists suggest that he knows his country's path to EU membership also runs through Budapest.

A fresh — but not always smooth — start

One of Magyar's statements on Tuesday was key: "We've finally put a stop to this completely unnecessary and inexplicable political escalation."

Even before taking office in early May 2026, Magyar had promised to reset relations with Ukraine. But the process has not been entirely smooth.

Posters belonging to Viktor Orban's Fidesz party portrayed Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Peter Magyar and Ursula von der Leyen as a risk and Fidesz as 'the better choice' in the run-up to the parliamentary election in April Image: Martin Fejer/estost.net/EST&OST/IMAGO

In many respects — but certainly not all — Magyar is distancing himself from his predecessor. He has made no bones of the fact that he sees Russia as the aggressor, but he rejects both arms deliveries to Ukraine and even the transit of weapons across Hungarian territory.

Magyar previously accused Ukraine of treating ethnic Hungarians as second-class citizens — a claim that is not borne out by the facts. He pressed for greater minority rights and for a time blocked the opening of negotiating chapters in Ukraine's EU accession talks.

Magyar also departed from diplomatic convention by choosing the location of his meeting with Zelenskyy in Ukraine: Indeed, it was Magyar who invited Zelenskyy to Transcarpathia.

Hungarian attitudes to Ukraine

Magyar's sometimes confrontational tone toward Ukraine can also be explained by the need to avoid appearing too pro-Ukrainian to the Hungarian public.

According to a November 2026 poll conducted by the think tank Globsec , 33% of Hungarians would now support their country providing military aid to Ukraine. Although this is much more than during Orban's time in office, many Hungarians remain skeptical of Ukraine.

That's why Olena Halushka, a Ukrainian political scientist at the International Centre for Ukrainian Victory (ICUV), sees some aspects of Magyar's visit as a concession to public opinion in Hungary.

A monument to members of the military killed during Russia's war in Ukraine in the city of Berehove, the political and cultural center of Ukraine's Hungarian minority Image: Hanna Sokolova-Stekh/DW

"Magyar has taken over a deeply polarized country," she told DW's Ukrainian Service. "A visit to Transcarpathia is more of a step for the Hungarian population than for Ukraine."

Ukraine accommodated not only Magyar's choice of location but also Hungary's demands for better protection of minority rights, which were set out in a 10-point plan in June. That's because EU integration is one of the country's top political priorities.

After planned restrictions on the use of minority languages were withdrawn in late 2023, Ukraine's parliament in early October passed a law on minority language rights that in some respects goes even further than European standards.

Hungary subsequently dropped its obstruction of the opening of negotiating clusters for Ukraine's EU accession.

'Historic' meeting

Laszlo Zubanics, chairman of the Hungarian Democratic Federation in Ukraine (UMDSZ, one of two Hungarian political parties in Transcarpathia), told DW that the Magyar-Zelenskyy meeting was "historic."

He particularly welcomed the fact that Ukraine will probably implement practical improvements in the protection of minority rights "not only by the end of 2027, but much sooner, within just a few months."

Laszlo Zubanics welcomed the fact that Ukraine is likely to implement practical improvements in the protection of minority rights 'within just a few months' Image: Hanna Sokolova-Stekh/DW

A Hungarian diplomat who spoke to DW on condition of anonymity also called the meeting "historic," adding that after the Orban government's anti-Ukrainian policies, trust now needs to be rebuilt, and that personal meetings between the two leaders play an important role in that process.

The diplomat went on to say that Hungary not only wants to ensure that the rights of the Hungarian minority are protected, it also has a strong interest in being involved in Ukraine's reconstruction.

Overall, the diplomat concluded, both sides are very keen to expand economic cooperation.

A path forward

Hungarian political scientist Daniel Hegedus of the Institute for European Politics (IEP ) in Berlin told DW that while the meeting was a "symbolic milestone," it will be important to see "how the two political leaders capitalize on the symbolic political capital generated by this meeting."

No observers have suggested that this is the grand finale of reconciliation between Hungary and Ukraine.

Nevertheless, Tuesday's reset sends an important signal to Europe, namely that if the political will is there, a deep gulf that has existed for years can be transformed into a set of diverging interests that can be addressed through negotiations.

Or, as Zelenskyy put it, now there are "all the opportunities to build hopefully constructive relations."

This article was originally published in German.

World.title: Spain: Canary Islands witness 1-day migration record
World.content:
The arrival of over 2,000 migrants to the islands comes as Spain holds elections this weekend. The president of the Canary Islands said the archipelago is facing "unprecedented migration pressure."

The Spanish Canary Islands witnessed a one-day migration record on Tuesday, with over 2,100 people arriving to the region in over 24 hours.

Most of the migrants landed on the the island of El Hierro, according to Spanish authorities.

'The Canaries can't take it anymore,' regional leader says

"The Canaries can't take it anymore. We're experiencing an unprecedented migration pressure," President of the Canary Islands Fernando Clavijo wrote on X. He requested an urgent meeting with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to discuss an immediate EU response.

Around 100 minors arrived on Tuesday, with a baby also born during the trip from Africa to the islands.

The Canaries, a tourist destination whose shortest gap with northwest Africa is around 100 kilometers (around 62 miles), tends to see more migrant arrivals in the fall when the waters are calmer. The waters become rougher in the winter due to storms and swells.

Earlier this month, nearly 1,600 migrants from West Africa were saved and taken to the Canary Islands in a previous record. Over 26,000 migrants came to the Canaries this year so far — with half of that figure in November alone.

Spain's Canary Islands see record migrant rescues To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The route from Africa to the Canaries is one of the deadliest in the world for migrants.

Boats taking off for the islands sometimes drift out to open sea, with the migrants onboard facing starvation, dehydration and lack of medical care. Human smugglers frequently organize the trips and abuse the migrants.

Migration major topic as Spain holds snap vote Sunday

The spike in migration to the Canaries comes as Spain will hold a snap election on Sunday.

Migration, along with housing, will be one of the topics at the forefront of voters' minds when they cast their ballots.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who belongs to the center-left Socialist Party, has faced backlash from the opposition regarding his tolerant attitude towards migration. The Spanish government earlier this year enacted a plan to legalize up to 500,000 undocumented migrants.

Moroccan migrants refuse to leave Ceuta To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In late July, over 80,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into the Spanish North African enclave of Ceuta, triggering a crisis for the Sanchez government. Countries such as Germany and Italy tightened or extended border controls due to the influx of migrants into Ceuta.

The far-right Vox party, which could receive its best-ever result in upcoming election, has called for Sanchez and his ministers to be prosecuted for treason over the Ceuta crisis. The conservative Popular Party could form a coalition government with Vox after the election.

World.title: €561 Billion and Still Not Enough: Germany's 2027 Budget Exposes a Coalition on the Brink
World.content:
The budget for 2027 has reached new highs, and pension funds, defense spending and a weak economy are increasing the pressure. At the same time, tensions are mounting within the government.

At first glance, everything seems to be business as usual. Lawmakers in the Bundestag, the lower house of parliament, are holding four days of final debates on how much money the federal government may spend in the coming year, and on what. These follow a familiar pattern: The government pats itself on the back, while the opposition voices criticism. But anyone listening more closely will notice that there are doubts even in the ranks of the coalition parties, the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), their Bavarian allies, the Christian Social Union (CSU), and the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD).

"As a country, we are in a difficult situation geopolitically, technologically, and demographically, and next year's budget is an accurate reflection of that," Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) acknowledged on Wednesday in the Bundestag.

"If we don't change course, in a few years we'll find ourselves in a situation where all federal revenue will have to be spent on social programs, interest payments, and defense," he reflected on Wednesday during a four-hour debate focused on government policy as a whole, rather than the individual budgets of the ministries.

€200 billion in new borrowing: Germany's not so frugal budget To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

This government has now been in office for about 20 months. Back in early 2025, expectations were enormous. Merz had promised to bring the budget back in line with the debt brake enshrined in the constitution, which stipulates that the government can spend only slightly more than it collects (with exceptions now made for defense and security).

Yet for 2027, spending — at just under €561 billion ($614 billion) — will be higher than ever before, and tax revenues are nowhere near sufficient to cover this, meaning Germany is looking at record borrowing for the year totaling €210 billion.

The largest opposition party, the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) calculated that the government will incur €401,000 in new debt every minute next year. In the Bundestag, AfD co-leader Tino Chrupalla called it a "debt orgy" that will paralyze the country. Merz will "go down in history as the chancellor who led Germany to bankruptcy," he exclaimed.

Record spending and record debt

Germany's budget deficit has only ever been higher in the COVID-19 pandemic. The current pressures are obvious: The economy is struggling, the population aging, and Russia's war against Ukraine is about to enter its sixth year.

Merz accused of 'blackmail' over Ukraine funding To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The defense budget is now by far the highest in the history of the Federal Republic, with €109 billion allocated for 2027, an increase of €27 billion on last year. Added to this is the multi-year, debt-financed special military fund, intended to modernize the armed forces, bringing the total defense budget to €139 billion.

Defense spending rises to historic levels

The AfD and the socialist Left Party have sharply criticized this. Left Party parliamentary leader Heidi Reichinnek accused the government of pursuing "militarization and boundless rearmament on the one hand, and brutal social cuts and an orgy of budget cuts on the other."

The AfD's Chrupalla said that the temporary reduction in the electricity tax, pushed through at the last minute, would save the average family a mere €100 a year, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy "walks out of the chancellery here in Berlin with a check for €200 million after just one afternoon."

"Whose chancellor are you, Mr. Merz?" he asked.

The opposition Greens did not agree. While they also criticized the budget as "unserious," Green Party Bundestag member Britta Haßelmann described the AfD's stance on Ukraine as shameful. She rejected the idea that money was being wasted on Ukraine, saying that supporting Ukraine bolstered security for Germany and Europe.

Aid to Ukraine: Still a central controversy

The chancellor shares this view. "You can't say it often enough, either to the far right or the far left: Russia knows exactly what it wants. And Russia wants more than just Ukraine," Merz said.

He added that Russia is escalating tensions in the Baltic region, in Poland, in the Black Sea, and in space; and that Moscow is also seeking escalation in Germany, even at the cost of lives. "That is why we must show Russia its limits," he said.

But it is becoming increasingly difficult for the government to justify the high spending on Ukraine. Germany's pension and health care costs are only getting bigger: By far the largest single budget item is that of the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, which is rising to over €200 billion, even with cuts to unemployment benefits.



Social spending growing faster than revenue

Work is currently underway on a reform of the pension system — something that many see as urgent, as the workforce born in the 1960s, when more than a million children were born in Germany every year, is on brink of retiring. Birth rates nearly halved by the mid-1970s and declined even further afterward. For now, so-called "boomers" still make up one-third of the current workforce — but soon they will be drawing pensions.

Even now, Germany's pensions cannot be financed solely with contributions on wages and salaries. In 2025, just over €420 billion in pensions were paid out, with the government contributing €127 billion of that amount. By 2027, the government aims to save €3 billion on this figure, which is likely to further increase pension contributions.

Pension reform becomes a test for the coalition

The coalition parties are stuck in a row over how to reform the pension system. Chancellor Merz insisted in the Bundestag that the coalition was solving the country's fundamental problems, but he warned that in future, tax revenues "will no longer be enough to afford everything we have become all too accustomed to," he said. "All of us here will have to give up some of the ideas we cherish."

The SPD, on the other hand, is counting on increasing federal revenue. Its parliamentary leader Matthias Miersch emphasized in the Bundestag that large fortunes and inheritances must contribute more to "public costs."

That, he said, must also apply to large companies. Currently, heirs to family-owned businesses often pay significantly less in taxes than heirs to real estate or financial assets, because they can be exempted from inheritance tax if they continue to run the business. This is intended to protect them from having to pay taxes in the event of a breakup or sale of the company.

SPD calls for higher taxes on fortunes

According to Miersch, the government must now think about taxing the wealthy more. "For us, this issue is by no means off the table; on the contrary, we are putting it on the agenda," he said. The government's revenue situation is "an issue we need to discuss."

All in all, the outlook for 2027 is strained — and not just financially. The political differences between the CDU/CSU and the SPD are likely to make working together even more difficult. Conflict is inevitable, especially with several state elections scheduled for the spring.

The chancellor knows this and tried to appear confident that better collaboration was possible. "We must seek compromise in our joint decision-making, represented by these — admittedly quite different — coalition partners," he said.

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: US Army detonates unstable lead-based explosives in Iowa
World.content:
The US Army says a controlled blast is the safest way to deal with explosive chemicals that began crystallizing in storage. US President Donald Trump said "mitigation efforts have far exceeded expectations."

The United States Army detonated nearly 5 tons of aging lead azide at an Iowa ammunition plant on Wednesday, saying the explosive chemical has become too unstable to store.

The controlled blast occurred a little after 9 a.m. local time (1500 GMT) at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, and will destroy the country's entire stockpile of the chemical. Plumes of smoke were seen on camera in video footage after the controlled blast in Middletown.

The US Army has said residents of a small town and other nearby areas should leave "out of an abundance of caution."

"We don't believe that the public should be in a panic," said acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle. "Our goal is to keep as much of it as we can here on our Iowa Army Ammunition plant to prevent it from traveling."

"Early reports from Iowa are that the Army's mitigation efforts have far exceeded expectations," US President Donald Trump said on his Truth Social platform.

What do we know?

The material was moved to Iowa for storage from bases around the country in 2009.

But a March inspection found that it had partly crystallized, making it sensitive to friction and cold and potentially capable of triggering a spontaneous explosion.

"Inaction is no longer an option," said Major General Eric Shirley, who leads the operation.

Rob Cekada, director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, told reporters: "It's not a matter of if, it's a matter of when, and that would not be a great place for us to be in."

The US Army set up blast bunkers around the detonation site amid fears of a toxic lead cloud Image: Austin Johnson/AP Photo/picture alliance

Is it safe to detonate the chemical?

To limit toxic lead dust, the Army has built barriers around the bunkers holding the material and will use foam and water to trap particles.

Reuters reported that Army projections show dust could settle up to 40 miles (64 km) southwest, reaching northern Missouri.

Officials expect the wind to carry the plume away from Burlington, a city of nearly 25,000 people.

While residents within 5 miles (8 kilometers) were encouraged to evacuate, the Federal Emergency Management Agency has also advised people 5 to 20 miles away to stay indoors with windows closed.

The date of the planned explosion has been changed three times over public backlash Image: Austin Johnson/AP Photo/picture alliance

How have people reacted?

The date of the detonation changed three times after public backlash over its impact on the environment and public health. A federal appeals court cleared the plan on Monday after environmental groups sued.

Farmer Jill Holler, who organized a protest, told Reuters: "I'm not opposed if this is the only safe option."

"What I'm saying is that it's been so mishandled that people are confused and don't trust anything they're saying," she added.

World.title: Llega el apagón de encuestas: ¿Qué dice el promedio con las últimas?
World.content:
Esta es la última actualización del promedio de EL PAÍS, del 23 de noviembre. Además, construye tu propio promedio

Se publican decenas de encuestas en una campaña. Son el mejor instrumento para predecir unas elecciones, sobre todo cuando las miramos juntas: eso hace nuestro promedio. Combina todos los estudios dando más peso a las encuestadoras que más aciertan. En su última actualización, ese promedio sitúa al PP con el 31,4% de los votos, unos 2,5 puntos por delante del PSOE (29,1%), y con Vox alrededor del 18%.

En el gráfico puedes elegir entre tres promedios. El “medio” es el que usamos habitualmente; los otros dos sirven para comparar: “agresivo” (que reacciona antes a los cambios pero tiene más ruido), y otro “cauto” (que se mueve menos).

Los sondeos se han movido desde la convocatoria del 6 de octubre. El cambio más claro es la subida del PSOE, que estrecha la ventaja del PP: era de 6 puntos y ahora es de menos de 2,5, y bajando. Nuestros cálculos dicen que el PSOE tiene al menos un 25% de probabilidad de ser primero.

Algo que también ha cambiado es la izquierda del PSOE. Las últimas encuestas estiman un 6,8% de voto para lo que hemos llamado Frentes (Frente Amplio y las coaliciones con Podemos, Compromís, Ara Més o Unidad del Pueblo Canario) y un 1,1% para Podemos en solitario. Juntos rondan el 8% de voto, lejos del 12,3% que logró Sumar en 2023.

La suma de izquierdas y derechas

El número clave de las elecciones es el resultado por bloques. Al cierre, la derecha suma el 51,1% de los votos (PP, Vox y SALF) y la izquierda, el 38,7% (PSOE, Frentes, Podemos y Adelante Andalucía). Son 12,4 puntos de distancia, cuando en las generales de 2023 casi empataron, con 45,6% y 44% respectivamente. La suma de PP y Vox tendrá seguramente la mayoría si supera el 47% de votos.

La ventaja de la derecha creció entre 2024 y el verano de 2025, cuando sus votos pasaron del 48% al 52%. Pero en campaña se ha reducido unos tres puntos. Se ha cumplido nuestra hipótesis inicial: la izquierda, que partía desmovilizada, ha recuperado terreno con la convocatoria electoral, aunque siga por detrás.

El promedio también constata que las encuestadoras discrepan. Casi todas ponen al PP primero, pero con ventajas distintas: desde menos de un punto, según 40dB. o Ipsos, hasta los casi siete de Hamalgama. Solo SW Demoscopia y Cluster17 sitúan al PSOE por delante, además del CIS. Pero el dato de este último es poco informativo porque el centro sobrestima a la izquierda desde 2018.

¿Y si corregimos los llamados sesgos? Algunas encuestadoras se desvían hacia la derecha o hacia la izquierda. Nuestro promedio no lo corrige por un motivo: esas desviaciones cambian de una elección a otra y casi nunca son sistemáticas. Pero podemos ver qué pasaría si lo hiciéramos: el siguiente gráfico permite corregir cada encuesta con el sesgo histórico de su casa.

El resultado depende de qué elecciones miramos. Con los errores de todas las elecciones desde 2018, generales y autonómicas, la ventaja del PP sobre el PSOE sube de 2,5 a 3,5 puntos: en conjunto las encuestas se han quedado cortas con la derecha. Pero en las generales ha pasado lo contrario: subestimaron a la izquierda. El caso más recordado es 2023: las últimas encuestas daban a la derecha 5,4 puntos de ventaja, y en las urnas sacó solo 1,6. Si ajustamos las encuestas con sus sesgos solo en las tres generales desde 2018, la ventaja del PP baja a un punto, aunque la suma de derechas sigue claramente por delante.

Todos estos números son tentativos. Primero, porque las encuestas son una aproximación. Y segundo, porque entre las últimas encuestas y el 29-N hay seis días. La izquierda venía recortando distancia. Esa tendencia podrá seguir o no, pero ya no podremos contarlo aquí con sondeos públicos: la ley impide publicarlos en los cinco días previos a la votación.

¿Cómo funciona el promedio?

Un promedio de encuestas suele ser más preciso que cualquier encuesta aislada: suma la muestra de todas y compensa en parte sus errores, porque mezcla la “cocina” de cada encuestadora. El nuestro funciona así:

1) Todas las encuestas. Usamos las de voto al Congreso publicadas desde las generales de 2023, salvo las encargadas por partidos y las que no tienen trabajo de campo propio. La mayoría las tomamos de Wikipedia.

2) Con distinto peso. Cada encuesta importa según su encuestadora, su muestra y su antigüedad. La nota de cada casa sale de nuestro comparador, que valora su error, su sesgo y si publica sus microdatos (las mejores pesan el doble que una casa normal). El peso de una encuesta se reduce a la mitad cada diez días y desaparece a los 30.

3) Cada casa cuenta una vez. De cada encuestadora pesa su último sondeo, para que no mande quien publica más.

4) Mira hacia atrás. El promedio de cada día solo usa las encuestas con el trabajo de campo terminado hasta entonces. Si una se publica con retraso, la línea de esos días se corrige un poco.

5) Tres ritmos. El promedio central y dos para comparar: el agresivo reduce el peso a la mitad cada 8 días y corta a los 14; el cauto, cada 30 y a los 60.

6) Las listas del 29N. Desde el 14 de octubre medimos las candidaturas nuevas, y las encuestas anteriores se traducen a ellas. SALF y Adelante Andalucía entran en el promedio poco a poco, a medida que las publican las encuestadoras.

7) El sesgo, aparte. La corrección del interactivo usa el error de cada casa en la ventaja entre bloques desde 2018, entero: enseña qué pasaría si las casas volvieran a fallar como de media.

8) El promedio es sólido, pero no infalible. Lo hemos probado con 41 elecciones desde 2018: cinco días antes de votar, falla 1,5 puntos por partido de media. Cambiar la ventana o los pesos lo mejora una décima como mucho. Cuando falla es porque fallan todas las encuestas a la vez, algo que ningún promedio puede corregir: por eso nuestro modelo añade esa incertidumbre.

Todas las encuestas

World.title: La industria de las mil pantallas: los cambios que han transformado el mercado audiovisual
World.content:
Pocos hubieran imaginado hace dos décadas que una incipiente plataforma de vídeos caseros como YouTube sería la cantera del nuevo talento de Hollywood, o que las producciones extranjeras vendrían a España por sus paisajes y por sus profesionales altamente cualificados. Así ha cambiado este sector que ha convertido a España en el primer productor de contenidos de la Unión Europea

La forma de consumir productos audiovisuales que conoció el empresario barcelonés Juan Carlos Tous hace 20 años, cuando creó Filmin, tiene poco que ver con la de hoy. Tanto es así, cuenta, que entonces nadie confiaba en su proyecto, que en la actualidad es una de las principales plataformas españolas de películas y series en línea. “Nos decían que no funcionaría porque nadie pagaba por ver cine en internet, pero sabíamos que el futuro del sector sería la distribución por internet”, contaba en el último capítulo de El poder de las empresas, el pódcast de los que hacen, de Banco Sabadell.

Actualmente, vemos muchísimas películas y series desde la televisión inteligente, el canal más usado, aunque el consumo audiovisual en móvil crece, especialmente entre los jóvenes. La mitad de la población no va a las salas, aunque el 13% acude al menos una vez al mes, según la Asociación para la Investigación de Medios de Comunicación (AIMC). Una situación que está cambiando, pues muchos joven están redescubriendo la experiencia de ir a una sala. Al mismo tiempo los exhibidores han recurrido a la tecnología para aumentar su atractivo proponiendo que la película sea no solo un viaje emocional, sino también físico gracias al sonido envolvente o las butacas que se mueven. Innovaciones que no existían cuando Tous inició su aventura ni en 2008, cuando Ignacio Segura, director ejecutivo de la productora y distribuidora DeAPlaneta Entertainment, llegó a esta compañía.

El consumo doméstico y la experiencia en la sala son parte de la respuesta a los nuevos retos de la industria. A ellos se suman el impacto de la IA, la llegada de talento procedente de nuevos formatos digitales y redes sociales, y la consolidación de España como destino para rodajes. Un escenario de desafíos, pero también de oportunidades para quienes quieran emprender en una industria que, en 2025, convirtió a España en el mayor polo de producción de la Unión Europea (UE), con 423 producciones, un 31% más que el año anterior.

La sala de cine como experiencia

El público acude hoy a la sala de cine como parte de una experiencia compartida. Incluso el más joven, que ha crecido con miles de películas al alcance de un clic, señala Juan Carlos Tous, consejero ejecutivo de Filmin. “Para ellos es un descubrimiento. Les ayuda a romper con una rutina, salir de casa, encontrarse con sus amigos y hacer algo a una hora concreta, cuando ellos están acostumbrados a tenerlo todo cuando quieren”, justifica. Al mismo tiempo, las empresas exhibidoras han enriquecido su oferta con formatos que permiten vivir una experiencia radicalmente opuesta a la doméstica, explica Borja de Benito, responsable de marketing de la Federación de Cines de España (FECE).

De Benito menciona tres innovaciones tecnológicas que cada vez se ven en más salas: el 4DX, que sincroniza una serie de efectos, como el viento o la percepción de olores con lo que sucede en la pantalla; el D-BOX, que busca transmitir físicamente los movimientos de la película mediante balanceos y vibraciones en la butaca; y el Dolby Atmos, con sonido envolvente que imita la manera en que le llegaría al espectador si estuviera dentro de la película.

Otros cines ofrecen opciones prémium con gran acogida entre el público, explica el portavoz de FECE. Son las salas con butacas reclinables y servicio de restaurante, también los espacios júnior, adaptados alas necesidades del público infantil. “Cuentan con entretenimientos alternativos, como toboganes,y ofrecen un parón a media película para que los niños puedan ir al baño”, explica. En 2024 en España había 729 salas con alguno de estos formatos prémium y se habían invertido más de 150 millones de euros tras la pandemia para acondicionar salas tradicionales, de acuerdo con el Dossier de datos de 2024, de FECE. Y se prevé que la cifra siga creciendo, completa De Benito.

Consejos de Empresario Si empezara hoy, crearía una empresa con visión europea y con presencia en varios territorios Ignacio Segura, director ejecutivo de la productora y distribuidora DeAPlaneta Entertainment

España como destino para rodar (y producir) cine y televisión

La industria audiovisual española ha apostado por convertirse en destino habitual para las grandes producciones extranjeras, señala Juan Manuel Guimeráns, presidente de la Spain Film Commission, organización dedicada a atraer rodajes de otras partes del mundo. Esfuerzo que ha dado sus frutos: en las últimas dos décadas han tenido lugar en España rodajes de sagas como Star Wars y Los Juegos del Hambre y series como The Crown o The Walking Dead. Que Hollywood elija España para rodar no es una novedad, ya en los sesenta se rodaron multitud de wésterns, pero puntualiza Guimeráns, ahora ya no desembarcan con todo el equipo humano, sino que contratan empresas y profesionales de una industria local extraordinaria que cada vez es más internacional, valora.

El Gobierno presentó un proyecto en 2021 para convertir al país en un polo de producción audiovisual, inversión internacional y talento. Uno de los elementos centrales del plan eran los incentivos fiscales, de manera, señala Guimeráns, que las productoras extranjeras ahora se encuentran en España una combinación de ahorro fiscal, profesionales especializados y gran variedad de localizaciones. Un estudio de la consultora Olsberg en colaboración con Spain Film Commission señala que el 70% del gasto de las productoras extranjeras hasta 2022 no se habría producido en el país sin esos incentivos. Las empresas que tengan una visión internacional del negocio, añade Segura, de DeAPlaneta Entertainment, tienen más posibilidades de prosperar. “Si empezara hoy, crearía una empresa con visión europea y con presencia en varios territorios”, puntualiza.

Consejos de Empresario La industria española está produciendo más que nunca, una inercia que da la oportunidad a los empresarios de mostrar su trabajo al mundo y hacer crecer el negocio Juan Carlos Tous, cofundador y consejero ejecutivo de Filmin, compañía española de 'streaming' de series y películas

Este dinamismo se ha traducido en un aumento de la capacidad de las empresas españolas para crear contenidos, explica Tous, de Filmin. “La industria está produciendo más que nunca, una inercia que da la oportunidad a los empresarios de mostrar su trabajo al mundo y hacer crecer el negocio”. Ese empuje se observa en la reactivación, tras años de inactividad, de la Ciudad de la Luz, en Alicante, un complejo cinematográfico donde se han rodado taquillazos como El cautivo, de Alejandro Amenábar, y donde Disney filma ahora la adaptación con actores de Enredados. De ese auge también es consecuencia Madrid Content City, un recinto multiempresarial, impulsado en 2025 por el grupo español Secuoya, donde ya se ha instalado Netflix. Ambos complejos destacan por reunir en un mismo recinto empresas de toda la cadena de valor, lo que multiplica las oportunidades de colaboración.

Los ‘youtubers’ son los nuevos creadores

Ignacio Segura, director ejecutivo de DeAPlaneta Entertainment, apunta a un cambio importante en la industria audiovisual: las redes sociales están dejando de ser consideradas como una cantera de aficionados para convertirse en una fuente de talento que Hollywood empieza a tomarse en serio. “Estos creadores de contenido han sido mal vistos en el mundo serio del cine. Ahora dos de los grandes éxitos de este año, Backrooms y Obsession, son responsabilidad de youtubers”, afirma el empresario.

El creador de Backrooms es Kane Parsons, un joven de 20 años que comenzó publicando en la red vídeos sobre espacios laberínticos y desiertos que han acumulado más de 190 millones de visitas. Parsons trasladó aquel ambiente a un largometraje que ha superado en la taquilla al último estreno de Star Wars, The Mandalorian. Obsession está firmada por Curry Barker, 26 años, que se dio a conocer con cortometrajes de terror en YouTube. Rodó su cinta con 750.000 dólares — unos 684.000 euros al cambio actual— y superó los 365 millones de euros en recaudación. Llevar el talento de YouTube a la industria del cine permite probar nuevas ideas y lenguajes con poco presupuesto y contar con creadores que llegan con una audiencia creada, lo que facilita la promoción.

La industria española también cuenta con experimentos de trasvase entre YouTube y el cine, aunque mucho más discretos y menos convencionales. La webserie Malviviendo fue el punto de partida de la carrera como director y productor de David Sainz, que desde entonces ha dirigido tres largometrajes. El youtuber Míster Jägger llevó a la gran pantalla el universo surrealista de sus vídeos y Wismichu presentó en el Festival de Sitges una cinta que consistía en una escena repetida en bucle con la que pretendía provocar al público para grabar sus reacciones.

La IA como vector de crecimiento

La irrupción de la IA está cambiando la manera de crear, producir y distribuir películas y ha abierto debates sobre el futuro de los profesionales y sus derechos. El reto en este sector, indica Guimeráns, va a ser gestionar la propiedad intelectual de todas las creaciones, de la imagen de las personas a los guiones y la música.

Esta tecnología que plantea retos, ya ha sido abrazada por la industria. La IA se emplea a lo largo de toda la cadena de valor, especialmente en la preproducción y la posproducción. No solo sirve para crear imágenes, también se utiliza para gestionar los planes y agilizar procesos al automatizar tareas técnicas.

El proyecto piloto Film Data España, impulsado por la Spain Film Commission, por ejemplo, propone un motor de búsqueda de localizaciones, que será actualizado por los propios usuarios, y que permitirá conocer las características, los servicios del entorno y qué películas ya se han rodado en cada uno de los lugares.

Guimeráns cree que la IA abre nuevas e interesantes vías de negocio a las que los emprendedores deben prestar atención. El estudio El impacto de la IA en la industria audiovisual en España, de la consultora Public First y Google, estima que esta tecnología disruptiva en el audiovisual puede aportar hasta 9.400 millones de euros anuales al producto interior bruto español (PIB) en 2035. Permitirá a los profesionales hacer más en menos tiempo, como señaló Johann Choron, responsable de Alianzas e IA generativa para Cine y Televisión de Google, en el festival de San Sebastián del año pasado, aunque también hará que muchos empleos se transformen.

World.title: El profesor que enseña cocina tradicional a través de las recetas familiares de sus alumnos
World.content:
El chef y docente Ricardo Fernández ha impulsado en el CIFP Carlos Oroza, en Pontevedra, una iniciativa que anima a sus estudiantes de FP a recuperar las elaboraciones culinarias de sus madres, abuelas y vecinas. El objetivo, en línea con el proyecto ‘Gastronomía para una Inmensa Minoría’, es preservar la memoria cultural

En el Centro Integrado de Formación Profesional (CIFP) Carlos Oroza de Pontevedra, los alumnos de la asignatura de Cocina Tradicional recopilan recetas familiares transmitidas de generación en generación. En los últimos siete años han reunido cerca de 600 elaboraciones procedentes de madres, abuelas, vecinas... Además, junto a las instrucciones de preparación, los estudiantes incluyen las historias personales de las mujeres que han compartido sus conocimientos.

El proyecto recoge el testigo de Los recetarios, una iniciativa dedicada a recoger, localizar y digitalizar estos platos tradicionales —especialmente los transmitidos por las mujeres—, con el objetivo de proteger la identidad culinaria de un territorio. El profesor Ricardo Fernández encontró en esa propuesta, creada por periodistas y expertas en gastronomía, una fuente de inspiración y una oportunidad para mostrar a sus alumnos cómo las técnicas y costumbres que han dado forma a la cultura popular ayudan también a comprender la evolución de la cocina.

Fernández, profesor y chef, reflexiona sobre el proyecto junto con los también cocineros Verónica Gómez, formada en el Basque Culinary Center y conocida por su paso por MasterChef; Javier Olleros, fundador del restaurante Culler de Pau, en Reboredo (O Grove, Pontevedra); y Manuel Costiña, responsable de Costiña, en Santa Comba (A Coruña). Los dos últimos, reconocidos con dos estrellas Michelin, destacan la importancia de iniciativas como la que se desarrolla en el CIFP Carlos Oroza. “Son fantásticos para, desde la memoria, preservar y avanzar”, insiste Olleros.

Esta es una de las iniciativas que forman parte de Gastronomía para una Inmensa Minoría, el proyecto impulsado por Cervezas 1906, que nace con el objetivo de poner en valor propuestas auténticas, que no siguen modas, que parten de la tradición para innovar y que son una defensa del territorio y origen. Gracias a su apoyo, las recetas recopiladas en el CIFP Carlos Oroza han podido digitalizarse y ponerse a disposición del público: de este modo, el patrimonio culinario sale del aula y queda disponible para cualquier interesado en conocer o preparar estos platos caseros.

World.title: Muere Miki Espuma, cofundador y creador del universo sonoro de La Fura dels Baus, a los 67 años
World.content:
El músico y cofundador de La Fura dels Baus Miquel Badosa, conocido artísticamente como Miki Espuma, ha muerto a los 67 años. En un comunicado este miércoles, la compañía teatral ha lamentado su muerte y ha apuntado que su trayectoria es “indisociable” de la historia del colectivo y de la construcción de su lenguaje, destacando su mirada musical, su energía creativa y su capacidad para entender el sonido como fuerza escénica. “Hoy, La Fura dels Baus pierde uno de sus pilares creativos. Perdemos un compañero y un amigo. Su música, sin embargo, continuará sonando”, reza el comunicado.

Miki Espuma nació en el barrio de Sant Andreu de Barcelona en 1959, e inició su trayectoria profesional como cantante de rock a los 16 años, incorporándose a La Fura dels Baus como músico y director artístico en 1980. Su aportación fue “esencial” en espectáculos de los inicios de la compañía, como Accions (1984), Suz/o/Suz (1985), Tier Mon (1988), Noun (1990), M.T.M. (1994), Ombra (1997), OBS (2000) y XXX (2002), entre otros. A lo largo de su carrera también firmó composiciones musicales para la Bienal de Valencia de 2001, la conmemoración del 25 aniversario del descubrimiento de las minas de Atapuerca en 2003 o el Mundial de Ciclismo de Mallorca en 2007.

Eel músico y compositor Miquel Badosa Ricart, conocido artísticamente como Miki Espuma, en una foto de archivo. Elvira Urquijo A. (EFE)

Como músico y compositor, Miki Espuma desempeñó un papel decisivo en la definición del universo sonoro de La Fura dels Baus. Su trabajo aunaba rock, música en directo, texturas industriales, voz y ritmo dentro de una misma arquitectura teatral. “La música nunca fue un mero acompañamiento de la acción: se convirtió en un elemento dramático, físico y narrativo, capaz de marcar el pulso de una representación, activar a los intérpretes y transformar la experiencia del público”, señala el comunicado. A lo largo de los años, Miki Espuma desarrolló y dirigió grandes producciones de estilo La Fura en países como India, México, Singapur, Colombia, Portugal, Reino Unido, Australia y Corea del Sur, entre otros. A través de estas creaciones, desarrolló una concepción profundamente personal de los espectáculos de gran formato.

Paralelamente a su trabajo en grandes producciones, Miki Espuma continuó explorando nuevos lenguajes y formatos teatrales. En 2014 creó su propia versión de Histoire du soldat, de Igor Stravinsky, que dio lugar a Temptacions. Ese mismo año dirigió Free Bach 212, un espectáculo-concierto inspirado en la Bauernkantate, BWV 212, de Johann Sebastian Bach, que combinaba música barroca, flamenco, danza y experimentación contemporánea. Con la participación de la cantaora Mariola Membrives y del conjunto barroco Divina Mysteria, el proyecto emprendió un recorrido internacional y dio lugar también a la publicación de un álbum con su banda sonora.

Estas producciones, de carácter más íntimo, mantenían los principios fundamentales de su investigación artística: la intensidad física, la proximidad con el público, la energía musical y el deseo constante de ampliar los límites de la experiencia teatral. “Miki Espuma fue un artista capaz de transitar con naturalidad entre los conciertos, el arte de acción, el teatro físico y las grandes producciones”, recoge el texto publicado en la web de La Fura. Su formación musical, unida a un extraordinario instinto teatral, le permitió crear paisajes sonoros de gran fuerza y transformar la música en una energía generadora de imágenes, movimiento y emoción. “Como cantaba en su canción Koki —tema dedicado a un amigo fallecido—, hoy Miki volverá a reunirse con sus seres queridos. ¡Vuela alto, querido Miki!“, concluye el mensaje.

World.title: Family of man who died in freezer “told not to let him indoors”
World.content:
A 20-year-old man who arrived in the Netherlands as a refugee from Syria has been found dead in a chest freezer in Utrecht.

Police said they were not treating the death of Mohammed al Omar as a crime and believe he may have perished after climbing into the unit outside his family’s house in Timmerstraat. Outdoor temperatures dropped to minus 4.5C in the city overnight.

Mohammed’s family told RTV Utrecht they had been told by support agencies to shut him out of the house because of his issues with drug addiction and mental health, or risk having their other children taken away.

“I came from Syria to bring my children to safety,” his father, Abdulkarim, told the local news network. “Sadly I have lost my eldest child here.”

He fled to the Netherlands with his son six years ago because of the bombings, but Mohammed fell in with “bad friends” and developed psychological and addiction problems.

“We couldn’t accept that we had so many arguments,” Abdulkarim said. “He had financial problems and arguments with others as well. We tried everything, but he wasn’t listening to us any more.”

“Every parent’s nightmare”

He said that social workers warned him not to let Mohammed into the house or they would have his other children removed. “I didn’t know what to do. Either they’d take my other children away or I had to leave Mohammed outside.”

City mayor Sharon Dijksma said the circumstances of Mohammed’s death and the advice given by government agencies would be investigated.

“I think it’s very important in a case like this that we find out exactly who had what role, exactly what did and didn’t happen and what advice was given,” she told NOS.

“I understand extremely well that the parents are very angry and distressed at the moment. Losing your child is the worst thing that can happen to parents. It’s a nightmare.”

World.title: Minister warns meat sector over abuses and attacks on inspectors
World.content:
A growing number of staff at food safety watchdog NVWA no longer want to work at certain Dutch slaughterhouses because of “aggression and violence in the workplace”, junior agriculture minister Silvio Erkens has told MPs.

In a letter to parliament on Tuesday, Erkens said it was “unacceptable” that inspectors faced such conditions while carrying out their legal duties. He added that it made the watchdog’s work harder to plan. He did not name the slaughterhouses involved.

He called on the meat industry to “take concrete measures and show visible leadership” to make abattoirs safe for inspectors, and said he would meet the NVWA and industry body Vlees.nl soon.

The letter was a response to Caroline van der Plas of the farmer-citizen movement BBB, who asked about staff shortages at the NVWA. Meat processor Vion had complained that a lack of inspection was cutting its slaughter capacity.

Erkens said the NVWA was tackling high sick leave, but that some bottlenecks came from slaughterhouses booking more inspection time than they needed.

He also said he was concerned about “persistent occupational risks and abuses” in the meat sector, which the labour inspectorate documented in a report earlier this year.

From March 1, 2028, slaughterhouses and meat processing firms will be banned from using temporary agency staff. Government-commissioned research found that more than a third of the sector’s 37,000 workers are hired through agencies, and over 80% of those agency staff are foreign workers, mainly from Poland and Romania.

Many live in housing arranged by their agency, so losing their job can also mean losing their home. An investigation by Investico and De Groene Amsterdammer this summer found that shelters for homeless migrant workers only admit people judged “motivated” to find new work.

A 34-year-old woman has died after being stabbed while riding her bike in Houten, Utrecht. The victim was attacked by a man passing by her on a fatbike, according to RTV Utrecht.

The incident happened at 8.30am on Wednesday morning. An ambulance and trauma helicopter rushed to the scene after passersby found her seriously injured. She succumbed to her in hospital.

The suspect, a 39-year-old man, initially fled but later turned himself into police. He is being detained. The victim reportedly knew the man, NOS said.

She was riding her bakfiets, and had apparently just dropped off her children at school with it, RTV Utrecht said.

World.title: Silver coins stolen from Dutch shipwreck returned to Australia
World.content:
The Netherlands has returned two coins that were plundered from the wreck of a Dutch colonial ship in Australian waters more than 50 years ago.

The two silver pieces were among a haul of 23 coins that went missing from the wreck of the Zuytdorp, which went down off the coast of Kalbarri, Western Australia in 1712 with the loss of everyone on board.

Divers managed to reach the wreckage, which lies off one of the most inaccessible spots of the Australian coastline, in 1964 and make off with a number of coins.

The Zuytdorp and its contents are classed as heritage property under Australian law and owners need a permit to keep them legally.

Australian police began an international investigation, calling in help from the FBI and Dutch police, to trace the missing silver. They found two of the coins had been sold illegally to a Dutch auction house from a batch of 23 that were in the United States.

Ben van Welzenis, the Dutch embassy’s police attaché, handed them over to Australian police after they were confiscated in the Netherlands. “More than three centuries after the Zuytdorp went down off the coast of Western Australia, her coins are returning to Australia where they belong,” he said.

Shared responsibility

The Netherlands and Australia signed an agreement in 1972 to share responsibility for the wreck of the Zuytdorp as “shared underwater cultural heritage”.

“This return shows what countries can achieve together to preserve our shared heritage for future generations,” said Van Welzenis. The coins will be handed over to the Western Australia Museum in Fremantle for safekeeping.

The loss of the Zuytdorp was not reported immediately when it sank in 1712 because there were no survivors, and it is still not known what caused it to wreck.

The ship was on its way to Batavia, modern-day Jakarta in Indonesia, with around 200 men and around 128,000 guilders’ worth of silver coins on board.

In 1927 a quantity of coins were found washed up on the rocks at the foot of the Zuytdorp Cliffs, which stretch for 200 kilometres along the coast at Kalbarri.

World.title: “Wake-up call” after alcohol-related traffic deaths increase
World.content:
As many as one-third of traffic deaths in the Netherlands involve a driver who was under the influence of alcohol, according to a new study by road safety research bureau SWOV.

Researchers estimate that 180 and 270 people died in collisions where alcohol was a factor, representing between 24% and 35% of all deaths. In one-third of cases the victim was not the driver of the vehicle.

The figures suggest the proportion of alcohol-related deaths is increasing. In the last analysis in 2013 SWOV calculated that between 19% and 28% of road deaths were the result of drink-driving.

At the same time the total number of deaths on the roads has been rising since 2022, after a steady decline between the 1970s and 2010. Last year 759 people died in traffic collisions, the highest number since 2007.

37% of victims were cyclists, 30% were drivers or passengers in vehicles and 8% were on foot. The rest were travelling on motorbikes, mopeds and scooters, or in lorries.

The latest estimates by SWOV also show a rise in the number of people admitted to hospital with injuries sustained in alcohol-related collisions. In 2025 between one-sixth and a quarter of admissions were alcohol-related, compared to up to one-fifth in 2013.

The figures are estimates because Dutch law prevents testing being carried out on the bodies of people who die in traffic collisions, even if they are suspected of drink-driving, because they cannot be prosecuted.

Wake-up call

SWOV researcher Heike Martensen said the figures were “shocking” and a “wake-up call” for politicians and the justice system.

She said more effort needed to be put in to detecting drink-drivers after SWOV found that the proportion of all drivers who had consumed alcohol had risen from 1.7% to 2.3%.

Police have cut back on large-scale roadside breath tests because drivers can use social media to alert each other to their presence, which has reduced their visibility, Martensen told Dutch News.

“The chance of being caught hasn’t gone down, but people’s perception is that the risk is lower,” she said. “If people think the chance is small, the consequences are less effective.”

Alcohol locks

Martensen also called for the government to review direct sanctions such as fitting alcohol locks on cars of people who have been convicted of drink-driving, so that they have to pass a breath test before they can start the engine.

An earlier scheme to enforce the device through court orders was abandoned 10 years ago after judges said it amounted to a “double punishment”. The court also said the high cost of fitting a lock for two years were too punitive for offenders who were unable to afford them.

Martensen said advances in car technology had brought the cost down to the point where all new cars could potentially have the option of fitting an alcohol lock.

“We think it should be re-evaluated. We know from other countries that it is an effective way of preventing people driving under the influence of alcohol.”

Awareness not enough

Fitting alcohol locks as standard on all cars would be the ultimate step, but Martensen admitted that there was no public support for such a move at the moment.

“Look at seatbelts – that problem was solved when cars forced people to wear them,” she said. “Hardly anybody drives without a seatbelt now, so if the car forced you to drive sober it would solve the problem.”

She said awareness campaigns were not enough on their own to change people’s drinking and driving habits. “It’s part of a wider social problem. People who repeatedly drive under the influence often have issues with alcohol addiction,” she said.

“And then you have situations where people have a drink and don’t have any other means of getting home. Having alternative options like public transport is more effective than telling people it’s dangerous to drink and drive.”

World.title: DNB warns AI, cyberattacks and debt could rock financial system
World.content:
The Dutch central bank DNB has issued a new warning that a convergence of risks is posing a severe threat to the country’s financial stability; namely, the power of AI cyberattacks, the possibility of an AI economic bubble, and the fact that only a small number of cybersecurity companies are protecting financial institutions.

At the same time, interest rate rises are putting increasing pressure on government debt.

“The systemic risk lies primarily in the potentially dangerous confluence of shocks, such as cyberattacks, a stock market correction, or the impact of higher interest rates,” DNB president Olaf Sleijpen said in a statement on Tuesday.

“Moreover, the ability to absorb setbacks has diminished now that government fiscal space is limited. As a result, shocks can spread more quickly and widely throughout the financial system.”

There is widespread fear that massive global investments in AI infrastructure could cause an economic downturn. The DNB notes that the Dutch investment exposure here is around €13.5 billion (compared with global AI investment of around $1 trillion this year, according to Goldman Sachs).

While this amount is relatively limited, complex financial structures and the use of leverage (borrowing money to fund investments, which amplifies gains and losses) mean impacts can spread fast and are hard to predict.

Interest rates around the world have risen sharply in recent months, to their highest level since 2000, DNB said. That makes it more expensive for governments to borrow, and harder for countries that are already deep in debt to pay it off.

Governments also have less money to spare for a new crisis than they did during the coronavirus pandemic, the bank said.

DNB said banks, insurers and pension funds should keep investing in protection against cyberattacks and in back-up systems. They should also hold regular crisis drills with other key sectors such as energy and telecoms.

It also called for better crisis planning across Europe and closer ties between EU banking and investment markets, so companies can make more of opportunities such as AI. That, the bank said, will take “political will and courage”.

World.title: MPs vote to remove “remigration” from language of Dutch law
World.content:
Dutch MPs have voted to change the name of the Remigration Act to a more neutral term amid warnings that the term has become a rallying cry for far-right groups.

The law was passed in 1999 to allow benefits to be paid to migrants who return to their country of origin voluntarily, but no claims have been processed since the start of last year.

The English term is widely used on government websites such as the social security bank (SVB) that advise Dutch residents on how to claim benefits.

Security services have warned that “remigration” is increasingly by far-right political parties as a euphemism for enforced deportation.

“If extremist ideas and language are normalised and the boundaries shift, it can have implications for people’s safety,” the intelligence agency AIVD and anti-terrorism co-ordinator NCTV warned in a recent report.

The three coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA supported a motion by the left-wing opposition party Pro on Tuesday that would remove the word “remigration” from the name and text of the 1999 law.

Payments to Syrians

The right-wing party JA21 and independent MP Mona Keijzer tabled a motion calling for the government to start funding the payments again so the law could be reactivated, but the plan was voted down.

The VVD succeeded with a motion to offer Syrians a one-off payment of €10,000 to leave the country if they agree to return home voluntarily.

The government says large areas of Syria are safe to return to, even though the Dutch embassy in Damascus remains closed and the official travel advice says it is “too dangerous“ for visitors because of the “unpredictable” situation.

Parliament also passed a motion by the far-right PVV which would allow dual nationals to have their Dutch passport cancelled if they join proscribed organisations such as Al Qaida or Islamic State.

World.title: Prosecutors demand life sentence for Tarwekamp mastermind
World.content:
Prosecutors have called for a life sentence for the man accused of masterminding the Tarwekamp explosion in The Hague in 2024, which killed six people and collapsed a part of an apartment complex.

The public prosecution service (OM) told the district court on Tuesday that the defendant, Moshtag B., came up with the “insane plan” as revenge against his ex-girlfriend. He sought to blow up the bridal shop she ran on the ground floor of the building, it said.

The OM wants 30 years for Mourad ben T. (31), who they say carried out the attack, and 28 years for his cousin Ilias B. (31), who took part but didn’t come up with the plan. Adil A. (34) faces a possible four-year sentence because he was involved in the plan but pulled out beforehand.

According to the OM, the attack was planned for months in advance. The men allegedly looked up how flammable wedding dresses were and worked out in a group chat how to best burn the shop down. On the day, they used high-powered fireworks and around 175 litres of petrol.

The blast hit the Mariahoeve district at around 6.15am on December 7, 2024. Besides the six who were killed, it also injured five people and left a row of homes in ruins.

Three of the six people who died were from one family: a father (45), a mother (41) and their 17-year-old daughter. Their 8-year-old son was the only one of them pulled alive from the rubble. The others killed were two men aged 44 and 63, who also lived on the Tarwekamp, and a 31-year-old man from Voorburg who was staying with a friend in the building.

Within a fortnight, B. had been identified as the ex-partner of the shop’s owner. Broadcaster NOS reported that he was in London when the explosion happened.

At a pre-trial hearing in March last year, B. told judges he was “so unbelievably sorry”.

NOS said the four men barely reacted when the sentences were read out. Victims’ relatives were split: many thought the demands were tough, but some had hoped for heavier ones.

World.title: Poland plans no-fly zone on eastern border to aid downing of Russian missiles
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland’s defence ministry has announced plans to establish a no-fly zone along the country’s eastern border with the aim of making it easier to shoot down Russian missiles and drones that violate Polish airspace. Meanwhile, foreign minister Radosław Sikorski has again suggested that Poland should be allowed to shoot down Russian missiles that are over Ukraine but heading towards the Polish border. However, the defence ministry acknowledged today that NATO is so far opposed to the idea. Wiceminister obrony Cezary Tomczyk zapowiedział wprowadzenie strefy zakazu lotów przy wschodniej granicy Polski. Jak poinformował minister Tomczyk, rozporządzenie trafiło do rządowego zespołu, strefa ma obejmować od kilkunastu do 50 kilometrów przy granicy wschodniej Polski i ma… pic.twitter.com/3xF68uNNRU — Dariusz Wiewiorka (@darekwiewiorka) November 25, 2026 Speaking on Wednesday at the opening of a new military satellite imaging centre, deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk announced that his department “will request the government to establish a no-fly zone on the country’s eastern border, to ensure Poland’s security”. Tomczyk acknowledged that, after three Russian missiles struck southeastearn Poland last Friday, NATO had offered support, including the deployment of an Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) to Poland. “But at the same time, the Polish military must do everything possible to protect our interests here and now,” he added. The defence ministry recently took one such step by allowing easier identification of objects that can be shot down, said Tomczyk. “The no-fly zone at the state border will be an additional factor supporting the operations of the Polish Air Force.” At a subsequent press briefing, Tomczyk provided more details of the plan. The proposed no-fly zone would stretch for a distance of between “a dozen or a few dozen kilometres from the border”, he said. “When a Polish fighter pilot knows that an aircraft is entering Polish airspace from Ukraine, is flying at a certain altitude and speed, is entering the no-fly zone and is detected on radar, this constitutes grounds for shooting down such an object…We will also urge NATO as a whole to establish such a rule on the eastern flank.” The deputy minister said that a relevant regulation had already been submitted and “will be processed in the coming weeks”. He expressed hope that the measures could be in place by the end of December or in early January. As well as last Friday’s missile strikes, on Monday this week a Russian drone entered Poland from Ukraine and spent a few minutes in Polish airspace. The Polish military had been authorised to fire upon it, but eventually did not do so after it turned back towards the border. Poland is changing the procedures under which its military can fire upon foreign aircraft, citing the "growing threat from Russia". Visual identification of targets will no longer be required, with other forms of data to be used instead https://t.co/foCWsBDazH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 29, 2026 The government’s plans for a no-fly zone were, however, questioned by Mariusz Błaszczak, a former defence minister and now head of the parliamentary caucus of Law and Justice (PiS), the main opposition party. Błaszczak noted that current regulations already allow the introduction of a temporary no-fly zone. He suggested that what the government had announced was simply a “cosmetic measure” and asked what “real operational capabilities” it would provide to the military. Earlier on Wednesday, Bloomberg reported, based on unnamed sources, that Poland had, at a NATO meeting called on Monday to discuss last week’s Russian missile strikes in Poland, asked about the possibility of shooting down Russian missiles that are over Ukraine but heading towards NATO states. Asked about the issue, Tomczyk said that he could not confirm Bloomberg’s reporting, but noted that discussion of shooting down Russian missiles over Ukraine had been going on for months. “NATO is not in favour of this in any way,” said Tomczyk, quoted by broadcaster TVN. “If we want to make any decisions that concern the space over Ukraine, it must always be a decision of the entire NATO…Many months ago NATO decided that such a procedure was out of the question. And that’s where we stand now.” NATO has approved the deployment of an Airborne Warning and Control System to Poland in response to three Russian missiles striking Polish territory last week. Hours after the decision was announced, Poland’s airspace was again violated by a Russian drone https://t.co/gudQJsPlQ5 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 24, 2026 On Wednesday morning, before Bloomberg’s report had been published, Sikorski, the foreign minister, was asked during an interview with Polskie Radio about the idea of shooting down missiles over Ukraine before they reached Poland. “A missile or drone approaching our airspace already poses a direct threat to us, so I believe that shooting [it] down over Ukraine at Ukraine’s request would fall within the definition of self-defence,” said Sikorski. However, he acknowledged that any such policy would need to be agreed by NATO. As far back as 2024, Poland proposed the idea of shooting down Russian missiles over Ukrainian territory. But it was rejected by NATO, whose then-secretary general, Jens Stoltenberg, said that it would risk NATO “becoming part of the conflict”. World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
