World.title: US unveils tariffs on EU, China and others over ‘unfair’ trade
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on the European Union, China and a dozen other countries over their alleged unfair economic practices, threatening renewed tensions with both friends and foes via President Donald Trump’s trade war.

The proposal follows a months-long investigation into excess manufacturing capacity and production, launched days after the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s previous slew of tariffs.

The duties range up to 20 percent and face a period of public comment before taking effect, at the earliest in January.

A senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, noted that the proposals seek to take existing trade deals into account.

The new levies target some of the largest US trading partners, including China, the European Union, India, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.

China is among the countries facing the highest 20-percent tariff, but US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the new levies were within the bounds of existing trade negotiations with Beijing.

“China understands that we’re going to have some level of tariffs. This falls within that understanding,” he told US broadcaster CNBC, adding that the US was offering China exemptions on around $30 billion of goods.

The EU said it rejected the premise of new tariffs and expected Washington to stick by a deal struck with Brussels last year.

“The EU and the US share a real concern about global overcapacity, much of it state-driven and concentrated in third countries. We regret the lack of joint action,” European Commission spokesman Olof Gill said.

China’s foreign ministry, responding to a question about the new levies before they were officially announced, warned Washington not to engage in “tariff wars and trade wars.”

Not stacked on deals

Vietnam also faces a proposed 20-percent tariff; Cambodia and Indonesia 18 percent; and India 17 percent, according to the USTR’s office.

Partners like the EU, Korea and Taiwan, which have signed earlier trade deals, will see tariffs broadly capped at 15 percent.

In a separate announcement, USTR also proposed additional tariffs on goods from Brazil, including aircraft, over alleged inaction on addressing US trade concerns.

The Brazilian president’s office called the tariffs “unacceptable” and said Brazil would “not yield to this type of threat.”

Trump’s tariffs have targeted Washington’s friends and foes alike, and are part of a push in his second term to remake global trade by forcing countries to buy US products or produce their goods in his country.

With Trump preparing to host G20 leaders in Miami next month, the senior US official rejected the notion that the new tariffs could cause tensions at the summit.

“We actually expect that we may be signing more agreements at the G20 in the wake of these announcements,” the official said.

Inflation pressures

Overcapacity concerns affect a range of sectors, from batteries to cement, chemicals to processed food, the senior US official said.

The duties could add further pressure on US businesses already squeezed by earlier tariffs, with firms now likelier to pass on expenses to consumers already frustrated with the high cost of living.

Affordability was a key issue in recent US midterm elections, which saw Trump’s Republican Party swept out of power in both chambers of Congress by Democrats.

The US Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge also came in at a three-year high in October.

Fed policymakers, responsible for keeping inflation to a long-term two-percent target, say that most price effects of Trump’s previous tariff rollout have passed through the economy — but any new levies could push prices up further.

‘Hollowing out’

Trade lawyer Ryan Majerus told AFP that he expected this probe to be among “the most important” actions for the Trump administration, given its underlying concern that factories with excess capacity start operations abroad and “never get turned off, even if there’s no demand.”

This potentially leads to an oversupply of goods, depressed prices and a “hollowing out” of US manufacturing, he added.

While the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s global tariffs in February, his sector-specific duties remain intact.

The new tariffs will not stack on top of those sector-specific tariffs on items like automobiles and steel, the senior US official said.

In July, Trump imposed a separate wave of tariffs on 60 economies, accusing them of insufficient action against forced labor.

For economies facing both the forced labor and excess production tariffs, the levies would not stack, the US official said. Instead, the higher rate of the two would prevail.

World.title: Spanish artist Julio Lafuente’s sculptures help define Jeddah’s visual identity
World.content:
JEDDAH: Around 30 art installations by Spanish artist and architect Julio Lafuente adorn the streets and squares of Jeddah, serving as visual landmarks deeply embedded in the memories of residents and visitors alike. Over the decades, these works have helped shape the aesthetic identity of the “Bride of the Red Sea,” turning the city into an open-air art gallery that blends artistic expression with the authenticity of its local environment.

Lafuente’s creations accounted for the largest share of the “Beautification of Jeddah” project, launched in the 1970s. Beyond their aesthetic appeal, the sculptures served a practical purpose as navigational markers and reference points, much like digital maps do today. Over time, they have become iconic landmarks closely associated with the city.

Since beginning his collaboration with Jeddah Municipality in the mid-1970s, Lafuente produced a diverse collection of artworks rich in symbolism and meaning. Using materials sourced from the local environment, he reinforced the connection between the sculptures, their surroundings, and the collective memory of residents and visitors.

Among his most notable works is the “Bicycle” sculpture, a familiar Jeddah landmark distinguished by its striking design and massive iron structure, which stands 15 meters tall. Located north of King Abdulaziz Road, the globe sculpture, made of glass and colored concrete, symbolizes Makkah’s central position in the Islamic world. Meanwhile, four lantern sculptures along Al-Andalus Road evoke the beauty and authenticity of traditional Mamluk-era lamps.

Lafuente’s works explore diverse artistic themes with cultural and religious dimensions. One sculpture, oriented toward the Grand Mosque, combines marble lines and geometric forms to express Islamic identity. Another, featuring a Quranic verse, brings together marble, bronze, and Arabic calligraphy, reflecting the artist’s understanding of local culture and his ability to translate it into artistic expression.

His work also carries a public-awareness message. The “Reckless Speed” sculpture features five actual cars embedded in a concrete cube, warning of the dangers of speeding and reckless driving. Lafuente’s architectural contributions include the design of the former Literary Club building in Jeddah, which now houses the Saudi Arabian Society for Culture and Arts.

Lafuente’s works remain a testament to a significant chapter in Jeddah’s urban beautification journey. They have become an integral part of the city’s visual identity and collective memory, passed down through generations while reflecting its artistic and cultural heritage, beauty, and authenticity.

World.title: Cardamom ad sparks clash between Bollywood star, Indian food regulator
World.content:
NEW DELHI: An  for cardamom is at the center of a legal spat between a Bollywood actor and India’s most prominent food commissioner, with a court ruling set to shape how far companies can go in indirectly advertising brands whose promotion is restricted.

India restricts advertising for liquor and tobacco but officials have for years also frowned upon the use of indirect means, called surrogate advertising, by companies in such sectors promoting their brands in the guise of sodas, water or glassware.

While companies say these are genuine businesses in their own right whose advertising cannot be curbed, health officials say the s are aimed at generating recall of the parent brand whose publicity ‌is restricted. Since ‌2024, India has been trying to finalize stringent guidelines to prohibit such s ​outright.

In ‌the ⁠case involving ​Bollywood ⁠stars, actor Ajay Devgn has sued the food authority of Maharashtra state, arguing he has been wrongly told to stop appearing in s for Vimal cardamom packs, according to a non-public court filing dated October 15 reviewed by Reuters.

The state, whose food safety commissioner Tukaram Mundhe has become a national sensation for his aggressive stance on public health, asked Bollywood stars Devgn, Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff in August to stop appearing in s promoting Vimal cardamom, arguing the brand is mostly known for its betel nut mix, or pan masala, which is banned in the state.

The spat in the High ⁠Court in Mumbai could set a precedent, New Delhi-based lawyer Anuj Tiwari said. “The ‌case will test both the fairness of the department’s process before it ‌imposes restrictions... and the parameters for deciding what counts as indirect advertising,” he ​said.

Court spat on cardamom ad

In the  available ‌on Vimal Cardamom’s YouTube page and posted two years ago, the Bollywood stars are seen celebrating, throwing saffron at ‌each other after Devgn consumes the product. The Hindi-language  has 107 million views, while clips dubbed in other Indian languages have garnered millions more.

“Ajay, Shahrukh, and Tiger played saffron Holi like crazy and drenched the entire community in saffron!” says the ’s description, referring to the Hindu festival of color.

Devgn in his filing argues cardamom has not been prohibited in the state and “there is ‌no bar in endorsing a product which is not prohibited.”

Devgn did not respond to Reuters queries. Mundhe told Reuters the state believes the s are against public health ⁠interests, and the state ⁠is separately reviewing responses submitted by Khan and Shroff, although Reuters could not ascertain details of their submissions.

Dushyant Mahant, a lawyer for PB Agro, which holds the license to make Vimal cardamom and pan masala, told Reuters the allegations were futile as the company does not promote Vimal in Maharashtra and only advertises the product via nationally televised broadcasts that cannot be restricted geographically.

Industry estimates show India’s pan masala market was worth around $5 billion last year. Health experts say the product is a leading cause of oral fibrosis that often progresses to oral cancer.

While Maharashtra bans it, Vimal’s tobacco-free pan masala sachets in other states cost around 5 rupees (5.4 US cents). But they are often consumed with chewing tobacco, sold at kiosks as “twin packs” — a pan masala sachet alongside a tiny pouch of unbranded tobacco.

An adverse ruling in Devgn’s case could affect Bollywood stars as endorsements can amount to up to 30 percent of an ​actor’s earnings, and promoting tobacco-linked products is more lucrative than ​other s, said Suresh Mathew, a Mumbai-based screenwriter.

“Most actors know if a product is a surrogate for another product,” he added. “There are cases where certain actors have refused to lend their name to a product that they feel is harmful.”

World.title: Nvidia CEO’s comeback fuels debate over misogyny and impunity for the rich and powerful
World.content:
NEW YORK: Just over a year ago, the chief executive officer of an Ohio tech company was forced to resign when he was caught on video embracing an employee at a Coldplay concert. The CEO of McDonald’s was among several pushed out over a consensual relationship at the height of the #MeToo movement.

Now the stunning reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang despite similar allegations of sexual misconduct is fueling fears of a resurgence of impunity for the rich and powerful.

Huang resigned from Nvidia after he admitted to having an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, and following reports that he was involved with a second woman who was his subordinate. Huang has acknowledged that he violated the company’s code of conduct, which warns against personal relationships that may create conflicts of interest.

But in an extraordinary turnaround following a pressure campaign from Huang’s tech allies and President Donald Trump, Nvidia’s board voted unanimously Monday to reinstate him. The board said it had received assurances from the US government that Huang was not a national security concern, but there was no mention of the sexual misconduct allegations at the center of the scandal.

Trump, however, did address Huang’s personal conduct

The president, who has a history of marital infidelity and has faced allegations of sexual assault he says are false, predicted the scandal would only help Huang’s reputation.

“Sex sells, fellas,” Trump declared in an interview on CNBC.

He also posted a doctored image of Huang raising a red bra in triumph, a pose that parodied a famous photograph of Trump himself moments after he survived a 2024 assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request by The Associated Press for comment Wednesday.

‘Horrible message to men everywhere’

Trump’s response reinforces the impression “that there is a class of men who see violence against women, coercion of women as a currency of power,” said Cheyenne Hunt, an attorney who founded the advocacy group Reckoning Action after her role in bringing to light the sexual assault allegations that brought down Democratic Sen. Eric Swalwell and Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner.

“This sends a horrible message to men everywhere that it’s open season on their direct reports,” Hunt said.

Randall Peterson, a professor of organizational behavior at the London Business School, said the #MeToo movement had reinforced the idea that company leaders who engage in relationships with subordinates “are in serious trouble because you cannot rule out coercion. You just cannot.”

Peterson said the messaging now is that “you are at risk, as in the days before #MeToo.”

“I’m sad about that,” he said. “I thought we had moved on from that.”

An apologetic but jubilant comeback

Huang, for his part, apologized to his employees a day after returning to Nvidia, saying he had made mistakes and was in daily therapy, according to a livestreamed meeting reviewed by The New York Times. He also warned that his reinstatement didn’t mean other employees could violate the company’s code of conduct, saying that “sometimes, it’s appropriate to forgive” and “sometimes it’s not.”

He also addressed a report by The Times about his management style that included publicly berating and threatening violence against employees. He acknowledged he had sometimes gone too far and promised that the company’s human resources department would henceforth collect feedback about his conduct.

The saga, however, has “made very clear that Huang is untouchable,” said Ann Lipton, a University of Colorado Boulder law professor who specializes in corporate and securities law.

“It suggests that if you’ve had a certain amount of success, then you should be able to get away with pretty much whatever you want,” Lipton said.

That’s especially true in the male-dominated tech industry, she added, citing Meta founder Mark Zuckerberg’s comment last year that corporate culture needed more “masculine energy.”

The Nvidia scandal has brought scrutiny to the independence of its 10-member board and a corporate culture centered around hero-worshiping its celebrity CEO.

Thousands of people, including former and current employees, had signed a petition calling for Huang’s return. Nvidia’s collapsing stock had fueled fears that the AI bubble would pop and, for Huang supporters, bolstered their argument that his vision, connections and deal-making skills were indispensable to the entire industry.

Nvidia’s shares rocketed up 31.5 percent upon his reinstatement on Monday — although they have since fallen — and employees chanted Huang’s name as he returned to headquarters. The company did not respond to requests for comment for this story.

Freada Kapor Klein, an investor and activist in equity and access issues around tech, said Nvidia and other successful tech startups “become cult-like. And people get addicted almost to being part of this inside powerful club.”

While America has a history of industries idolizing big names like Henry Ford or Andrew Carnegie, tech culture adds to that by “glorifying geniuses. And so there is something extra special about technological prowess, more than or on top of just business success,” Klein said.

Speaking up in the face of impunity

Women make up just 21 percent of Nvidia’s global workforce and an even smaller share of its managers and leaders, according to the company’s latest sustainability report, which touts its efforts to achieve gender pay parity as well as establish employee resource groups for women and other groups, and family-supporting policies such as generous paid parental leave.

The company’s code of conduct, meanwhile, says employees “must report” suspected violations and offers extensive guidelines and reassurances about protection against retaliation.

Huang’s triumphant return, however, is exactly the sort of outcome that silences victims of sexual misconduct, said Fatima Goss Graves, president and CEO of the National Women’s Law Center, which runs the Time’s Up Legal Defense Fund, a program to support workers facing sexual harassment.

Still, she said the legacy of the #MeToo movement continues to inspire women to speak out about sexual harassment and misconduct, adding that public scandals like the one at Nvidia sometimes provoke outrage that leads to an uptick in complaints to Time’s Up and other organizations.

Goss Graves noted that on the same day Huang was reinstated, Democratic Rep. Jimmy Gomez of California resigned from Congress after the House Ethics Committee released a report finding “substantial evidence” that he made unwelcome sexual advances toward a House staffer and subjected the staffer to unwanted sexual contact, the latest in a string of lawmakers or candidates brought down by misconduct allegations in recent months.

Meanwhile, Trump’s role in getting Huang’s job back drew immediate bipartisan fire and the CEO is expected to testify next week before the Senate Banking Committee.

“What comes next really matters,” Goss Graves said. “If everybody shrugs their shoulders and says some people are too important to be held accountable, then we will have a problem.”

World.title: US approves sale of F-16 maintenance equipment to Ukraine
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The US has approved the sale of maintenance equipment and other items to Ukraine for its fleet of F-16 fighter jets, a transaction worth $622 million financed by European partners, the State Department announced Wednesday.

The funding comes from Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands and Norway, the State Department said in a statement, underlining that “there will be no US funds associated with this transfer.”

It said the package includes “Cartridge Actuated Device/Propellant Actuated Devices; lab equipment; and transportation support,” which will be added to a smaller previous sale below the limit required to be reported to Congress.

“The proposed sale will improve Ukraine’s capability to meet current and future threats by further equipping it to conduct self-defense and regional security missions with a more robust air defense capability,” the statement said.

The Wall Street Journal reported in early October that delays in maintenance and a shortage of parts had grounded more than half of Ukraine’s fleet, and all of its US-made aircraft could be affected by year-end.

Ukrainian officials denied there were any dire issues with aircraft availability, but admitted that certain components for the F-16s were no longer in production and harder to source.

Kyiv pushed its Western allies for it to be given advanced fighter jets after Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022 and finally received its first batch of F-16s two years later.

World.title: UKMTO reports explosion near tanker west of Dubai
World.content:
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said it had received a report of an ‌explosion caused ‌by an ‌unknown projectile near a tanker 50 nautical miles west of Dubai in the UAE on ‌Thursday.

The ‌tanker’s master ‌reported the ‌explosion, but the vessel sustained no damage and ‌there was no environmental impact, UKMTO said in an advisory note, adding all crew members were safe and accounted for.

World.title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
World.content:
The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-lofty goal of Elon Musk’s rocket company, in a move that has raised both skepticism and alarm among some scientists.

The US Federal Communications Commission lauded its authorization as a historic first amid the artificial intelligence race. It said that SpaceX’s one million “orbital compute modules” (forming a data center constellation called “Starmind”) would process massive amounts of data that would be used back on Earth — and bring humans closer to harnessing “the full power of the sun.”

“America is leading the world into the era of super intelligence,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, who was appointed by Republican President Donald Trump, said in a statement. He added that Wednesday’s move “opens a bold new frontier.”

A lengthier authorization order published by the FCC noted that the company must deploy at least “one authorized space station” by 2033 — and then gradually add more and more through 2040. Musk welcomed the decision over social media.

The world’s richest man has long vowed to form vast, solar-powered data centers in space to help run AI tools on Earth. But scientists and industry experts have stressed enormous technical and financial obstacles, as well as a host of environmental concerns.

Adam Becker, an astrophysicist and author, called the prospect of launching a million satellites into space to create data centers “a fantasy.”

“It’s not going to happen,” he said Wednesday.

Proponents of data centers in space argue that capturing the sun’s energy would ease pressure on power grids and cut demand for sprawling computing warehouses on Earth (and resources like water needed to cool them). Space seems to offer a solution because it is cold, but it is also a vacuum, trapping heat inside objects much like a thermos. Becker explained that there are “basic physical limits” to otherwise radiating that heat out — and sending lots of smaller satellites could potentially carry the necessary material combined, but it would be expensive and difficult.

He and others also point to additional risks, such as atmospheric pollution through launches and reentries, as well as possible in-orbit collisions that could impact other essential satellites.

“You could end up with a cascading set of space junk collisions,” said Becker, noting such crashes could create “a cloud of debris” in the low Earth orbit — where many weather and telecommunication satellites are also found.

In its ruling, the FCC maintained that SpaceX’s proposed Starmind constellation operates consistently with its orbital debris rules. It also acknowledged that it had received a “substantial number” of public comments leading up to its authorization Wednesday, including petitions to deny SpaceX’s request. But the regulator maintained that deploying the satellites “serves the public interest” — and said that it dismissed topics that it didn’t have authority over, such as environmental concerns.

The American Astronomical Society, satellite communication company Viasat and Amazon-owned Kuiper Systems were among those who called on the regulator to deny SpaceX’s proposed data centers in space.

In a statement Wednesday, the AAS said it was “disheartened and dismayed” by the FCC’s decision. The organization said that SpaceX’s proposed position of data centers in low Earth orbit would undermine decades of federal investment in astronomical facilities and “the ability of astronomers and the public to enjoy and study the night sky.”

“The proposed constellation involves larger (and therefore brighter) and more numerous objects,” AAS said, noting that “these satellites would therefore be visible as extremely bright objects for longer periods in the night sky.”

Becker echoed that sentiment. “It also is pollution of the night sky to the naked eye,” he said.

Viasat, Amazon, SpaceX and the FCC did not immediately respond to The Associated Press’ requests for further comment Wednesday.

World.title: ‘Decaying Stakes’ examines imprisonment and suffering under Syria’s former regime
World.content:
HOMS: A theatrical production in the central Syrian city of Homs is revisiting one of the darkest chapters in the country’s modern history, exploring political repression, imprisonment and human suffering under the deposed regime during the 1980s.

The play, “Decaying Stakes,” was staged at the Palace of Culture as part of the 26th Homs Theater Festival, organized by the Syrian Artists Syndicate in cooperation with the Homs Directorate of Culture.

Playwright Mowaffaq Qara Hassan told SANA that the production examines the erosion of political life under the military rule of the deposed regime, exploring how repression, enforced silence and imprisonment shaped Syrian society in the decades leading up to the outbreak of the Syrian revolution in 2011.

Director Omar Awany said the narrative follows two characters from contrasting ideological backgrounds, a Marxist communist and a man with a religious background, who are brought together by their shared experience of imprisonment.

Through their stories, the production revisits a series of historical events culminating in the 1982 Hama massacre.

The play premiered at the Syria Theater Festival in Aleppo before making its second festival appearance in Homs.

Awany said the Homs performance holds particular personal and artistic significance, carrying forward the legacy of his father, Tammam Awany, who contributed to the festival as a playwright, director and member of its organizing committee.

Suffering beyond ideological divides

Actor Mohammad Khabbaz, who plays Wael, said the production highlights the abuses endured by Syrians in the prisons of the deposed regime, portraying suffering that transcended political and ideological differences.

He stressed that the violence spared no one, noting that the play’s closing line, “What happened was far worse,” captures a scale of suffering that remains difficult to comprehend.

The 26th Homs Theater Festival continues to showcase diverse productions exploring Syria’s collective memory, using theater as a platform to address humanitarian, social and political issues while encouraging public dialogue on defining moments in the country’s history.

World.title: Iraq in discussions with Apple to activate Apple Pay
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi authorities are holding official talks with Apple to introduce Apple Pay in Iraq as part of a broader push to expand digital payment services.

Head of the Communications and Media Commission (CMC) Baligh Abu-Kallal said in early November that Iraq is negotiating with Apple over launching Apple Pay, privacy policies, and gaming sector cooperation.

In August, Iraq accredited Apple as a verified digital platform, covering services such as the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, Apple Arcade, and Apple Ads under local regulations.

Abu-Kallal stated that launching Apple Pay depends on completing technical, legal, and financial procedures, local news outlet Shafaq News reported.

Iraqi banks have also signaled interest in digital wallet expansion amid wider banking modernization and digital payment reforms.

Earlier in July, an Iraqi government source mentioned that the committee in charge of activating Apple Pay services met with Apple’s regional managers to make the service accessible in Iraq.

The initiative is part of the Iraqi government’s efforts to enhance the electronic payment infrastructure and boost the adoption of modern technology, thereby fostering financial inclusion and advancing digital transformation.

Iraq aims to make Apple Pay available to users, in accordance with the government’s strategy to expand the online payment sector and support the transition to a digital economy.

World.title: Iraq expands digital services for Iraqi Airways
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport has expanded digital services for Iraqi Airways to facilitate passenger travel and reduce airport congestion.

Travelers can complete check-in procedures and issue their electronic boarding passes online before arriving at the airport.

Passengers can also choose their preferred seats in advance during booking or check-in.

Users can now electronically change their flight schedules and destinations without visiting a sales office.

The airline enhanced its electronic reservation and online payment systems for both domestic and international flights.

A new pricing structure lets passengers select different fare classes with varying baggage allowances and modification terms.

Passengers can use these services through the Iraqi Airways official website or via the mobile app.

The step is part of the company’s strategy to grow its digital capabilities, improve passenger experience, and stay up with the latest standards in the aviation industry.

The service generally opens for check-in between 48 and 24 hours before the scheduled flight departure and closes up to two hours prior to takeoff.

World.title: Iraq’s judiciary rules that Baghdad can deploy forces along all borders
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Federal Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday that the federal government in Baghdad can deploy troops to secure all international borders, including those in Iraqi Kurdistan.

The decision backs Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s push to assert central control over border crossings and oil fields across the country.

The court affirmed federal jurisdiction over international borders, customs oversight, and the auditing of oil and gas fields, while allowing shared management with regional authorities and provinces.

Ali al-Zaidi ordered federal takeovers of Kurdish-run border crossings and disputed oil fields following an oil smuggling investigation. The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) described the moves as constitutional violations and military threats, calling instead for dialogue.

The crackdown, which also targets militias with ties to Iran, is seen by analysts as part of Zaidi’s larger effort to consolidate power. As a result, the Supreme Judicial Council has called on all parties to uphold the 2005 constitution.

A day earlier, al-Zaidi ordered federal authorities to take control of all border crossings in Iraqi Kurdistan and directed the Oil Ministry to manage oilfields under Kurdish security control in Diyala, Kirkuk, Salah al-Din, and Nineveh provinces.

The KRG was instructed to approve crude oil and petroleum product exports only through the federal Oil Ministry.

The directives followed an investigation into smuggling at the state-run North Oil Company and a wider campaign against illicit oil networks—including alleged smuggling in Jurf al-Sakhar linked to the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah group, which denied the accusation.

World.title: Iraq presses OPEC+ to raise oil output
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is pushing OPEC+ to raise its estimated crude oil production capacity ahead of the group’s scheduled meeting on November 29 to set 2027 output quotas.

Baghdad rejected preliminary findings from OPEC+’s independent capacity review—conducted by consultant DeGolyer and MacNaughton—which put Iraq’s capacity at 4.9 million barrels per day, according to Reuters.

OPEC+’s review estimated Iraq’s sustainable production capacity at approximately 4.9 million barrels per day. However, Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair contends that Iraq can achieve a capacity of 5.2 million barrels per day.

Additionally, there are broader efforts within Iraq aimed at increasing this figure even further to support a larger production allowance.

Iraq’s current OPEC+ production limit stands at 4.43 million barrels per day. In OPEC’s November report, Iraq reported October output at 4.88 million barrels per day, while OPEC’s external secondary sources estimated it lower at 4.49 million barrels per day.

Capacity figures serve as a key benchmark for calibrating member quotas in 2027. Higher capacity estimates strengthen a member’s case to pump more oil or claim a larger share of group output.

To restore its economy and meet its financial obligations, Baghdad is looking for more oil earnings. Iraq threatened to leave OPEC earlier in 2026 due to the capacity assessment, but it subsequently dropped the threat when the UAE left OPEC and OPEC+ in May 2026 to increase output.

World.title: Iraq foils oil smuggling operations in Dhi Qar, Kirkuk
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi National Security Service (INSS) announced on Wednesday that it foiled oil smuggling operations across Dhi Qar and Kirkuk provinces.

The actions are part of a wider government crackdown led by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi against illicit oil trade and pipeline tampering.

Security forces uncovered an illegal tap on an oil pipeline in the al-Luhays area, which is administratively part of Basra province. Three hoses connected to illicitly installed valves were siphoning crude oil into tanker trucks.

With judicial authorization, INSS units intercepted and seized a vehicle illegally modified with side openings to offload fuel. Kerosene was found inside its tank, and a suspect was arrested.

Earlier in the week, Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council reported an organized crude oil smuggling ring using tankers near the Dhi Qar–Basra border, leading to detentions of a suspect and several Energy Police officers.

A committee completed fieldwork investigating alleged smuggling of Kirkuk oil through Iraqi Kurdistan toward Iran and Afghanistan.

The operations follow recent security deployments in Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, in Babil province and arrests related to pipeline breaches in Najaf.

World.title: Kata’ib Hezbollah retains core Jurf Al Sakhar stronghold and absorbs 2,000 fighters into state payroll
World.content:
Bahjdad (IraqiNews.com) – Five days after federal security forces entered Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr), informed sources revealed to Al-Mada newspaper—in a report on Wednesday, November 25, 2026—that the military operation has produced no substantive change to the balance of power on the ground.

According to the report, Kata’ib Hezbollah retains full control over the town center and its vital surrounding perimeter, including the areas of Abd Ways, Al-Farsiya, Al-Hujayr, and Al-Fadhiliya.

No federal security forces have entered this core perimeter—referred to by insiders as the “Kata’ib Hezbollah Square”—and the newly inaugurated joint control headquarters remains situated outside Jurf al-Sakhar’s administrative boundaries.

Rather than retreating, the faction utilized the official deployment announcement to absorb more than 2,000 of its previously off-roster fighters into the official payroll of the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF/Hashd al-Shaabi) under the 72nd and 79th Brigades, shifting their financial burden onto the state budget while securing institutional cover and legal immunity.

Field accounts indicate that the federal deployment touted by Baghdad was largely confined to peripheral sectors and routine troop rotations:

Iraqi Army: Deployment was restricted to the 38th Brigade of the 10th Division along the northwestern edge of Jurf al-Sakhar toward Anbar’s Amiriyat al-Fallujah axis and the canal linking Lake Habbaniyah to Lake Razzaza west of Karbala.

Federal Police: The only state force maintaining direct contact with Kata’ib Hezbollah zones simply rotated existing positions, replacing the 16th Brigade with the 17th and 11th Brigades without advancing into faction-held territory.

Counter-Terrorism Service (CTS): No CTS units deployed inside Jurf al-Sakhar, aside from a Karbala provincial regiment stationed at the garrison camp in Musayyib district outside the subdistrict’s borders.

Meanwhile, informed sources noted that Kata’ib Hezbollah leveraged the publicized “withdrawal” to execute a wide-scale military redeployment, transferring substantial weaponry and equipment to establish new positions in western Anbar and western Karbala in anticipation of a potential renewed military confrontation between the United States and Iran, while Iranian and Houthi advisors remain active inside Jurf al-Sakhar.

Political observers cited by Al-Mada suggest Tehran and allied factions orchestrated a nominal concession in northern Babylon—long targeted by Washington as a financial artery for Iran—in order to open a new security and political front against the Kurdistan Region.

According to these assessments, Tehran is pressing Baghdad to obtain a list of Iranian Kurdish opposition members residing in Kurdistan and relocate them to Samawah in southern Iraq to neutralize their potential involvement in any U.S.-Iran conflict.

This geopolitical maneuvering coincides with Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi’s announcement on Tuesday of heightened anti-smuggling measures around the Kurdistan Region’s perimeter, alongside Erbil’s denial of rumors regarding federal troop deployments inside the region or a return to the 1991 “Blue Line.”

Simultaneously, allies of Al-Zaidi view the nationwide crackdown on oil pipeline tapping as leverage to prosecute and imprison leaders of defiant armed factions by choking off illicit revenue streams. The anti-smuggling drive took a sharp political turn after Najaf MP Abdul-Hadi Al-Hasnawi stated that a farm implicated in oil pipeline tampering in Najaf belongs to the Harakat al-Nujaba militia rather than a private family, following arrest warrants issued for two of his brothers.

In Erbil, former Kurdistan Parliament member Abdul-Salam Barwari warned that actors implicated in Jurf al-Sakhar’s illicit economy are attempting to deflect scrutiny by manufacturing crises around the Kurdistan Region—effectively signaling that oil theft is not confined to northern Babylon.

While characterizing Al-Zaidi’s official rhetoric on state monopoly over weapons as generally measured, Barwari cautioned that commentary from aligned media and activists revives a 2017 Kirkuk-style mentality hostile to Iraq’s constitutional federalism, seeking to exploit internal Kurdish political tensions following the recent reactivation of the Kurdistan Parliament.

World.title: Turkey highlight urgent European demand for Development Road at Baghdad Transport Expo
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Transport Wahab Salman Al-Hasani announced on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, that Iraq is reclaiming its economic role as a vital transit bridge between East and West through an integrated infrastructure vision linking seaports, airports, railways, and highways, while Turkish Minister of Transport and Infrastructure Abdulkadir Uraloğlu revealed that European officials inquire daily with mounting urgency about the completion timeline for the Iraq-Turkey Development Road project.

Speaking during the opening of the Iraq International Exhibition and Conference for Transport, Airports, and Logistics at the Baghdad International Fairground.

Al-Hasani stated that the Ministry of Transport is modernizing its operational systems to convert Iraq’s strategic geography into an engine of economic strength.

He highlighted major milestones in southern Iraq, noting that core components of the Grand Faw Port are nearing completion as Iraq’s maritime gateway to global markets, reinforced by the recent inauguration of the Khor al-Zubair immersed tunnel to shorten transport distances and connect ports to inland road networks.

Al-Hasani confirmed that the strategic Development Road project has reached advanced stages in its engineering designs, establishing an overland economic corridor linking the Arabian Gulf to Europe via Iraq and Turkey to diversify national revenue, attract investment partnerships, and generate employment.

Alongside maritime and rail infrastructure, he noted that the ministry is upgrading air navigation systems, modernizing domestic airports, and expanding Iraqi Airways’ international route network to elevate aviation safety and global connectivity.

Addressing the conference alongside international partner firms and diplomatic envoys, Turkish Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloğlu underscored that disruptions in global supply chains have made diversifying transport routes and enhancing corridor efficiency critical.

Positioning the Middle East at the crossroads of Asia, Europe, and Africa, Uraloğlu stated that complementing Turkey’s existing East–West transit lines with a North–South axis through Iraq’s Grand Faw Port creates an unprecedented commercial and logistics artery between Asia and Europe.

Uraloğlu emphasized that the success of the Development Road depends not only on physical rail and highway construction, but also on streamlining border crossings, accelerating customs procedures, and implementing digital transformation across transit networks so borders function as gateways rather than barriers.

Offering the international expertise of Turkey’s engineering and contracting sectors to support Iraq’s infrastructure rollout, he concluded by noting that European officials contact Ankara every day persistently asking when the Development Road will be completed—a testament, he said, to how recent developments in Europe have validated the corridor’s strategic necessity.

World.title: US dollar edges higher across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged slightly higher across major domestic parallel markets on Wednesday morning, November 25, 2026, with purchasing bids hovering near the 169,000-dinar threshold in key commercial centers after briefly testing the 168,000-dinar range earlier in the week.

According to morning market figures, physical banknote rates opened across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra with notable regional spreads.

In Baghdad, currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 169,250 IQD against buying offers of 168,750 IQD per $100.

In Erbil, currency desks recorded the sharpest uptick, quoting retail selling rates at 169,950 IQD—just 50 dinars shy of the 170,000-dinar mark—alongside purchasing bids of 169,700 IQD per $100.

In Basra, foreign exchange offices posted retail selling rates at 169,750 IQD and buying offers at 169,250 IQD per $100.

Wednesday’s modest rebound keeps parallel market rates trading roughly 17,250 to 17,950 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official cash rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar)—a spread of approximately 11.3% above the official rate, down slightly from the wider gap recorded at the start of the trading week.

World.title: 'Zero tolerance for terrorism': EAM Jaishankar remembers 26/11 victims on attack anniversary
World.content:
NEW DELHI: External affairs minister

on Thursday paid tribute to the victims of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, remembering the innocent lives lost and the security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice while fighting the terrorists.

Marking 18 years since the attacks that shook the country, Jaishankar reiterated India's commitment to combating

in all its forms and bringing those responsible to justice.

"Remember innocent lives lost & salute the brave security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice during 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks. Committed to combating terrorism in all its forms & manifestations and bringing those involved to justice.



Zero tolerance for terrorism," Jaishankar wrote in a post on X.

This year marks 18 years since 10 Pakistan-backed

(LeT) terrorists launched a series of coordinated attacks across Mumbai, targeting some of the city's busiest locations.

Commonly known as 26/11, the attacks began on the night of November 26, 2008, when the terrorists entered Mumbai by sea. Over the next four days, they carried out strikes at several locations, killing 166 people and injuring around 300.





Among the targets were the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, the Oberoi-Trident Hotel, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Nariman House, Cama Hospital, Metro Cinema and Leopold Cafe. Several of these locations were frequented by foreign nationals and Mumbai's workforce.

The attacks left a lasting impact on the city, with the memories of the siege continuing to haunt survivors and families of those killed. Bullet marks at Leopold Cafe and Nariman House, along with memorials honouring the security personnel who lost their lives, remain reminders of the tragedy.

Nine of the 10 terrorists were killed during the security operation, while the lone surviving attacker, Pakistani national Mohammad Ajmal Amir Kasab, was captured. Assistant Sub-Inspector Tukaram Omble played a crucial role in apprehending Kasab before succumbing to his injuries.

Kasab was sentenced to death in May 2010 and hanged at Yerawada Central Prison in Pune on November 21, 2012.

World.title: A commitment to strengthen our Constitution
World.content:
'For crores of Indians, including me, the Constitution of India is an inseparable part of our life journeys.'

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The writer is the Prime Minister of India

On November 26, 1949, the Constituent Assembly adopted our Constitution. Today, we remember Dr Rajendra Prasad, Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar and every member of the Constituent Assembly. Their greatness lay in drawing extensively from the rich traditions and civilisational wisdom of Bharat while framing a modern Constitution.For a nation as diverse as Bharat, with its numerous faiths, languages, customs and schools of thought, it is important that the Constitution has a resonance far beyond the precincts of Parliament and the courts. Our endeavour has been to deepen its connect with the collective consciousness of our people, especially our youth and strengthen the spirit of unity essential to Indiaâs bright future. That is why over a decade ago, our government decided to mark November 26 as Constitution Day.For crores of Indians, including me, the Constitution of India is an inseparable part of our life journeys. Whenever I look back at my childhood, the humble circumstances in which I grew up, the struggles that were a part of everyday life, I am filled with an overwhelming sense of gratitude towards our Constitution. That a child born into a family of modest means, with no privileges or advantages of birth, could one day be entrusted with the responsibility of serving the worldâs largest democracy speaks volumes about how extraordinary our Constitution is.It is due to our Constitution that circumstances of oneâs birth no longer determine the limits of oneâs future.In our own humble way, we have sought to repay this debt of gratitude by strengthening our Constitution.The distinguished constitutional scholar, Granville Austin, described our Constitution as âfirst and foremost a social documentâ. The quest for social and economic justice runs through the very fabric of our Constitution. Thus, what can be more satisfying than working towards the realisation of this cherished vision of the makers of our Constitution?A recent World Bank report highlights that nearly 50 crore Indians have moved out of poverty. Breaking free from generations of deprivation, crores of parents can now dream of a better future for their children.When PM Awas Yojana ensures a family moves from a thatched roof to a pucca home, the constitutional promise of dignity acquires meaning.When Ujjwala Yojana frees a mother from the hardships of a smoke-filled kitchen, we advance the ideals of equality and well-being.When Ayushman Bharat enables a poor family to access quality healthcare without the fear of debt, social justice becomes a lived reality.When MUDRA and PM-SVANidhi provide collateral-free credit to small entrepreneurs and street vendors, economic justice finds expression.When digital technology and platforms like UPI transcend all divides and place opportunities once available to a privileged few within the reach of every citizen, we advance the constitutional ideal of inclusivity.There are many more manifestations of this constitutional vision.The list of amendments we brought can be viewed through the same prism. The 101st Amendment ushered in GST, a long-awaited reform. The 102nd Amendment granted constitutional status to National Commission for Backward Classes, fulfilling a long-standing dream of the marginalised sections of society.The 103rd Amendment received broad social acceptance. By providing reservation to Economically Weaker Sections, it addressed the long-overlooked aspirations of economically disadvantaged families from communities outside the existing reservation framework.For the first time since 1950, an updated version of our Constitution is now available in all 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule. This has brought our Constitution closer to the people.Even after our Constitution came into force in 1950, we continued to be governed by the colonial penal code dating back to the 1860s. With Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, we have sought to bring about a fundamental shift in our criminal justice system, moving from the colonial emphasis on punishment (Dand) to a citizen-centric pursuit of justice (Nyay).Over the past decade, we have laid special emphasis on Kartavya, or the duties of a citizen. Our civilisation has always emphasised the responsibilities that accompany every role in society. The spirit of Kartavya has found expression in several mass movements, from Swachh Bharat to water conservation and environmental protection.However, there is another reality that I feel compelled to share. There have been occasions in our history when those entrusted with upholding Constitution chose to weaken it. Ironically, they are the same people who had the opportunity to govern India for five decades.This year marks 75 years since the First Amendment of 1951, when a government that was not popularly elected used its majority in the Provisional Parliament to restrict fundamental freedoms. Its timing, barely months before Indiaâs first general election, proves that it was intended to influence the electoral process and stifle public opposition. It is also 50 years since the 42nd Amendment at the height of Emergency. This curtailed judicial review and fundamentally altered the balance of institutional powers. I would also urge youngsters to study the 38th and 39th Amendments to know what a power-hungry and anti-constitutional leadership can do.The repeated misuse of Article 356 to dismiss elected state governments presents another troubling chapter. One party has the dubious record of imposing Article 356 almost a hundred times and one former PM has scored a half-century in this field.The makers of our Constitution had hoped that it would be implemented in letter and spirit across India. But, for over 70 years, Articles 370 and 35A did not allow the full Constitution to be implemented in Jammu & Kashmir, thus trampling over the rights of SC, ST, OBC communities and women. It was only in 2019 that this historical wrong was corrected.For decades, in several parts of India, particularly in tribal areas, Naxalites used the might of the gun to deny the poorest people the rights guaranteed to them by our Constitution. The successful elimination of Naxalism this year is particularly heartwarming because it has ensured that the poorest of the poor can finally exercise their constitutional rights without fear. Now, we are left only with âDimagi Naxalsâ, far removed from the realities of our times but persistent in their efforts to derail our growth trajectory.It is most appalling that the biggest party in the opposition wants to reduce OBC reservation and bring Muslim reservations, something the makers of our Constitution, notably Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar, were totally against.The journey of our Constitution would be incomplete without recognising the remarkable women who helped shape it. But what happened earlier this year should fill our hearts with shame. A legislation aimed at giving women adequate representation in legislative bodies was disallowed from being passed by the one opposition party, once again showing its disdain for constitutional values. I assure the Nari Shakti of India that no force can prevent us from ensuring that justice is done to them.Our constitutional democracy has a clearly defined role for the opposition. Sadly, the leading opposition party seems to have become more of an Avrodh Paksh (obstructionist) than a Virodh Paksh (opposition). They should know that disrupting democratic processes is no substitute for discharging constitutional responsibilities.Today, India stands at a defining moment. As we work towards Viksit Bharat by 2047, two simple yet powerful principles can guide our collective endeavours: India First in our thinking and Kartavya (Duties) in our actions. With these as our guiding principles and Constitution as our source of strength, we can secure a bright future for generations to come.

World.title: Chemistry most popular subject after English for 12th CBSE students
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The gap between science and commerce subjects in CBSE schools has widened considerably in eight years, with candidate numbers in chemistry growing by 70 per cent, physics by nearly 58 per cent and mathematics by 55 per cent, against around 32 per cent each in business studies and accountancy.

As CBSE gears up for V Class 12 exams in 2027, with a record 19 lakh registrations, over half the candidates have individually opted for chemistry and physics. Chemistry has emerged as the most popular after English, with 10.8 lakh registrations, accounting for nearly 57 per cent of all candidates.

Gap between chemistry and business studies more than doubled

Physics follows with 10 lakh (52.6 per cent) and mathematics with 8.3 lakh (43.4 per cent). English tops the list with 18.5 lakh registrations, accounting for over 97 per cent of the examination cohort.



Economics, with 5.8 lakh registrations, has attracted nearly one in three candidates, followed by business studies (4.51 lakh) and accountancy (4.5 lakh), each accounting for nearly 24 per cent of the candidates.

In 2019, chemistry and physics had around 6.4 lakh candidates each, mathematics 5.3 lakh and economics 4.3 lakh, while business studies and accountancy had around 3.4 lakh each. While commerce subjects continue to attract more students, their numbers have not kept pace with the growth recorded in core science subjects.





The gap between chemistry and business studies has more than doubled â from 2.9 lakh candidates in 2019 to 6.3 lakh in 2027 â an analysis of CBSEâs examination statistics registration data accessed by TOI shows. The gap between physics and accountancy has similarly widened from 2.9 lakh to 5.5 lakh.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The figures also reflect the steady expansion of CBSEâs examination cohort. Class XII registrations have increased by nearly 31 per cent in five years, from 14.5 lakh in 2022 to 16.9 lakh in 2023, 17 lakh in 2024 and 17.8 lakh in 2025.

Registrations reached 18.6 lakh in 2026, with the provisional numbers for 2027 recording a further increase of 2.3 per cent.

The dominance of science subjects in CBSE schools comes amid their growing popularity nationally. An education ministry analysis of school board exam results showed science accounted for 47 per cent of Class XII passouts across the country in 2024, up from 44 per cent in 2023. For the first time in at least a decade, more girls cleared Class XII in science than in arts in 2024.

The board allows flexible subject combinations, and officials said the provisional registration numbers could change marginally.

World.title: 7th high court posting? Justice Rao may be Karnataka Chief Justice

NEW DELHI: Justice M S Ramachandra Rao has been recommended as Chief Justice of the Karnataka high court. This would mark his seventh high court since his appointment as a judge of Andhra Pradesh HC on June 12, 2012.The collegium also recommended the transfer of Karnataka HC CJ Vibhu Bhakru to the much smaller Jharkhand HC, and the appointment of Justice Vivek Singh Thakur, a judge of Himachal Pradesh HC, as Chief Justice of Tripura HC. This will be consequent to the transfer of Justice Rao from Tripura HC to Karnataka HC.Justice Rao, after the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, had opted for Telangana HC on Jan 1, 2019.Even when Justice M S Ramachandra Rao was a judge of Andhra Pradesh High Court, the collegium led by CJI T S Thakur had, in 2016 considered a proposal to transfer him out of his parent high court, but the move was stalled.A similar proposal was also stalled during the tenure of Justice Ranjan Gogoi as CJI.However, adverse reports about him forced the hand of the CJI N V Ramana-led collegium in 2021, and Justice Rao was transferred to Punjab and Haryana HC as a judge, where he served from Oct 12, 2021, to May 29, 2023. The collegium led by CJI D Y Chandrachud next appointed him Chief Justice of Himachal HC, where he served from May 30, 2023, till Sept 24, 2024.During his tenure there, the Supreme Court had quashed an HC collegium recommendation for appointment of judicial officers as HC judges on the grounds that he had proposed the names unilaterally without consulting his two most senior colleagues.The Justice Chandrachud-led collegium then transferred him from Himachal Pradesh High Court to Jharkhand HC as CJ, a position he held from Sept 24, 2024, to July 21, 2025.He was transferred by the CJI B R Gavai-led collegium to Tripura HC, where he has been serving as CJ since July 25 last year. If govt accepts the latest recommendation, Justice Rao will have served in seven HCs â and as CJ in four of them within a span of three and a half years.

World.title: Karnataka charts India’s first comprehensive care and rehabilitation policy for burns survivors
World.content:
The Karnataka Cabinet has approved a comprehensive policy for the prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration of burns survivors, paving the way for a Statewide network of specialised burns care facilities. Karnataka is the first State in the country to come out with such a policy.

The policy envisages setting up 15-bed burns care wards in district hospitals and government medical college hospitals, besides upgrading the Mahabodhi Burns Care Centre at Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute (BMCRI), Bengaluru, as a Centre of Excellence.

Ritvik Ranjanam Pandey, Principal Secretary (Health), said the focus would now shift to implementing the policy. “With the Cabinet approval in place, the next step is implementation. We will work towards putting the various components of the policy in place,” he told The Hindu.

Expanding access to specialised care

Karnataka records an estimated 2.5 lakh to 3 lakh burns cases annually, according to the Cabinet note. However, specialised treatment, including intensive care and rehabilitation, remains concentrated in Bengaluru and Mysuru. The proposed district-level facilities are expected to address this gap.

Each 15-bed unit will comprise 10 general beds, three high-dependency unit beds and two intensive care unit beds. The wards will also have operation theatres for burns procedures, isolation facilities and physiotherapy services.

Mr. Pandey said the policy adopts a comprehensive approach covering emergency response, transportation, stabilisation, treatment, referral services and long-term rehabilitation. It also provides for standardised protocols for wound management, intensive care and surgical interventions. Physiotherapy and rehabilitation are to begin from the first day of treatment, wherever clinically appropriate.

BMCRI to be Centre of Excellence

The Mahabodhi Burns Care Centre at BMCRI will function as the State’s apex institution, providing specialised treatment, training, research and technical support to district-level facilities.

The proposed upgrade includes improvements to operation theatre and intensive care facilities, besides strengthening physiotherapy and rehabilitation services. Dedicated facilities for hydrotherapy, prosthetics, radiology and laser treatment are also envisaged.

The centre will undertake capacity-building programmes, develop treatment protocols, support telemedicine services and establish a State Burns Registry.

A hub-and-spoke model will link the Centre of Excellence with district-level units through standardised guidelines and referral protocols connecting primary, taluk, district and tertiary healthcare facilities.

Rehabilitation and social reintegration

Beyond emergency medical care, the policy emphasises the psychological and social consequences of burns. It envisages counselling, reconstructive surgery, social security and support for survivors to return to their families, education, employment and community life. The policy also provides for livelihood support and vocational rehabilitation to help survivors rebuild their lives.

The estimated one-time expenditure for establishing the 15-bed burns care wards is ₹100.95 crore, while ₹4.5 crore has been earmarked for upgrading the Centre of Excellence. The latter will involve a recurring expenditure of ₹1.2 crore annually.

Recognise disfigurement

Welcoming the policy, women’s rights activist and Aweksha co-founder Donna Fernandes, however, said it would have been more inclusive had it explicitly recognised disfigurement as a disability, making survivors eligible for disability benefits and compensation.

“We are disappointed that the policy has not included disfigurement as a disability,” she said, pointing out that survivors with severe facial injuries face social ostracism, humiliation and psychological trauma that cannot be captured through conventional assessments of functional disability. “Disfigurement is a disability. You cannot measure it, you cannot quantify it, and you cannot assign a percentage to it,” she said.

Harrassment and violence

Besides, the policy should also recognise that burns involving women are not necessarily accidental, but can result from domestic violence, dowry harassment and deliberate attacks by husbands or in-laws. Treating such cases merely as cooking or stove accidents overlooks the circumstances behind the injuries.

Ms. Fernandes further called for burns survivors to receive compensation and healthcare benefits on a par with acid attack survivors, as both groups suffer extensive skin and tissue damage, disfigurement and long-term consequences.

Recognising disfigurement as a disability and extending equivalent benefits to burn survivors would have strengthened the policy, she added.

World.title: Supreme Court issues notice on bail pleas by Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam in 2020 Delhi riots case
World.content:
The Supreme Court issued notice on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) on the bail pleas of former JNU scholar Umar Khalid and activist Sharjeel Imam, accused in the larger conspiracy case linked to the 2020 Delhi riots. The court, however, declined to take up their pleas for interim relief, saying a three-judge Bench would be set up to decide whether prolonged incarceration and delay in trial can override stringent bail curbs imposed by the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), 1967.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana sought the Delhi Police’s response to the bail pleas by December 14. It also directed the Registry to place the matter before the CJI on the administrative side for the constitution of a larger Bench in light of the court’s May 22 judgment in Tasleem Ahmed v. State Government of NCT of Delhi.

“Issue notice, returnable on 14.12.2026. The Registry is directed to put up the matter before Hon’ble the Chief Justice of India, on the administrative side, for constitution of a three-Judge Bench in light of the judgment dated 22.05.2026,” the Bench said.

The May 22 reference arose from divergent interpretations by coordinate Benches of the law governing bail under the UAPA. In its January 5 verdict, a Division Bench comprising Justices Aravind Kumar and P.B. Varale had granted bail to five other accused in the case but denied relief to Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam on the ground that the roles attributed to them stood on a “qualitatively different footing”. The court permitted them to renew their bail pleas after a year or upon completion of the examination of protected witnesses, whichever was earlier.

Subsequently, on May 18, a Bench comprising Justices B. V. Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan, while granting bail to an accused in a narco-terrorism case, expressed reservations about the January 5 judgment, observing that it had failed to correctly apply the binding principles laid down in the court’s 2021 ruling in Union of India v. K. A. Najeeb. In Najeeb, the court had held that the stringent bail embargo under Section 43D(5) of the UAPA could “melt down” where prolonged incarceration and delay in trial infringed an accused’s fundamental rights.

Following this, Justices Kumar and Varale referred the matter to the CJI on May 22 for the constitution of a larger Bench to ensure “parity and consistency” in the application of binding precedents by coordinate Benches. The Bench, however, granted six months’ interim bail to Tasleem Ahmed and Abdul Khalid Saifi, two other accused in the conspiracy case, observing that they “cannot be made to suffer” merely because a question of law awaited authoritative settlement.

Also read | The continued custody in Delhi Riots cases is an injustice

‘Conflicting interpretations’

At the outset of Wednesday’s hearing, senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Siddhartha Dave, appearing for Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam, respectively, urged the court to consider their pleas for interim bail, pointing out that both had been in custody for over six years. Mr. Dave argued that the prayer for interim relief was distinct from the larger question of law referred to the CJI on May 22.

“Only the main matter on the legal issue is under reference. Let the issue of interim come up for hearing,” Mr. Sibal submitted, seeking an early hearing.

The CJI, however, said he would have to first examine the conflicting interpretations of the Najeeb ruling, which he had authored.

“…in the light of the conflict of observation, I have to apply my mind. It was my judgment (Najeeb case) which is being discussed. So, I am feeling a little embarrassed. One bench says Najeeb means this; another bench says it does not mean… I am being told what I have said,” the CJI remarked.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the Delhi Police, pointed out that the May 22 reference had arisen from bail proceedings involving other accused in the same conspiracy case.

‘Unjustified delay’

The two activists have challenged a September 30 ruling of the Delhi High Court rejecting their fresh bail pleas, contending that the case remains at the stage of framing of charges and that the trial is yet to commence.

A Division Bench of the High Court had held that judicial discipline prevented it from modifying the conditions imposed by the Supreme Court in its January 5 judgment.

“These two conditions would show that the specific liberty is clear and conditional, and this Court would not be in a position to modify the condition,” a Bench comprising Justices Prathiba M. Singh and Dinesh Bhatt had said.

In his petition filed through advocate Fauzia Shakil, Mr. Imam pointed out that despite his incarceration for over six years, not one of the more than 900 prosecution witnesses named in the case had been examined. Of these, 47 are protected witnesses.

Given the pace of proceedings, he contended, “On no fair assessment can examination of protected witnesses be expected to commence, much less to conclude, before January 5, 2027, or for a considerable period thereafter.”

Mr. Imam further argued that his continued detention had ceased to serve a procedural purpose and had become “punitive by reason of unreasonable and unjustified delay”.

Of the 18 accused in the conspiracy case, five, including Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam, remain in custody. Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmed were granted bail on January 5.

The Delhi Police have booked the accused under the UAPA and various provisions of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), alleging that they conspired to orchestrate the communal violence that broke out in northeast Delhi on February 23, 2020, amid protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act. The riots left 53 people dead and hundreds injured.

Mr. Imam was initially arrested on January 28, 2020, before the riots, while Mr. Khalid was taken into custody in September that year.

World.title: Country could face a ‘blood revolution’ unless the Constitution is saved: Prakash Ambedkar
World.content:
Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi (VBA) chief Prakash Ambedkar on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) warned that the country could face a “blood revolution” unless the Constitution is saved and people are allowed to choose their own representatives.

Speaking at the Samvidhan Samman Sabha, held ahead of Constitution Day, Mr. Ambedkar said it is “unfortunate” that the ideals of the Constitution were under threat as Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and the BJP is doing everything to be in power.

Constitution Day LIVE updates

“They have this mindset of paying Pakistan and get bomb thrown at the country,” said Mr. Ambedkar, alleging that BJP and RSS were returning to communal politics to win elections, with an agenda built on being “anti-Muslim and anti-Pakistan.”

Referring to the Pulwama attack, he asked whether any country had stood behind India, and said European nations had backed Iran. He also asked why Nepal’s Prime Minister had visited India and what happened in Sri Lanka meeting, urging people to “understand the game plan.”

North-South balance

Mr. Ambedkar said India’s unity rested on a balance between North and South. He cautioned that RSS and BJP want to create the divide by increasing the dominance of North. Hinting on delimitation bill, he said, “A mechanism built over 70 years ensured there was a balance between northern and southern dominance. BJP and RSS are trying to break this arrangement out of greed. The day the South feels its dominance in Delhi is weakening, it won’t stay.”

After Independence, he said, the country chose nation over religion. The BJP, he alleged, had instigated a North-South divide to break India into pieces, put religion at the centre once more, and run the country through corporates such as Adani and Ambani.

Opposition criticised

He also criticised Shiv Sena (UBT) Chief Uddhav Thackeray and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for not asking questions on these issues. He also advised Shiv Sena chief Eknath Shinde to be alert as Mr. Thackeray wants to be in power.

He called NCP-SP supremo Sharad Pawar’s friend of Dawood Ibrahim, saying “I know everything about these leaders and RSS has documented the history.”

Rafale, national security

Questioning the government on defence, Mr. Ambedkar said India was reported to have taken delivery of 36 Rafale jets, but the count on the ground was 32. He demanded to know how many the country actually has, and, if a jet had been shot down in conflict, where the pilot was: “with them or in the country.”

He further claimed that the Prime Minister’s “56-inch” image had suddenly shrunk and that he had “taken refuge at America’s feet.”

Drought warning

Mr. Ambedkar also spoke on the drought, warning that after December, rural Maharashtra would begin migrating to Pune, Mumbai and other metros.

World.title: Keralam Minister announces ‘Speak up to stand up’ for woman survivors of violence
World.content:
Keralam Minister for Women and Child Development Bindhu Krishna on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) announced ‘Speak up to stand up,’ a scheme for ensuring comprehensive support and financial empowerment of woman survivors of violence to lead them towards independence.

Inaugurating the State-level observance of International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women at Government College for Women, Vazhuthacaud, Thiruvananthapuram, the Minister said the objective of the scheme was to create a Keralam where each girl and woman could walk without fear, study, work, and choose the life she wanted.

The initiative was a continuation of Kerala Police’s ‘Speak up’ scheme that aimed at rehabilitation and financial empowerment of woman survivors. Intended to help woman survivors rebuild their lives with confidence, ‘Speak up to stand up’ would be implemented with the support of the Women and Child Development (WCD) department, Kerala Women’s Commission, and Kerala State Women’s Development Corporation (KSWDC) Ltd.

Rehabilitation plans

The needs, interests, and skills of each survivor of violence will be analysed and individual rehabilitation plans prepared with their consent. They will be provided with safe accommodation, counselling, social and emotional support, free legal aid, opportunities for continuing their education, employment, and skill training.

Self-employment schemes of the KSWDC and Kudumbashree network mechanisms would also be tapped into to help women start own ventures and earn an income.

The emergency protection for the survivors and further services will be provided through the WCD’s women protection officers, 181 Mitra help line, and Sakhi one-stop centres.

The Minister took the occasion to remind the attendees that dowry was not a symbol of status or pride, but an illegal practice. Defamation through social media, misuse of private pictures and information, and cyber threats should also be taken seriously. “The youth should be ready to react to violence and question wrong practices,” Ms. Krishna said.

An art wall with the message of ‘Not silence, but reply,’ mime, and flash mob by students kicked off the day’s events. An interaction between the Minister and the students was also held.

Kerala Women’s Commission chairperson P. Satheedevi presided over the programme.

World.title: India Pavilion bags Visitors’ Lion at Venice Biennale; PM Modi calls it ‘proud moment for country’
World.content:
The India Pavilion has won the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at the prestigious Venice Art Biennale, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailing the award as a “proud moment” for India’s art and cultural world.

The pavilion, under the theme ‘Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home’, explored memory and belonging in a rapidly transforming world.

Earlier in the day, Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat described it on X as a “remarkable recognition” of the country’s growing cultural influence.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailed the award as a “proud moment” for India’s art and cultural world.

“Delighted that the India Pavilion at the Venice Art Biennale has won the prestigious Visitors’ Lion for Best National Pavilion. Our artists are bringing fresh perspectives to the world of art, drawing inspiration from India’s rich and diverse cultural heritage. May this feat inspire many more young Indians to pursue art and explore new creative horizons,” he posted on X, while sharing Mr. Shekhawat’s post.

The biennale ran from May 9 to November 22, with previews from May 6-8.

The India Pavilion returned to the Biennale Arte — one of the components of La Biennale di Venezia — after a gap of seven years.

The pavilion was opened at the 61st International Art Exhibition at the Biennale, in Venice, in the presence of Shekhawat and other officials.

“A moment of immense pride! India wins the Best National Pavilion – Visitors’ Lion at the Venice Art Biennale, the Olympics of the art world. The honour, decided through votes by visitors from across the globe, is a remarkable recognition of India’s growing cultural influence,” Mr. Shekhawat said.

La Biennale di Venezia announces the winners of the Visitors’ Lions of the Biennale Arte 2026, awarded based on the “preferences expressed by the public through votes cast by visitors” to the 61st International Art Exhibition In Minor Keys, by Koyo Kouoh, its website reads.

U.S.-based artist Nick Cave won the Visitors’ Lion for Best Participant in the 61st Exhibition In Minor Keys by Koyo Kouoh, while the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation was won by India, which presented its pavilion at the historic Arsenale, it says.

Visitors eligible to vote were ticket holders who visited during the opening period of the 61st Exhibition, from May 9 to November 22, at both exhibition venues, the Giardini and the Arsenale.

“The Visitors’ Lions give a voice to the public’s choices and recognise the participants and national participations that have received the greatest appreciation from visitors during the 61st International Art Exhibition,” it said.

“The public of the exhibition embraced this recognition - the Visitors’ Award - as an opportunity to bring Pablo Picasso’s practice to life: a painting only comes to life through the person who looks at it. I can say without hesitation that La Biennale is brimming with ever-renewed energy thanks to the vibrant presence of everyone, president of La Biennale di Venezia, Pietrangelo Buttafuoco, was quoted as saying on the website.

The pavilion of India was curated by Amin Jaffer and presented by the Ministry of Culture in partnership with Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC) and Serendipity Arts, the Ministry said earlier.

Mr. Shekhawat on X said that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India’s cultural and artistic heritage is receiving “renewed global recognition, while contemporary Indian creativity is finding its rightful place on the world stage.

“Presented by the @MinOfCultureGoI in collaboration with NMACC and Serendipity Arts, India’s national pavilion, ‘Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home’, showcased five remarkable artists: Alwar Balasubramaniam, Ranjani Shettar, Sumakshi Singh, Skarma Sonam Tashi and Asim Waqif,” he said.

This global recognition is a testament to the talent of new-age Indian artists and the vibrancy of our contemporary art scene, the minister added.
